title: 겹에 넘긴 글이 집기로 끝나도 if ! 가 그것을 못 본다
칸이 열 개 넘으면 done 을 숨길 길이 없다

text:
리뷰 원문 (xhigh, `--fix`, agent-ae7506a61daea8502). 15건.

1. `src/tz.rs:164` — system_name() only strips an absolute /usr/share/zoneinfo prefix, so the
   relative /etc/localtime symlink that systemd's `timedatectl set-timezone` writes never yields a
   name. On Fedora/Arch, /etc/localtime -> ../usr/share/zoneinfo/Asia/Seoul; read_link returns that
   relative path, strip_prefix fails, system_name returns None -> Trouble::NoSystemZone. Every moai
   command (including every `moai hook` run) prints `moai: the system does not name its timezone`
   on stderr and every screen stays in UTC — exactly the bug the epic set out to fix. Same on
   macOS, where /usr/share/zoneinfo is itself a symlink to /var/db/timezone/zoneinfo.
2. `src/tui/mod.rs:2121` — adopt_look pushes the system-zone trouble into `problems` before the
   configured `[tui] timezone` overrides it, so the banner claims UTC while the screen shows the
   chosen zone.
3. `src/tui/draw.rs:917` — split_body folds the detail pane away on a short terminal but leaves
   app.detail_open true, so keys::Ctx.detail stays true and focus can land on a pane that is never
   drawn. Ctrl-w w sets focus = Pane::Detail and App::step routes Up/Down to self.detail.go(m) —
   an invisible scroll. The list cursor stops responding with no visible cause.
4. `src/tui/keys.rs:731` — Focus(Side) stays enabled whenever the detail pane is open, but
   Pane::step is a no-op when the pane is above or below, so the key bar advertises a key that does
   nothing.
5. `src/tz.rs:156` — the TZ filter accepts path forms and rejects an empty TZ, contradicting its own
   comment. `TZ=:/etc/localtime` passes the alnum check, is refused by safe_join and becomes
   Trouble::Unknown — one warning line on every command. `TZ=""` means UTC under POSIX but is
   skipped, so moai silently uses /etc/localtime while every other tool uses UTC.
6. `src/tui/zones.rs:61` — Zones::step re-implements scroll::cursor and pages by the drawn height,
   breaking the documented rule that every pane takes the same fixed page step (PAGE = 10).
   Move::Top/Bottom/HalfUp/HalfDown arms are also unreachable from pick_zone.
7. `src/tui/zones.rs:44` — Zones::shown() re-filters and re-lowercases the whole name list on every
   call, and it is called several times per keystroke and once per frame (~1,900 names here).
8. `src/view.rs:318` — the new Asked struct was inserted between `pub fn list`'s doc comment and the
   function, so list() lost its doc and Asked's doc opens with a paragraph about the removed
   `asked_deferred` parameter.
9. `src/tui/zones.rs:153` — set_zone clears App::notice unconditionally on a successful zone load,
   discarding any unrelated banner the session was showing.
10. `src/tz.rs:187` — walk() recurses on at.is_dir(), which follows symlinks, with no depth bound.
    A directory symlink to one of its own ancestors overflows the stack, taking the whole TUI down.
11. `tests/cli.rs:5985` — the_screen_follows_the_timezone_but_the_file_and_json_stay_utc hard-requires
    a system tzdb, while its sibling unit test guards the same assertions with `if let Ok(seoul)`.
    On the machines this epic documents as supported (static musl, no tzdb) the suite cannot tell
    "behaviour changed" from "this box has no tzdb".
12. `src/tui/keys.rs:546` — dropping SPC v d leaves no key at all for a done column past the ninth,
    because Column(n) is bound only for n in 0..9. The column can be revealed with SPC v a but never
    hidden again from the explorer.
13. `src/tui/draw.rs:922` — split_body computes (share, least) before the early vertical-fold return,
    and the horizontal minimum is a bare literal 10 while its vertical twin is the named
    DETAIL_MIN_V.
14. `src/tui/draw.rs:2009` — row_marks is recomputed up to three times for the same row in one frame
    (row_glyph, head_width, row_line's `cols.still` branch), each doing an Index::deferred_root
    lookup.
15. `src/tui/zones.rs:1` — the module doc declares `조각이다. App 도 터미널도 모른다` while the same
    file carries an `impl App` that reads the tzdb and writes the user config, and registers itself
    in input.rs's NOT_COMPONENTS.

고친 것 (리뷰가 직접): 1·2·3·4·5(일부)·6·7·8·10·11·13·15.
넘긴 것: 9(notice 정책은 UX 결정) · 12(`SPC v d` 를 걷은 것은 사용자 결정) ·
14(머리 폭 불변식을 건드릴 값이 없다).

`cargo test` 1258 + 481 통과, `cargo clippy --all-targets` 깨끗, `cargo fmt --check` 깨끗.

note: `SPC v d` 를 걷고 done 은 칸 번호로만 켜고 끈다. 번호는 설정의 칸 이름을 그대로 댄다.
안내와 주석이 대던 옛 키 이름 셋을 새 키로 — `SPC t w`·`SPC r`·`SPC m r`.
미룬 줄에 `‖` 를 세웠다. 낱말은 그대로 두고 칸 글리프 곁에 붙는다.
idea 줄에 `◇` 를 세웠다. 물어서 받은 idea 목록에는 안 단다.
두 글리프의 코드포인트와 폭을 글자로 못박았다 — 모양이 비슷한 이모지 글자로 바꾸면 그 시험에서 멈춘다.
상세 칸이 `right`·`bottom`·`left`·`top` 넷에 선다. 자리를 맞바꿀 때 몫도 따라가 목록이 늘 큰 쪽이다.
`SPC o d` 가 자리를 돌리고 메뉴는 안 닫힌다. 켜고 끄는 것은 `SPC v p` 에 그대로 남았다.
세로일 때의 몫을 따로 뒀고(70%), 낮은 창에서는 아예 안 연다 — 눌린 목록은 커서 줄조차 못 낸다.
화면의 시각이 보는 사람의 시간대로 선다. 저장과 `--json` 은 UTC 그대로다.
`SPC o t` 가 고르는 창을 연다. 시간대 자료는 크레이트 없이 시스템 zoneinfo 를 직접 읽는다(사용자 결정).
못 푸는 이름은 UTC 로 떨어지고 한 줄로 알린다. 종료 코드는 그대로고, 고른 이름은 설정에 남는다.

text: 사용자 결정(2026-09-21): 다섯 벌을 `store::real(p) -> PathBuf` 한 자로 모은다. `store.rs` 가 이미 `gone`·`dir_of`·`lock_beside`·`stamp` 를 들고 있어 파일 시스템 잣대의 집이다. `read_marks::settle` 은 까닭을 대야 해서 그대로 둔다. 물음이 달라서다. 대신 글로 `real` 을 가리킨다. `cmd::skill::same_dir` 은 `user_config::same_dir` 로 접는다. `scratch` 한 자리는 못 모았다 — `tests/cli.rs` 가 그 파일을 `#[path]` 로 함께 들어 거기서는 `crate::store` 가 없다. 갈리지 않게 글로 맸다.

조상 훑기를 `store::climb` 하나로 들었다. `planted_elsewhere` 는 이제 `root.parent()` 에서 `climb` 을 부른다 — 제 자리는 안 묻는 것이 전과 같다. `main != root` 를 `user_config::same_dir` 로 견주는 것은 안 했다. 그 줄 자체가 사라졌다. 워크트리인지는 이제 `worktree::main_root` 하나가 답하고, 경로를 견주는 자리는 판정에서 빠졌다.

사용자 결정(2026-09-21): 딸린 워크트리 안이면 밑자리도 `Elsewhere::Worktree` 다. 가르는 자는 `worktree::main_root` 하나다. 대는 자리는 비친 자리(`<main>/<밑길>`, 없는 디렉터리일 수 있다)가 아니라 실제로 읽히는 트래커다 — 이 자리의 짝, 조상 트래커의 짝, 찾은 조상 순으로 고른다. 셋 다 비면 `None` 이라 그 자리에 세운다: 주 체크아웃에 트래커가 없는 워크트리는 거기가 트래커를 처음 들이는 자리다(moai-71ht.jlh 가 세운 갈래). moai-a2kn 의 천장과 moai-mz0e 의 경계는 안 건드렸다.

사용자 결정(2026-09-21): 알리는 표면은 `MOAI_HERE` 를 안 물려받는다. `init_belongs_at` 이 답하는 것은 나중의 다른 부름이 어디서 서느냐라, 그 부름의 셸이 손잡이를 켤지는 여기서 알 수 없다. 지금 이 프로세스의 거절(`planted_elsewhere`)은 그대로 꺼진 채 둔다. 표면 다섯이 `init_belongs_at` 하나를 보므로 `view.rs` 는 안 건드리고 닫혔다. 그 파일은 지금 옆 세션이 쥐고 있다.

사용자 결정(2026-09-21): 옛 철자 파일과 지금 자리는 늦은 도장이 이긴다. 옛 `[read]` 는 값의 뜻이 달라(본 때 vs 줄의 `updated_at`, moai-lyc1) 지금대로 자리로 가른다. 대기 자리도 그대로다. 가르는 잣대는 그 파일에 지금도 적히는가 하나다. 읽는 길(`overlay_later`)과 쓰는 길(`Wins::Later`)을 함께 옮겼고, 재 보기도 락 안과 같은 차례로 두 번에 나눠 합친다. 사람이 적어 둔 줄은 그대로 막힌 채다 — `Sheet::outdated_by` 는 때가 선 자리에만 참이다.

title: runuser -u <사용자> -- <명령> 을 아직 안 본다

text:
잰 결과 — 겹 상한을 낮출 까닭은 안 섰다. 곱으로 오르는 문은 하나뿐이고, 그 자리는 이미 `Lexer::WORK` 가 물고 있다.

표 A. 문마다 예순 겹, dev 빌드, `Lexer::WORK` 에서 치른 글자 수.

| 문 | 바이트 | 읽은 글자 | dev |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$( … )` | 610 | 18,300 | 7ms |
| `env -S '…'` | 550 | 14,730 | 12ms |
| `sudo -s …` | 490 | 14,760 | 15ms |
| `eval '…'` | 430 | 9,450 | 6ms |
| `bash -c "$( … )"` | 790 | 2,097,140 (예산을 다 씀) | 7.6초 |

- `env -S` 와 `sudo -s` 가 연 문은 값이 치환과 같은 자리다. moai-rang 이 걱정하던 것이 여기서 닫힌다
- `su -c`·`runuser -c`(moai-qqg2·moai-dkph 가 연 문) 도 같은 자리다

표 B. 곱으로 오르는 한 꼴 — 치환과 셸을 **함께** 쌓았다.

| 겹 | 바이트 | dev | 릴리스 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | 127 | 69ms | 20ms |
| 15 | 205 | 5.2초 | 1.3초 |
| 30 | 400 | 8.2초 | 2.3초 |
| 40 | 530 | 11.5초 | 3.1초 |
| 64 | 842 | 4.4초 | 1.1초 |

- 열다섯 겹 205바이트부터 2MiB 예산을 통째로 쓴다. 그 값이 곧 상한이라 겹을 더 쌓아도 안 늘어난다
- 릴리스는 develop 의 바이너리로 훅을 직접 불러 쟀다. 훅의 15초 제한 안이다
- 깊이를 낮춰도 이 꼴은 못 막는다 — 열다섯 겹이면 이미 예산을 다 쓴다. 막는 자는 양(`WORK`)이지 깊이(`DEEP`)가 아니다

시험으로 남긴 것: `every_door_that_hands_a_string_costs_what_a_substitution_costs` 가 문 여섯을 예순 겹씩 세워 치른 글자 수가 64KiB 안인지 본다. 새 문이 값을 곱으로 올리면 거기서 붉어진다. 표 B 의 꼴은 시험에 안 넣었다 — dev 에서 8초짜리 시험은 지워진다. 그 자리는 `a_string_handed_to_a_shell_is_read_as_commands` 가 아홉 겹으로 지킨다.

다시 열 때: 릴리스에서 1초를 넘는다는 말이 나오거나, 예산 상한을 건드릴 까닭이 설 때.

못 견주는 값은 양쪽 다 자리로 진다(`later`). 사람이 `"어제 읽음"` 처럼 낱말로 적어 둔 줄은 RFC3339 가 모두 `2` 로 시작해 글자 차례로 늘 뒤에 서는데, 그것이 지금 자리 파일에 앉으면 `updated_at > seen` 이 영영 거짓이라 그 줄은 다시는 [NEW] 로 안 선다. 자리로 가르던 때는 `taken` 이 막던 자리라, 문을 여는 이 판이 함께 닫았다. 재는 자는 `model::parse_rfc3339` 로 이 도구가 때를 읽는 자 그대로다 — 무엇이 읽음인가는 안 좁혔고, 좁아진 것은 견주는 자리 하나다.

되돌렸다 — 2026-09-21 사용자 결정. 표식을 걷는 일은 에픽 moai-hela 의 멤버다.

- 무엇이 어긋났나: 표식이 붙은 줄마다 줄머리가 한 칸 길어져 트리 선이 어긋났다. 표식 없는 줄은 두 칸(` ·`), idea 는 세 칸(` ·◇`), 미룬 idea 는 네 칸이다
- 사용자가 본 것: `moai-7cpd   ·◇‖ └─ …` — 미룬 idea 에서 셋이 겹쳤다
- 사용자 말: "이모티콘이 겹치면서 엉망이다. 당장 해결하기 어려워 보이니 글리프를 추가했던 것은 없던 일로 하자"
- 미룸만 칸 글리프 왼쪽(스피너 자리)으로 옮기는 안을 먼저 보냈다가 물렸다 — `◇` 가 남아 같은 어긋남이 그대로 선다
- **다시 세우려면 줄머리 폭을 먼저 푼다.** 표식이 붙어도 줄머리가 두 칸으로 서는 길을 찾기 전에는 같은 자리로 돌아온다
- 원래 요구(미룬 줄을 목록에서 한눈에 가른다)는 아직 안 풀렸다. 그래서 done 이 아니라 todo 다 — 꼬리의 흐린 낱말(`view.rs:387`, `status.put_off`)이 지금 그 일을 혼자 한다

이 에픽이 낸 글리프 둘을 걷었다 — 2026-09-21 사용자 결정. moai-pkvw 와 moai-h06a 를 todo 로 돌렸다.

Review complete. (No `ReportFindings` tool is exposed in this environment, so the findings are stated here.)

**Scope reviewed:** `git diff develop...HEAD` — commit `fb6b3a3` "fix(init): 갈린 셸에 --check 가 둘째 줄을 낸다 (moai-ha0f)" — `i18n/en.json`, `i18n/ko.json`, `src/cmd/init.rs` (+58/-5). Working tree was clean at start.

## Findings (2)

- `src/cmd/init.rs:1159` — **medium**: the new test was inserted between an existing doc comment and the test it documented. The block explaining `.gitattributes` declaration vs `check-attr` (`moai-9khu`, reviews `moai-vbmn.spv`) belonged to `the_declared_path_is_the_one_init_writes`; after the diff it reads as documentation for `a_split_shell_gets_a_second_line`, and `the_declared_path_is_the_one_init_writes` has none. Concrete effect: the next person editing the `.gitattributes` filter no longer finds the "패턴이면 이 거르개에 안 걸린다" caveat on the test that enforces it, and the MOAI_HERE test carries three paragraphs about a subject it does not test. In this repo those rationale blocks are the stated record of irreversible decisions (`CLAUDE.md`, "어디서 왔나"), so a mis-attached one is a real loss, not a style nit. **Fixed.**

- `src/cmd/init.rs:400` — **medium**: the new hatch line also fires in a worktree *subdirectory* whose worktree top already carries a tracker the same shell reads, and following it splits the tracker. `init_belongs_at` reports `Some(main)` for `<wt>/src/deep` even when `<wt>/.moai` exists (`store::elsewhere` prefers the `main_root` mirror over the `Above` branch), so `check_worktree` emits `MOAI_HERE=1 moai init`. Verified end-to-end: from `<wt>/src/deep` with `MOAI_HERE=1`, `moai add` wrote to `<wt>/.moai`; after running the suggested line, `moai init` planted `.moai` in `src/deep`, the next `add` went there, and `moai show --json` returned only the new row — the earlier issue looks like it vanished, and the stray `.moai` is a file nobody reads that conflicts on merge (exactly what `moai-pk4x` exists to prevent). **Not fixed** — suppressing the line when a tracker is already reachable would delete it in precisely the layout `tests/cli.rs::saying_where_init_goes_does_not_inherit_moai_here` sets up (`<wt>/.moai` committed, cwd `<wt>/src/deep`), i.e. it would reverse the moai-ha0f user decision rather than repair it. This wants an issue/idea and the owner's call; the honest variants are to point the line at the tracker the handle shell already reads, or to emit it only where planting would not shadow one.

## Checked and cleared
- i18n: only `en`/`ko` are populated (`zh`/`ja`/`es` are 9–10-key stubs), so en+ko is the right pair despite the issue body saying "다섯 말"; `korean_carries_every_key_english_does`, `english_has_every_key_the_source_asks_for` and the placeholder test all pass. Both keys are passed as literals, so `i18n::tests::keys_in` sees them.
- `away_root(&root, ctx.chdir)` is correct here — `root` is `current_dir()` after `-C` is applied, so the second line gets `-C` exactly when the first three lines do, and `cli_hint` remains the single place that decides.
- `--json` still returns `tracker_at` unchanged under `MOAI_HERE`; that is the deliberate `moai-ko4y` behaviour with its own CLI test, not an oversight.
- `moai init` really does plant and exit 0 under the handle (`planted_elsewhere` short-circuits), so the new line's claim is truthful.

title: 리뷰가 도는 워크트리에서 가지를 고치면 --fix 가 고친 것이 날아간다

text:
리뷰 원문 (`/code-review max --fix`, 10각 + Phase 3 훑기, 토큰 445,377, 4,848초).

열다섯 건. 앞의 여덟이 고쳐졌고, 아홉째(`nth`)와 열째(`kept`)·열한째(`Handed` 그늘)도 같은 커밋에 들었다. 나머지 넷은 안 고치고 짚기만, 열다섯째는 나에게 넘겼다.

1. `src/hook.rs:1419` — `Lexer::subs_of` 가 `Lexer::at(text, 0)` 으로 지어, heredoc 되풀이(`subs_of → subst → heredoc → skip_heredocs → subs_of`)를 `Lexer::DEEP` 이 못 셌다. 스택을 넘겼다.
   재현: `cat <<TOP` + 8,000겹 `$(cat <<Tk … Tk)`(174KB 한 줄)가 커밋된 바이너리를 114초 뒤 `fatal runtime error: stack overflow` 로 죽였다. 4,000겹(86KB)은 31초. 죽거나 제 시간을 넘긴 훅은 규칙 넷을 통째로 연다. 고친 뒤 0.44초.
2. `src/hook.rs:1440` — `subs_of` 가 `lex.inner` 만 내고 `lex.later` 를 버려, heredoc 본문 안 치환이 연 heredoc 의 치환을 통째로 잃었다. 바깥 글이 `<<` 종료어에서 잘렸다.
   재현: `cat <<TOP\n$(x <<E1\n$(sed -i s/a/b/ src/y.rs)\nE1\n)\nTOP` 이 정말 src/y.rs 를 고치는데 커밋된 바이너리가 빈손으로 넘겼다(develop 은 막았다). 규칙 1 의 `moai add` 도 같은 구멍. **이 diff 가 새로 열었다** — 걷어 낸 글자 자는 본문을 한 덩이로 그대로 냈다.
3. `src/hook.rs:4208` — `if !` 의 끝내는 묶음 탐지가 문턱 둘을 한꺼번에 놓았다(`came.is_some_and(|d| d > seg.level)` → `came.is_some()`). 관계없는 집기 둘이 `came` 과 `cond` 를 나눠 채운다.
   재현: `moai mv A in_progress && if ! bash -c 'echo x; moai mv B in_progress; echo y'; then exit 1; fi; sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs` — 조건은 늘 이기는 `echo y` 라 `fi` 가 아무것도 안 뜻하는데, 없는 묶음이 열려 `;` 뒤의 빈손 쓰기가 샜다. develop 은 막고 커밋된 HEAD 는 넘겼다.
4. `src/hook.rs:1419` — 같은 `Lexer::at(text, 0)` 이 thread-local `LEFT` 를 heredoc 본문마다 2MiB 로 다시 채워, `Lexer::WORK` 가 일의 양을 못 묶었다.
   잰 것(A/B, 같은 바이트 수, dev): 겹친 `bash -c "$(…)"` 덩이 여섯을 `cat <<'E'` 로 가르면 11.6초, 따옴표 없는 `cat <<E` 로 가르면 28.2초. 일이 (1 + 따옴표 없는 heredoc 수) × WORK 가 되고, 그 수는 입력 길이 말고 아무것도 안 막는다.
5. `src/hook.rs:2251` — 새 `su`/`runuser` 줄이 첫 피연산자에서 옵션 읽기를 끊어, **스크립트가 실제로 쓰는 철자** `su <사용자> -c '<글>'` 이 `Wrapped::Stops` 를 내고 그 글을 아무도 안 읽었다.
   재현: `su alice -c 'sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs'`·`runuser alice -c '…'` 가 빈손으로 지나갔고, `su alice -c 'moai add x'` 가 규칙 1 을 지나갔다. util-linux 의 su·runuser 는 getopt 를 앞의 `+` 없이 불러 GNU 가 자리를 바꾼다 — 사용자 뒤의 `-c` 는 정말 옵션이다. moai-qqg2 가 닫으려던 구멍이 가장 흔한 철자에서 그대로 열려 있었다.
6. `src/hook.rs:2409` — `Runs::With` 가 "사용자 스위치를 봤는가" 를 이미 지나온 낱말(`rest[..n]`)을 다시 훑어 답했다. 스위치와 **다른 스위치의 값**, 붙은 값 속 글자를 못 가른다.
   재현: `runuser -s -u sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs` — `-s` 가 `-u` 를 셸 경로로 먹어 runuser 는 아무것도 안 돌리는데, 다시 훑기가 `-u` 를 찾아 `sed -i` 를 명령으로 읽었다. **거짓 막음**이고 CLAUDE.md 가 가장 비싸게 치는 쪽이다. `runuser -s/usr/bin/bash sed -i …` 는 경로 속 `u` 로 같은 자리에 닿는다.
7. `src/cmd/hook.rs:277` — 스냅샷 곳간을 막지 않은 Shell PreToolUse 마다 미리 채웠는데, 그것을 읽는 자(`stands`)는 `moai mv … --from` 토막에서만 닿는다.
   잰 것: 워크트리에서 `moai -C <루트> show <id>`(이 저장소 규약이 시키는 꼴)가 도구 호출마다 루트의 issues.jsonl 을 통째로 갈랐다 — 1,700 이슈에 +67ms, `-C <남의 저장소>` 는 +226ms(두 번 읽었다). 옛 `OnceCell` 닫힘은 그 경우 아무것도 안 읽었다.
8. `src/hook.rs:1169` — `Layer::Subst { nth }` 가 서로 모르는 0부터의 셈 둘(`end_by` 의 `inner`, `relex` 의 `texts`)에서 나와, 그 필드를 더한 까닭이 절반만 섰다.
   재현: `echo "$(set -e)" <<EOF` / `$(moai mv t-1 in_progress; sed -i …)` / `EOF` 가 `Subst{at:1,nth:0}` 인 겹 둘을 나란히 심어, `frames` 의 `take_while` 이 그 사이에서 안 걷는다. 지금 판정은 안 바뀌지만 그것은 깊이로 걷는 딴 자가 해 주는 일이고, 그 필드의 제 글이 바로 그것에 기대지 말라고 적었다.
9. `src/hook.rs:2233` — su 는 뒤 피연산자를 대상 셸의 argv 에 잇는다. `--` 뒤에 적은 `-c` 도 그 셸에 닿는데, 파서는 `--` 에서 끊어 못 본다.
   재현: `su alice -- -c 'sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs'` 가 훅을 지나가는데 su 는 alice 로 `bash -c 'sed -i …'` 를 바뀌지 않은 자리에서 돌린다. 같은 셈으로 `su alice ./script.sh` 의 스크립트도 안 보인다. **안 고쳤다** — su 의 argv 짓는 법을 모델로 세워야 닫힌다.
10. `src/hook.rs:2090` — `xargs` 가 `WRAPPERS` 에도 `PREFIXES` 에도 없다. 옆의 stdbuf·nice·env 줄과 같은 꼴인데.
    재현: `echo x | xargs sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs` 가 파일을 고치는데 훅이 빈손으로 넘긴다(확인했다). 이 diff 전부터고 **안 고쳤다** — 옵션 표를 틀리게 적으면(`-I`·`-i`·`-E`·`-a`·`-s`·`-n`·`-P`·`-L`·`-d` 가 다 값을 받는다) 없는 것보다 나쁘다.
11. `src/hook.rs:277` — `Text::Line` 이 `-c` 글 뒤의 낱말을 버리는 것은 맞지만, 그 글 **안**에서 `$0`·`$1`·`$@` 로 닿는다. 주석은 거짓 막음 쪽만 말한다.
    재현: `su -c 'sed -i s/a/b/ "$1"' alice src/x.rs` 가 지나간다. `bash -c` 와 함께 남는 자리고, 꼬리를 "닿을 수 없다" 로 읽지 않게 주석 한 줄이 든다.
12. `src/hook.rs:2294` — `hands` 가지가 `-c` 를 보는 순간 `Wrapped::Hands` 를 내, su 가 문서로 적은 로그인 꼴의 맨 뒤 `-` 에 닿지 못한다. 한 명령의 두 철자가 반대 판정을 받는다.
    재현: `su -c 'sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs' -` 는 막고 `su - -c 'sed -i …'` 는 지나간다. 둘 다 대상 사용자의 홈에서 로그인 셸을 돌려 상대 경로가 딴 곳을 가리킨다. **안 고쳤다** — `Hands` 반환을 피연산자 훑기 뒤로 미뤄야 한다.
13. `src/hook.rs:782` — `Lexer::kept` 가 `Lexer::inner` 와 글자째 같은 값이고, 그 위에 `leave()` 에서 치환마다 String 을 한 벌 더 떴다. 모든 명령줄의 모든 `$(…)`·백틱이 지나는 길이다.
    까닭: `inner` 는 `end_by` 만 비우는데 `subs_of` 는 `end_by` 에 닿을 수 없다(`Ctx::Doc` 은 아무도 안 걷어 `plain` 이 안 돈다). 둘을 매는 불변이 없어, 뒤에 누가 `inner` 를 딴 데서 비우면 조용히 갈린다.
14. `src/hook.rs:1100` — `Lexer::relex` 안에 둔 `enum Handed` 가 모듈의 `struct Handed` 를 가렸고, 한 식 안에서 둘이 같이 산다.
    `own.iter().map(|h| (h.text.as_str(), if h.fork { Handed::Fork { … } } else { Handed::Eval }))` 가 `h` 로는 구조체를 읽고 같은 줄에서 열거를 부른다. 스물다섯 줄 아래 이 파일의 제 주석이 `deep` 이라는 이름에 바로 그것을 하지 말라고 적었다.
15. `src/hook.rs:4073` — `open()` 을 뽑으면서 그냥 대입 하나가 말없이 `min` 이 됐다(`negated_at = Some(seg.level + 1)` → `open(&mut blocks.negated, seg.level + 1)`). `open` 의 제 글은 제가 흡수한 자리마다 이미 그 셈이었다고 적는다.
    `! ( ! ( true ) ; moai mv t-1 in_progress ) && sed -i …` — develop 에서는 안쪽 `!` 가 바깥 자리를 덮어써 안쪽 묶음이 닫히자마자 `left()` 가 걷었고, 집기가 세어져 쓰기가 지나갔다. bash 는 집기가 **져야** 그 `&&` 에 닿는다. 새 읽기가 옳지만 말없이 바뀌었고, 스스로를 순수한 중복 제거라 적은 덩이 안에서 재는 자가 없다. **보고만, 안 바꿨다.**

**뒤집힌 주장 하나**: `a || { if ! …; fi; }` 에서 `credit` 이 적은 집기가 `prune` 을 살아남는다던 것은 재현되지 않았다 — 그 꼴들 어디에도 집기가 안 적힌다.

**확인**: 새로 더하거나 늘린 시험마다 제 고침을 되돌려 붉어지는 것을 보았다. `cargo test` 1,274 + 484 통과, `cargo fmt --check` 깨끗, 건드린 파일에 `cargo clippy --all-targets` 깨끗(남은 경고 `src/view.rs:3436` 은 develop 머지가 들고 온 것이다).

반영과 넘김 — 내 판단

**반영(fix 커밋 둘).**

- `8939de6` 가 열하나를 받았다. 그 가운데 **여섯이 이 판이 새로 연 자리**다 — `subs_of` 가 겹 상한 밖에서 돌던 것(1번, 스택을 넘겨 바이너리가 죽었다), 같은 자리가 예산을 다시 채우던 것(4번), `lex.later` 를 버려 heredoc 속 heredoc 의 쓰기가 새던 것(2번), moai-n3wq 의 `came` 문턱이 너무 느슨했던 것(3번), moai-lwil 의 `nth` 가 두 셈에서 나와 절반만 서던 것(8번), moai-dkph 의 `Runs::With` 가 다시 훑다 거짓으로 막던 것(6번). 나머지 다섯은 열려 하던 구멍이 안 닫힌 자리(5번 `su <사용자> -c`)와 다듬기(7·13·14번)다
- `dbd8b94` 가 15번을 받았다. **코드는 안 바꿨다** — 고침이 옳아서다. 리뷰가 짚은 것은 값이 틀렸다는 것이 아니라 **말없이 바뀌었고 재는 자가 없다**는 것이었고, 주석과 시험을 세워 그것을 메웠다

**내가 직접 재서 확인한 것.** 리뷰 말을 그대로 안 받았다. 헤드라인 다섯을 이 트리에서 다시 재 봤다 — 3번의 샘이 이제 막히고, `su alice -c` 와 `runuser alice -c` 가 막히고, heredoc 속 heredoc 의 쓰기가 막히고, 6번의 거짓 막음이 안 서고, moai-n3wq 가 세운 둘이 그대로 지나간다. 15번은 `open` 을 옛 뜻으로 되돌려 재 보니 정말 Pass → Deny 로 갈렸다.

**넘김 — 사람의 결정이나 따로 선 일이 든다.**

- **9번 `su alice -- -c '<글>'`** 과 `su alice ./script.sh` — su 가 뒤 피연산자를 대상 셸의 argv 에 잇는 것까지 모델로 세워야 닫힌다. moai-qqg2·moai-dkph 가 연 문의 남은 구석이라 그 줄로 멤버를 세울 값이 있다
- **10번 `xargs`** — `echo x | xargs sed -i …` 가 빈손으로 지나간다. 이 diff 전부터고, 옵션 표를 틀리게 적으면 없는 것보다 나쁘다는 리뷰의 판단에 동의한다. 제 이슈로 서야 할 일이다
- **11번 `su -c '… "$1"' alice src/x.rs`** — `bash -c` 와 함께 남는 자리다. 주석 한 줄로 "꼬리가 닿을 수 없다" 로 안 읽히게 하는 것이 옳고, 이 판에서는 안 했다
- **12번 `su -c '<글>' -`** — 한 명령의 두 철자가 반대 판정을 받는다. `Hands` 반환을 피연산자 훑기 뒤로 미뤄야 해서 이 판의 범위를 넘는다
- 리뷰가 다듬기로 짚고 스스로 넘긴 넷(`Scope`·`Blocks` 가 세 경계에서 걷히는데 `left` 의 글은 한 목록이라 적은 것, `hands` 가 빈 네 줄에 `text`·`runs` 가 잡음인 것, `route` 가 토막마다 `PathBuf` 를 뜨는 것, 시험 일곱에 `judge`·`stands`·`flags` 닫힘이 되풀이되는 것) — 값은 있으나 쓰기 경로를 안 건드리는 일이다

**뒤집힌 주장 하나**를 그대로 남긴다. `a || { if ! …; fi; }` 에서 `credit` 이 적은 집기가 `prune` 을 살아남는다던 것은 재현되지 않았다. 리뷰가 제 손으로 재어 접었다.

**이 판에서 배운 것.** 정리 아홉 가운데 **여섯이 새로 열었다.** "동작을 안 바꾸는 정리" 라는 말이 그대로 서는 판은 드물고, 이 판에서 내가 스스로 잰 것(자마다 망가뜨려 보기)은 **내가 이미 아는 자**만 재 봤다 — `subs_of` 가 겹 상한 밖이라는 것도, `nth` 가 두 셈에서 나온다는 것도 그 훑기에 안 들었다. 다음 판에서 같은 자리를 다시 만나면 **새로 만든 함수마다 "이것이 어느 상한 안에 서는가" 를 먼저 묻는다** — 1·4번이 한 뿌리고, 둘 다 새 함수가 제 생성자를 부른 자리다.

사고 — 리뷰가 도는 중에 가지를 다시 썼다

다음 사람이 "이 리뷰의 고침이 다 들어갔나" 를 물을 자리다.

- 무슨 일: 리뷰가 `--fix` 로 돌고 있는 동안 `moai-t5op` 커밋 제목을 `refactor:` 에서 `fix:` 로 고치려고 `git reset --hard e2b3c4c` 를 했다. 그때 워킹 트리의 **커밋 안 된 리뷰 고침이 다 사라졌다**
- 산 것 하나: `src/cmd/hook.rs`. 리셋 전에 병합 충돌 해결본을 떠 뒀는데 거기 7번 고침이 이미 들어 있었다. 그래서 그 하나는 **머지 커밋 `3716e41` 안에 제 `fix:` 커밋 없이** 들어가 있다 — 규약이 "리뷰 지적을 반영한 것은 별도 `fix:` 커밋" 이라 한 까닭이 그대로 드러난 자리다
- 되찾기: `git fsck --unreachable` 로 닿지 않는 blob 431개를 훑었다. 리뷰 id 가 박힌 것은 하나도 없었고 stash 도 비었다 — 리뷰가 `git add` 를 한 적이 없어 객체가 안 남았다
- 메운 길: 리뷰 에이전트에 가지를 다시 썼다고 알리고 **파일을 다시 읽어 고치고, 끝낼 때 고친 것을 빠짐없이 대라**고 했다. 에이전트가 그렇게 했고, 그 목록과 트리를 하나씩 맞춰 확인했다. 되넣은 것은 `8939de6` 에 섰다
- 다시 돌린 결과: `cargo test` 1,275 + 484 통과, `cargo fmt --check` 깨끗. 헤드라인 다섯은 내가 따로 재서 확인했다(판단 노트에 있다)
- 옛 자리: `backup-before-reword` 가지에 박아 뒀다. develop 에는 아무것도 안 나갔다
- 까닭: 감독이 "병합 전이고 워크트리 안이라 고칠 수 있다" 고 보냈고 나는 리뷰가 도는 것을 알면서 그대로 했다. 감독이 앞으로 리뷰가 도는 워크트리에는 가지 고치는 일을 안 보내기로 했다. 내 쪽 몫은 **도는 판 위에서 이력을 다시 쓰지 않는 것**이다

note: 열다섯 가운데 열하나를 반영했다(8939de6·dbd8b94) — 이 판이 새로 연 여섯(subs_of 가 겹 상한 밖, 예산 되채움, lex.later 버림, came 문턱, nth 두 셈, Runs::With 다시 훑기)과 moai-qqg2 가 못 닫은 su <사용자> -c, 그리고 다듬기 넷. 15번은 고침이 옳아 코드는 그대로 두고 주석과 시험을 세웠다. 넘긴 것: su 의 argv 잇기(9번)·xargs(10번)·su -c 글 안의 $1(11번)·su -c <글> - 의 두 철자(12번)는 따로 설 일이고, 리뷰가 스스로 넘긴 다듬기 넷은 쓰기 경로를 안 건드린다. 리뷰가 도는 중에 가지를 다시 써 고침이 한 번 날아간 사고는 노트에 따로 적었다.

## Fixes applied

- **`src/store.rs`** — `journal_files()` now splits the extension check from the stat, uses `p.metadata()` and records `note_unread` on `Err` instead of folding it into `false`. `UNREAD` became `(root, at, why)` with `note_unread(root, at, err)`, mirroring `MISSED`'s shape, so `main` can tell its own repo from a neighbour's. Added `a_journal_dir_that_cannot_be_stat_ed_is_told_not_swallowed`; both existing permission tests now capture results and restore the mode *before* asserting.
- **`src/main.rs`** — `unread_journals()` returns early on empty (no `said_lang()` config read on the hot path), resolves `here` via `Repo::find`, and the new pure `any_mine()` gates `cmd::note_partial()` to the current repo's own roots (absent `here` → flag, so "can't tell" never means "stay quiet"). Added the call to the `Err` branch, ordered before `redirected()` to match the Ok path. New unit test `a_neighbours_unread_journal_is_told_but_does_not_fail_the_run`.
- **`tests/cli.rs`** — `an_unreadable_journal_is_named_and_only_my_own_fails_the_run` drives the real binary over all three cases (neighbour = told + exit 0, own file = told + exit 1 with the rest of the row still printed, unsearchable dir = told + exit 1). Mutation-checked: removing `unread_journals()` from `main` makes it red.
- **`docs/recovery.md`** — corrected the exit-code claim and documented the neighbour-worktree rule.

Skipped: findings 8, 9, 10 with reasons above.

title: 늦게 닿은 층 요약이 연 줄을 Look::Shut 으로 덮는다
탐색기 상세의 에픽·마일스톤 줄에 겹침 표가 안 선다
follow_site 의 whoami 를 읽는 스레드로 옮긴다

text:
리뷰 원문 — `/code-review max --fix`, opus. 범위 `git diff develop...HEAD` (15 files). 10 finder angles + 1 gap sweep. `--fix` applied.

## Findings

1. `src/tui/layer.rs:346` — **Layer::read lost both production call sites in relayer_with and is now test-only, so the bin target compiles it as dead code and CI's ci-gate fails.** Verified by running the exact CI command (`cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`): `error: associated function 'read' is never used --> src/tui/layer.rs:346:12 ... -D dead-code implied by -D warnings` / `error: could not compile 'moai' (bin "moai")`. `cargo test` stays green, so it is invisible locally without clippy. On develop the function was live at both arms of relayer_with.

2. `src/tui/mod.rs:2513` — **opened_seats() gained `.filter(|_| self.on_layer())`, which also silences its second caller load_read_in_places() — a one-shot path with no retry — whenever you are inside a project.** Layer with A and B expanded; Enter into A. An old binary or hand edit rewrites the legacy `[read]` table in the user config. follow_config sets moved=true, reloads Seat::Here, then calls load_read_in_places(), which now iterates nothing. Climbing back does not repair it: follow_read_in keys off each project's read-marks file stamp, which the user-config edit never touched. B's rows keep the pre-change legacy overlay and show wrong [NEW] for the rest of the session. The new doc's self-heal claim holds only for the stamp-driven caller.

3. `src/tui/mod.rs:4036` — **Site::me is resolved once per site read, but answer() only refreshes self.site.me (Seat::Here), so already-expanded layer projects keep a stale identity for the whole session.** Machine with no git user and no --user/MOAI_ACTOR. `moai tui` on the layer, expand A and B (follow_site resolves me=None for each). Jot into B, answer the who-are-you prompt. self.user is set and B gets the identity; A's place.site.me stays None. want_site early-returns on site.is_some() so A is never re-read, and folding keeps the site — [NEW] never stands on A's rows again and `SPC m a` there always says nothing to mark. Before the diff recount_unread_in called whoami(root) with the fresh self.user and picked it up on the next recount.

4. `src/view.rs:375` — **The EpicLabel::Gone arm dropped the `clip(t, EPIC_CAP)` guard the Named arm beside it still applies, in both list (375) and ready (1301).** Before the diff the dangling wording arrived as one more String in the map and went through clip(t, EPIC_CAP) (cap 20) like every epic title. Now it bypasses it, so the epic cell is the only one in the table that can exceed EPIC_CAP. en is 16 cells and ko ~11, so it is latent — but zh/ja/es carry no entry yet and any translation past 18 cells widens the column past the cap all real titles are held to.

5. `src/tui/layer.rs:631` — **Moving the discard below the success return lets a stale layer sweep land after a row was opened and read; Layer::adopt then overwrites place.look wholesale — including with a Look::Shut — and re-stamps read_at, so stale() will not re-pick it.** A sweep over a slow mount transiently yields Look::Shut for project P. Before it returns the user presses `l` on P: open_place takes the Ok branch (read_at=None, early return) and never reaches the discard; follow_site installs a full Site with P's rows. The stale Looked then arrives and adopt does `p.read_at = Some(now); p.look = l.look` unconditionally, so P's header reads "can't read" above its live issue rows, and Layer::stale no longer selects it (read_at fresh; Shut is only clocked for Unreadable). The commit doc budgets only for "one count going a minute stale" — a stale Shut is a stronger, self-contradicting state.

6. `src/tui/mod.rs:3044` — **follow_site runs whoami (two `git config` subprocesses, ~33ms) on the UI thread once per site read — the one path moai-12yx/moai-ezwu deliberately moved onto a worker thread.** Layer::adopt re-queues a site read whenever a place's Marks move, and marks_of folds in every linked worktree's HEAD and issues.jsonl stamp — so any commit in any worktree of an expanded project triggers a re-read, and the frame that adopts it blocks ~33ms in std::process::Command between term.draw and event::poll. In this repo (6-7 sessions committing) that is a visible stutter per commit per open project. The read thread already owns `repo`. counting_new_rows_on_the_layer_does_not_ask_who_i_am pins the cost out of recount_unread_in but asserts nothing about follow_site.

7. `src/view.rs:1596` — **detail used a second key, detail.missing_epic, for the condition report.epic_gone now names — and that key still shipped its own parentheses, against the rule the diff wrote into i18n/README.md.** Verified by running the binary: `moai show --all` printed `(epic not there)` and `moai show <id>` printed `(no such epic)` for the same dangling reference. A translator who applies the new rule to detail.missing_epic and wraps it the way list/ready/prime now wrap report.epic_gone reproduces `((no such epic))` — the bug moai-snus was filed for. The new guard test asserted !starts_with('(') for report.epic_gone alone. (`tui.missing`, "(missing)"/"(없다)", is a third wording for the same fact in the explorer panel.)

8. `src/tui/draw.rs:2141` — **moai-v8jl was fixed on the CLI detail only — the TUI detail pane's epic and milestone fields still render a bare title with no branch mark, on the surface people actually sit in.** `about()` pushes `(say(lang,"tui.about.epic"), site.title_of(id))`, and Site::title_of has no access to `origin` at all — while the same function already marks the row's own id from `site.origin.branch(&i.id)` (draw.rs:2075) and the list rows below carry the glyph. With overlay on, open an issue whose epic was edited in a sibling worktree: the CLI now says `에픽  argos-e001  ⎇ feat/x 옆에서 고친 저장 계층` and the explorer says `에픽  옆에서 고친 저장 계층`. The two detail surfaces disagree about the same row.

9. `src/view.rs:1161` — **prime's new EpicLabel::Gone arm was the only cell in that function not passing through one_line, against the invariant stated ten lines above it.** The comment reads "**모든 칸이 one_line 을 지난다 — id 와 칸까지**" and every sibling arm honours it. prime's output is markdown streamed straight into an agent's context: a report.epic_gone translation containing a newline (the bundles are contributor-edited JSON and i18n/README.md invites new languages) splits a `- \`id\` p2 — title (…` bullet mid-line, so the second half stands as a fresh top-level markdown line — the exact injection the invariant's own comment describes.

10. `src/tui/layer.rs:1612` — **Two of the three new tests spawn real worker threads and never join them, so a detached worker walks the scratch directory while Scratch::drop removes it.** unfolding_a_row_keeps_the_layer_sweep_running presses `l`, which reaches unfold -> want_site -> App::read_wanted (mod.rs:3470) and really spawns a project-read thread into layer.reading; a_registry_from_another_file_does_not_become_the_layers_own ends right after relayer_with -> layer.launch() spawns a real summary sweep. `a` is declared after `s`, so `a` drops first and the handle is detached, then Scratch::drop runs remove_dir_all. Benign today only because prepare returns R<_> for filesystem errors — but a detached JoinHandle bypasses App::discarded/reap, which exists to re-raise worker panics, so the test goes green while the worker dies.

11. `src/tui/layer.rs:1616` — **`assert_eq!(a.let_go, 0)` in the new unfolding_a_row_keeps_the_layer_sweep_running cannot fail, so the symptom its doc names (the session-long urgent banner) was unguarded.** App::discard only increments let_go once discarded.len() >= DISCARDED_KEPT (8, mod.rs:417); the test starts with an empty discarded and can cause at most one discard, so let_go is 0 whether or not the bug is present. Reinstate the unconditional discard in open_place and only the preceding pending.is_some() assertion catches it.

12. `src/tui/mod.rs:7907` — **The rewritten enabled-side loop lost an assertion: it paired each DetailAt with exactly one Side, so Focus(Side::Left) at DetailAt::Right — the default layout — was no longer covered.** The old loop was `for at in [Left, Right] { assert!(Focus(Side::Left).enabled(&c).is_ok()) }`. Combined with the duplicated predicate below, if someone later narrows the keys.rs guard to "only the side pointing at the detail pane stands", Ctrl-w h goes silently dead at DetailAt::Right and the suite stays green, because the only assertion covering that pair was deleted.

13. `src/tui/mod.rs:3750` — **keys::Ctx's four pane-name fields (left/right/up/down_pane) are never read anywhere, and the diff's new guard is justified by a bar behaviour that cannot occur.** Their only consumer is Browse::what(), and nothing reaches what() for a Focus: draw::browse_hints lists only B::FocusNext, fkeys' keys::next_keys filters on `b.label.is_some()` while every Ctrl-w h/l/k/j row is declared with None, and menu::entries only walks SPC-prefixed rows. key_ctx pays four Pane::step(..).word(..) calls per frame for values nobody reads (the diff grew it from two to four), and the new arm's comment — "바가 '→ 탐색기' 라고 대면 …" — describes something the bar never does, so the next reader believes a behaviour that does not exist.

14. `src/tui/layer.rs:921` — **leave_project's placeholder Site is built with Site::of (me: None) and explicitly hand-carries lang across but not me, so the current seat's identity is dropped on every climb.** Benign today only because the blank site has no issues and no repo — recount_unread_in(Seat::Here) clears an empty set, follow_read_in bails on repo.is_none(), and App::write refuses on the layer before an Ask can be raised. It is the one transition in the ownership enumeration where the moved state is dropped rather than carried, and any future reader of Seat::Here's me while on_layer() silently sees "user unknown".

15. `src/tui/keys.rs:752` — **Three blocks are written twice with no shared home: the axis predicate (keys.rs:752 vs Pane::step at mod.rs:239), the want/mine/reg.filter registry guard (layer.rs:1015 and 1051), and pending.take()+discard (layer.rs:631 and 800).** The axis comment literally reads "가르는 자는 Pane::step 과 같은 자다 — 여기와 저기에 저마다 적으면 자리를 하나 더하는 날 한쪽만 고쳐져" and is followed by the second copy; the_pane_keys_follow_the_split drives both through a hand-written table so a drift stays green. For the registry guard only the Some(mut old) arm has a test, so the obvious next refinement (Registry::path is never canonicalized, so a symlinked or trailing-slash spelling compares unequal — user_config::same_dir exists for exactly this) lands in the tested arm while the untested copy keeps the old comparison and the first-build path silently adopts a foreign config.

**Refuted (kept out):** a candidate that `Ctrl-w Ctrl-j` is unreachable because crossterm maps Ctrl-J to Enter. crossterm 0.29 `event/sys/unix/parse.rs:99` reads `b'\n' if !is_raw_mode_enabled() => Enter` — the TUI runs in raw mode, so Ctrl-J falls through to the Ctrl+char branch and the binding works.

**Also noted, cut for the 15-item cap:** in a vertical split on a terminal shorter than `LIST_MIN_V + DETAIL_MIN_V`, `split_body` draws no detail pane while `c.detail` (= `detail_open`) is still true, so `Ctrl-w j`/`k` are accepted for a pane that does not exist and `draw.rs:135` undoes the focus next frame — `Ctrl-w w` already behaves this way by the same accepted post-draw reset, so the new keys join a pre-existing class.

## Fixes applied

Correctness:

- `Layer::read` → `#[cfg(test)]`. The CI gate now exits 0 (it failed before).
- Split `opened_seats()` into `seats_with_site()` (ungated) and `opened_seats()` (gated on `on_layer()`); `load_read_in_places` uses the ungated one. New test `a_changed_legacy_read_reaches_an_open_project_from_inside_another`, confirmed to fail with the fix reverted.
- Added `App::relearn_me_in_places()`, called from `answer()`, refreshing `me` on every layer place holding a `Site` (folded included). title: 감싸는 명령 표에 없는 것 열넷 — 그 뒤의 쓰기가 샌다
릴리스 캐시가 태그 판에서 안 맞는다 — 캐시는 판을 낸 ref 와 기본 가지에서만 읽힌다

text:
리뷰 원문 (`/code-review high --fix`, agent-a4894021ff19c8596). 이 세션에도 `ReportFindings` 가 없어 글로 냈다.

Reviewed `git diff develop...HEAD` (4 commits, CI/toolchain only — `ci.yml`, `release.yml`, `smoke.yml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `rust-toolchain.toml`). No Rust changed. The workflow logic itself holds up: the cache steps really do precede the first rustup proxy call in every job that needs one, the `msrv` gate mirrors `size-budget`'s `!cancelled() && … != 'false'` shape, and the `rust-version` parse is validated before it reaches a shell.

## Findings

- `CONTRIBUTING.md:47` — **medium.** "CI has three jobs … the third shows as skipped - not failed - on a pull request that touched documentation alone." The diff adds a fourth job (`msrv`) and updates `ci.yml`'s own header to "잡은 넷이다", but leaves this sentence at three. A contributor reading it counts three checks on their PR and takes the fourth as something gone wrong; and the skip note now applies to two jobs, not one.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:72` — **medium.** "`rust-version` in `Cargo.toml` now records the minimum rather than proving it — nothing builds on that version." That is exactly the statement the `msrv` job was created to falsify. `rust-toolchain.toml` and `CHANGELOG.md` were both rewritten for it in this diff; this third copy was missed, so the docs now contradict each other on whether anything walks 1.88.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:91` — **low.** The new toolchain cache lives in a workflow that only fires on `push: tags` and `workflow_dispatch`. GitHub restores caches from the current ref or the default branch only, so a cache written under `refs/tags/v0.1.0` is invisible to `refs/tags/v0.2.0`, and the key `rustup-${{ matrix.target }}-…` is never written on `develop`. Concretely: every release still pays the full 129MB fetch + xz unpack per matrix leg, while the step comment promises "캐시가 맞은 판에서는 이미 자리에 있어 아무것도 안 받는다." The ordering fix in the same hunk is correct and worth keeping — it is only the payoff that will not land. (The pre-existing `cargo-rel-*` cache has the same scoping problem, so this is a pattern, not a new regression.)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:106` (also `release.yml:81`, `smoke.yml:62`) — **low.** `sed -n 's/^channel *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/p'` accepts only the double-quoted, space-separated form. Valid TOML that the file's own "올릴 때" instructions do not forbid — `channel = '1.97.1'`, or a tab before `=` — yields an empty match and hard-fails every job with "channel 을 못 읽었다". And because `set -euo pipefail` is on, a *missing* `rust-toolchain.toml` kills the step at `sed` before the friendly `::error::` ever prints; the `-z` guard only covers "file present, line absent."

## Fixed

- Both `CONTRIBUTING.md` findings, in the working tree (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, +9/-7, uncommitted). Job count corrected to four with the `msrv` job described, the skip note widened to "the last two", and the stale `rust-version` sentence replaced with what the `msrv` job actually does. English-only text, so no Korean polishing pass applies.

## Skipped

- The `release.yml` cache-scoping finding: the only real fix is either dropping the step or restructuring how release runs get a warm cache (e.g. priming it from a default-branch run), both design calls well outside this diff. Left the step in place and reported it instead.
- The `sed` fragility: the three copies work on the file as committed, and hardening the expression in all four places means editing Korean workflow prose for a case nobody has hit. Reported rather than churned.

title: 리뷰 — 넘긴 글과 감싸는 명령 표, 치환을 두 번 읽던 자리

text:
내가 판단한 것 — 리뷰가 넘긴 둘을 넘긴 채로 두지 않는다.

1. `CONTRIBUTING.md` 둘 (1·2번) — **리뷰가 고친 것을 그대로 담았다** (`3a9bade`). 같은 말이 넷에 흩어져 있었고 이 가지가 셋만 고쳤다.

2. `release.yml` 의 캐시가 태그 판에서 안 맞는 것 (3번) — **주석의 약속을 걷고 idea `moai-uave` 로 담았다** (`37b808e`). 리뷰가 옳다. GitHub 은 캐시를 판을 낸 ref 와 기본 가지에서만 읽고, 이 워크플로는 태그와 손으로 돌린 판에서만 돈다. 다만 기본 가지가 `develop` 이라, 누가 거기서 한 번 돌려 두면 태그 판이 그것을 읽는다 — 오늘도 두 판이 그렇게 돌았다. 스텝을 걷지 않은 까닭은 순서를 바로잡은 값이 그와 별개로 서기 때문이다. 맞히는 판에서 캐시가 rustup 앞에 서 있어야 값이 있고, 그 자리가 비어 있던 것이 리뷰 `moai-ch4z.639` 가 원래 짚은 것이다. 고치는 길(릴리스 행렬을 develop 에서도 돌린다 · 태그 판은 캐시를 안 쓴다)은 둘 다 설계 결정이고, 옆의 `cargo-rel-*` 도 처음부터 같은 자리라 한 스텝만 고쳐서는 안 끝난다.

3. sed 가 좁은 것 (4번) — **고쳤다** (`e02a99c`). 꼴을 넓힌 것(따옴표 둘 다·탭)보다 중한 것은 지는 방식을 바꾼 것이다. 이 스텝이 하는 일은 캐시를 맞히는 것뿐이라 못 맞히면 rustup 이 그대로 받으면 되는데, 거기서 `exit 1` 을 하면 코드와 상관없는 까닭으로 멀쩡한 PR 이 붉어진다 — 리뷰가 낸 여섯째 각도("이 게이트가 막아야 할 것만 막나")에 그대로 걸린다. 경고 한 줄을 내고 캐시 스텝만 건너뛴다. 파일이 아예 없을 때 sed 가 `set -e` 를 걸어 스텝을 죽이던 것도 같은 한 줄로 닫혔다.

리뷰가 "재 봤다" 고 적은 것 하나를 덧붙인다. 캐시 스텝이 rustup 프록시보다 앞에 서는지는 글로만 본 것이 아니라 여기서 쟀다 — `rustup toolchain list` 한 줄만 불러도 `rust-toolchain.toml` 이 걸려 박아 둔 1.97.1 을 통째로 받는다.
Next: 고침과 시험은 섰다. 리뷰 moai-r3l9.lmy 를 받아 반영한 뒤 develop 에 병합하고 닫는다.
Next: 고침과 시험은 섰다. 리뷰 moai-r3l9.lmy 를 받아 반영한 뒤 develop 에 병합하고 닫는다.
Next: 고침과 시험은 섰다. 리뷰 moai-r3l9.lmy 를 받아 반영한 뒤 develop 에 병합하고 닫는다. moai-bujq 는 이 줄이 닫히면 12/12 가 된다.
Next: /code-review max --fix 가 worktree-moai-r3l9 에서 도는 중이다. 원문 노트와 닫는 한 줄을 남기며 닫는다.

본문이 적어 둔 고칠 자리("낱말 전체가 치환 하나인 경우를 shell_text 가 unknowable 처럼 뺀다")만 했더니
막던 줄이 열렸다. 재서 찾았다.

    eval '$(moai mv t-1 in_progress --from todo)'   집기 []        (빼기 전에는 [t-1])
    eval '$(sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs)'                쓰기 Pass      (빼기 전에는 Deny)

작은따옴표 안의 `$( … )` 는 치환으로 안 돈다. 렉서가 그것을 안 읽으니 `eval` 이 그 글자를 읽어
그때가 처음 도는 자리고, 빼는 순간 그 줄의 집기도 쓰기도 아무도 안 본다. 따옴표 하나에 답이
뒤집히는데 낱말만 보아서는 그 둘이 똑같이 생겼다.

그래서 `Seg::eaten` 을 더했다 — 렉서가 그 토막의 낱말에서 **실제로 읽어 낸** 치환의 수다.
`shell_text` 는 덩이 수가 그보다 많으면 안 읽힌 것이 섞였다는 뜻으로 보고 글을 그대로 넘긴다.
겹 상한(`Lexer::DEEP`)과 예산(`afford`)에 걸려 넘어간 치환도 안 센다 — 안 읽은 것을 읽었다고
세면 같은 구멍이 난다.

**본문의 길로 돌아가지 마라.** 세지 않고 빼는 판은 시험
`a_word_that_is_only_substitutions_is_not_the_text_handed_to_a_shell` 의 작은따옴표 줄에서
붉어진다.

## Fixes applied (`src/hook.rs`, +149/−86, working tree only — nothing committed)

**Fixed**

- **#1 + #5 + #8 + #13 together, at the root.** `Seg::eaten` now holds the substitution **texts** the lexer actually read (`Vec<String>`, moved out of `Lexer::inner`, pushed only after the inner lexer really produced a segment), and the new `read_already` matches the handed text against those recorded texts character-for-character instead of re-scanning it. `subst_groups` is deleted — with it go the second hand-rolled shell scanner, its quote-blindness, its two-meaning `None`, and the unguarded `depth -= 1`. There is now one reader of the grammar, and it is the lexer.
- **#6** `su -- - -c '<write>'` — the `--` tail is tracked separately (`dashed`), so only a `-` getopt actually saw counts as the login `-`.
- **#7** `--open-tty` added to `xargs`' `free`.
- **#14** `Wrapped::Shell(Vec<usize>)` carries positions like every other variant; `ops.extend` is guarded by `mixes`.
- **#15** the seven doc links repointed at `handed_text`; the moai-drli paragraph moved down onto the `Hands` branch it describes.
- Also: `basename(head)` bound once in its own `match`; `hands_at` holds an `Option<Wrapped>` rather than two of `Wrapped::Hands`' three fields (the positional tuple `Wrapper`'s own doc argues against).
- **Tests**: the moai-6qkc test gained the sibling-substitution, redirect-target, assignment-prefix, `$()`/`$(<f)` and quoted-paren cases (each was green before the fix and red without it); the su test gained `su -- - -c '…'` and the `./script.sh -c '<write>'` pair that pins `shell_argv`'s non-option anchor (four of its existing `Pass` rows are inert — they Pass for any implementation); the xargs test gained `--open-tty`.

**Skipped, with reasons**

- **#2, #3, #4, #10, #11, #12** need a concept the table does not have (suppress the pick axis for a command whose argv is knowably incomplete; let `Stops` blind only the cwd-relative judgments, not rule 4; teach the write rule about a replace-string). Each would change behaviour the commits deliberately chose and reach well outside the diff. **#2 and #3 are the two I would fix next** — #2 reopens the one rule CLAUDE.md names by itself, and #3 is a false deny, which this repo ranks above a leak.
- **#9** is unchanged by my fix and predates the diff: the drop is per-text, so `bash -c "echo $(pick)"` still double-records. Narrowing it needs the lexer to hand back spans, not texts.
- **`mixes` derived from `w.runs`** (flagged by two angles as wanting an explicit `Wrapper` field): skipped deliberately. Line 2666 needs `!Always` for a genuinely different question ("do the trailing operands go to a shell"), so a second near-identical field creates a new way for the two to disagree. The derivation is documented; I left it.
- **`runuser -u X -c '…'`** is rejected by real runuser but still judged (false deny) — pre-existing shape, not touched by the diff.

**Convention findings (not code, not applied)** — per CLAUDE.md "떠오른 것은 적어 둔다" / AGENTS.md fork 1:

- Idea `moai-5pse` ("감싸는 명령 표에 없는 것 열넷 — 그 뒤의 쓰기가 샌다") came straight out of `moai-ulaa`, a member of the still-open epic `moai-r3l9` ("훅이 아직 새는 자리"), and its stated reason for being outside is a not-now reason. When `moai-729n` and `moai-ulaa` close, the epic stands `done` with 14 measured leaks open. `moai idea promote moai-5pse -e moai-r3l9 --from -`.
- The `$1` positional-argument leak (`su -c 'sed -i s/a/b/ "$1"' 남 src/x.rs`, and `bash -c '<글>' 남 src/x.rs` identically) is conceded in a source comment at hook.rs:302 and exists nowhere the board, `ready` or `moai show -g` can find it.
- `su 남 ./script.sh` is listed in `moai-729n`'s body as something that leaks, but the new test asserts `Pass`; the reason lives only in a test comment, not on the issue.

note: 열다섯 가운데 여덟을 받았다. 가장 큰 것은 내가 낸 구멍이다 — eaten 을 수로 견주어 옆 낱말의 치환 하나가 안 읽힌 글을 덮었고 규칙 넷이 다 샜다. 렉서가 적어 둔 글과 글자째 맞추도록 고치고 subst_groups 를 지웠다. xargs -I 의 자리표를 경로로 풀어 잘못 막던 것, su -- - 의 로그인 오독, --open-tty, Wrapped::Shell 이 낱말을 베끼던 것, 어긋난 문서 링크 일곱도 받았다. 넘긴 것은 idea 셋으로 담았다 — moai-oq8k(Stops 가 자리를 안 타는 규칙까지 가린다), moai-tq28(xargs 가 argv 를 덧붙여 집기를 지어낸다), moai-4kus(자리 인자와 그 글을 받는 프로그램). mixes 를 Wrapper 의 필드로 빼라는 것은 안 받았다: 아래 !Always 는 다른 물음이라 둘이 어긋날 길이 새로 생긴다. moai-5pse 를 에픽 멤버로 올리라는 것은 감독 결정대로 idea 에 둔다. 시험이 되돌림을 잡는지 고침마다 코드를 되돌려 재 봤다.

text:
Max-effort recall review of `git diff develop...HEAD` in worktree `.claude/worktrees/moai-ug47`
(commits 70c10ab, c9dee65 — moai-i7b6, moai-l2he, moai-p3kb), with `--fix` applied.

Method: 10 finder angles + 1 gap sweep, all with `rustc` probes rather than reasoning alone.

## Findings (ranked)

1. `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:1072` — A third byte-identical copy of `runnable` survived the
   consolidation, and `cmd::runnable`'s new doc records the count as two. `merge_driver::on_path`
   feeds `chosen_command`, which writes an absolute binary path into `.git/config`. A portability
   fix landed on `cmd::runnable` (the only place anyone greps, because the doc says there were two)
   would miss it, and the merge driver keeps planting a path judged by the old rule — every merge of
   `.moai/issues.jsonl` then silently falls back to git's default line merge.

2. `src/store.rs:1510` — The root clamp added to the merged `lexical` is a verified no-op, so the
   doc, both new tests and commit c9dee65 record a hook rule-2 leak that never existed.
   `PathBuf::pop()` on "/" returns false and leaves "/" (`Path::new("/").parent()` is None).
   Compiling develop's unclamped fold against the new one: `/../repo/src/store.rs` gives
   `/repo/src/store.rs` under both, and `counted()` returns Deny under both. Seven independent
   sweeps (16 / 24 / 1296 / 200000 inputs) found zero divergences. Doc comments and commit messages
   are this repo's design record, so the next reader believes rule 2 leaked on develop and that two
   of three copies were unsafe; both false, and the new tests stay green with the clamp deleted.

3. `src/tz.rs:213` — `name_under` folds only the relative branch, so an absolute TZ path or
   localtime target carrying `..` yields a bogus zone name — and the diff rewrote the doc to claim
   `store::lexical` does the folding. `TZ=/usr/share/zoneinfo/../zoneinfo/Asia/Tokyo` returns the
   name `../zoneinfo/Asia/Tokyo`; `safe_join` rejects the `..`, the zone resolves to Unknown, the
   screen stands in UTC and every command grows the "this timezone is unknown" line — the exact
   failure the function's own doc says it prevents. Reproduced as a failing assertion.

4. `src/store.rs:1557` — `real.join("")` appends a trailing separator when the whole path resolves;
   the deleted `user_config::real_prefix` never did, so `spellings()` output changed bytes versus
   develop. `spellings("gone/../link", d)` with `gone` missing and `link` a symlink yields
   `.../real/` on HEAD where develop gave `.../real`. Inert today only because `PathBuf` equality is
   component-wise and every consumer matches with `contains`; one `display()`/`to_str()` comparison
   away from a spelling that matches nothing.

5. `src/cmd/mod.rs:129` — `runnable`'s doc promises "can the shell actually run this" but
   `mode & 0o111` answers "can anyone run this". A hook exe 0700-owned by another user, or on a
   `noexec` mount, passes `runnable`; `skill::runs` reports the hook healthy; the hook's
   `command -v … && "<exe>"` dies with EACCES/126 and `|| exit 0` swallows it. Verified with a
   mode-0001 file: `mode&0o111 != 0` true, `access(X_OK)` false, exec exits 126. `merge_driver.rs:793`
   already recorded this caveat; the consolidation promoted the shallow predicate to authoritative
   and wrote the stronger promise onto it.

6. `src/store.rs:1551` — The `Option<PathBuf>` → `PathBuf` change dropped the only structural guard
   against re-appending a `..` after resolving a symlinked ancestor. `real_prefix("/nope/..")`
   returned None before and now returns `/nope/..`; `<dir>/link/../x` would become
   `<link-target>/../x`, a different directory. Unreachable today since both callers pre-fold, but
   the helper moved from private to `pub(crate)` across three modules and the contract became prose.

7. `src/hook.rs:7833` — The regression assertion added for the root clamp passes unchanged against
   develop, so it guards nothing while its comment claims it closes a live rule-2 bypass.

8. `src/tz.rs:466` — The assertion that replaced the two deleted `flatten` unit tests is a verbatim
   duplicate of tz.rs:449, so the swap removed tz's only CurDir-folding coverage and added nothing.

9. `src/hook.rs:5420` — The rename note claims `read_marks::settle` hands back the reason it could
   not resolve, which is false for a missing path — the only case `real_path` exists to serve.
   `settle` returns `Settled::Fallen(None)` for NotFound/NotADirectory and says so in its own header;
   it attaches a reason only for other errors like ELOOP. moai-l2he's permanent record of how the two
   one-letter-apart names differ is written on the wrong axis, and the difference that actually bites
   (whole-path vs deepest-living-ancestor) is demoted. The same sentence is in commit c9dee65.

10. `src/cmd/mod.rs:139` — The recorded reason for leaving `tui::on_path` out of the merge is wrong
    on both halves. The TUI launches the editor through `sh -c '<editor> "$@"'` too, so it is in the
    same "must match what the shell sees" bucket the doc assigns only to `skill`; and `on_path` is
    consulted for exactly two built-in names, once per launch, so the cost weighed against is two
    `sh` spawns, not "many names".

11. `src/hook.rs:5423` — The moai-l2he rename moved the confusable name into the `store::real*`
    family this same commit creates — `hook::real_path` now sits one word from `store::real`.
    A later hook check writes `crate::store::real(&resolve(path, root))`, reading the two as
    synonyms. For a not-yet-created file `store::real` fails to canonicalize and returns the typed
    spelling; if any ancestor is a symlink (TMPDIR, macOS /tmp or /var, a symlinked project)
    `strip_prefix(root)` misses, `counted` returns false and the Write passes silently — the leak the
    2026-09-19 decision closed.

12. `src/store.rs:1685` — The new `real_prefix` fallback assertion depends on the test process's
    working directory. `real_prefix("없는자리/x")` only reaches the fallback because
    `canonicalize("")` fails. If the cwd ever holds a directory named `없는자리` the second ancestor
    resolves and the assertion flips; nothing sets the cwd.

13. `src/hook.rs:5386` — `counted` heap-allocates a full copy of the relative path purely to keep a
    borrow alive past the end of the statement. One malloc+memcpy per checked path, on every
    Edit/Write hook and once per path mined out of a shell snippet.

14. `src/user_config.rs:1703` — `spellings` keeps the `Option` array + `flatten` shape now that only
    one element is optional, and eagerly canonicalizes the same path twice.

15. `src/hook.rs:3489` — `guard_edit` resolves the same target string twice on the deny path —
    `counted()` then `rel_to()` each run a full lexical + real_prefix walk. Two redundant
    `canonicalize` calls per refusal at ~20 µs each.

## Fixes applied

All of the above except #15, and #14 only partly. 1780 tests pass,
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean. Diff: 6 files, +97/−45
(mostly doc corrections).

Behaviour changes, each proved by reverting the fix and watching the new test fail:
- `src/tz.rs:213` — absolute branch of `name_under` now folds through `store::lexical`. Reverted, the
  test reports `Some("../zoneinfo/Asia/Tokyo")` instead of `Some("Asia/Tokyo")`.
- `src/store.rs:1557` — `real_prefix` no longer appends a trailing separator, restoring develop's
  `spellings` output. Reverted, the new assertion reports `".../real/"` vs `".../real"`.
- `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs` — third `runnable` deleted; `grep -rn "fn runnable" src/` now returns
  exactly one definition. The absolute-PATH-entry filter stays on `on_path`, where it belongs.

text:
All green: 1,299 + 487 tests pass, `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## Findings

**`src/report.rs:1337` — medium — `Stand::deferred` undercounts when the group is itself deferred *and* a member carries its own deferral.**
`counted()` deliberately keeps members that dropped out only because the group inherited a deferral, so the difference `of.len() - counted.len()` is 0 for a wholly-deferred group — but it is 1 (not 0, not N) when one member was *also* deferred on its own. Reproduced with the built binary: an epic with two members, one deferred individually, then the epic deferred, renders `0/2   미룬 1   미룸` on the board and `"deferred":1` in `status --json`, while the member list right below shows **both** members as `미룸`. A reader (or an agent) computing `total - done - deferred` concludes one member is still pickable when none is. This contradicts the field's own doc (`묶음 제가 받은 미룸으로 빠진 멤버는 안 센다`) and the `view.rs` comment asserting the tail never appears on a deferred group.

**`tests/cli.rs:15778` — low — the `--worktree` half of `an_unread_journal_stands_in_the_json_beside_the_row_it_cost` was vacuous.**
It called `show <id> --json --worktree`, but the single-issue path reads only that row's own root's journal, so the locked sibling journal was never touched and `journal_unread()` was empty regardless. Proved by mutation: replacing `Some(journal_root)` with `None` in `src/cmd/show.rs:536` left the test green. The list path (`work_by_id`) is the only place where two checkouts' failures mix in one run.

**`src/main.rs:285`, `src/main.rs:397`, `tests/cli.rs:12599` — low — comments say the exit code is the *only* discriminator "until the `--json` key lands (moai-f2lc)".** This PR lands that key, so three comments now state the opposite of the code beside them.

**`src/view.rs:987`, `src/report.rs:1264` — low — comments assert an invariant the code did not hold** (see finding 1).

**`src/store.rs:1142` — low — `unread_kind`'s doc claims `NotFound` never arrives.** It does: `Repo::journal_files` (`src/store.rs:607`) calls `note_unread` on `p.metadata()` failure, which is `NotFound` for a broken symlink under `.moai/journal/`.

## What was fixed

- `src/report.rs` — `group_stands_in` now returns `deferred = 0` when the group itself is in `roots` (out of plan); the field doc and the inline comment were rewritten to say why. Added the in-between case to `a_groups_deferred_members_are_counted_beside_the_bar` (epic deferred + one member separately deferred → 0).
- `src/view.rs` — corrected the board comment, and extended `the_bar_says_how_many_of_its_members_are_deferred` with the same case at the rendering layer.
- `tests/cli.rs` — the `--worktree` block of the new JSON test now uses the list form (`show --json --worktree`) and asserts the sibling-only row *does* carry `journal_error` while the local row does not. Mutation-checked: widening the root filter to `None` now fails this assertion.
- `src/main.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `src/store.rs` — the four stale/incorrect doc claims above.

Nothing was skipped. Behaviour verified by hand: the normal case still renders `1/2   미룬 1   닫힘`, and the wholly-deferred epic now renders `0/2   미룸`.

text:
리뷰 원문 — `/code-review max --fix`, opus. 범위 `fb528e8...HEAD` (moai-ctcb 의 층 쓸기 세대 + moai-t0qd 의 상세 겹침 표, `src/tui/draw.rs`·`src/tui/layer.rs`). 10 finder angles + verification pass + gap sweep + 2 empirical probe tests (run and reverted). `--fix` applied.

## Findings (15)

1. `src/tui/draw.rs:2446` — **field() charges the branch mark against the value's budget but never clips the mark itself, so on common terminal widths the epic/milestone/blocked title collapses to nothing and the branch name ends up clipped at BOTH ends by the outer fit().** Reproduced with a probe test. Detail pane on the right (LEFT=55), Korean UI, branch `worktree-moai-hela2`. term=80 → `에픽 ⎇ …tree-moai-hela2 옆에…` (title down to 2 cells); term=60 → `에픽 ⎇ …tree-moai-h…` — title gone and the branch cut front AND back, destroying exactly the tail clip_front exists to preserve (draw.rs:1388 records that the tail carries the issue id). A name cut at both ends reads as a different worktree. FIXED.

2. `src/tui/layer.rs:683` — **open_place's rustdoc was not updated and now contradicts its own body**: it states the failed branch drops the sweep (it no longer does) and lists the just-fixed late-clobber as an accepted cost. `**못 연 갈래에서만 도는 층 읽기를 버린다**` is false — drop_layer_sweep's only caller is enter_project. The `**무는 대가**` paragraph describes a late sweep adopting a value over an opened row and re-stamping the clock, which is precisely what Place::set_at now prevents. In a repo where the doc is the design record, the next session reads this and re-adds the discard, undoing moai-0jqh. enter_project's inline comment said the same. FIXED (both rewritten, incl. the real new cost).

3. `src/tui/layer.rs:725` — **Stamping open_place's SUCCESS branch makes the expand path (read_wanted) throw away the in-flight sweep's perfectly good answer for the row the user just opened**, leaving its header on `읽는 중` for an extra sweep cycle. Reproduced: two projects, a sweep in flight with both answers built; press `l` on row one → want_site → read_wanted → open_place(Lean) → set_by_hand bumps rounds. After follow(): `two` (untouched) is Look::Open, `one` is still Look::Unread — header renders `읽는 중` with issue rows drawn underneath. Self-heals only after the current sweep drains (launch() refuses while pending.is_some()) plus a fresh read. moai-ctcb's bug is a late `Shut` landing on a live row; a late `Open` here is harmless. NOT FIXED — narrowing adopt to reject only pessimistic answers is a design call; the cost is now written into open_place's `무는 대가`.

4. `src/tui/layer.rs:1264` — **follow_layer advances self.site.now on every Ok from the channel even when adopt discarded the answer, so the header's `↻` claims a refresh that landed nowhere.** climb (layer.rs:959) documents that this clock must NOT move on a read that has not landed — `시각은 안 올린다 … 들일 때 follow_layer 가 올린다`. Before the generation guard every Ok was an adoption, so bumping was honest; now a sweep whose answers are all dropped still re-stamps the clock, and the hour-gap/day-based warnings recompute against a newer `now` while the summaries they annotate are the old ones. FIXED (adopt returns whether anything landed; the clock is gated on it).

5. `src/tui/mod.rs:3154` — **The second in-flight reader, Layer::reading (delivered by follow_site), carries no generation token and writes place.site unconditionally** — the symmetric race the fix does not close. Press `l` on project A; the read thread parses A at T0. Another session writes A at T0+10ms. The sweep lands at T0+60ms: set_at == round so it is adopted, p.marks becomes the NEW marks — but `again` is not pushed because p.site is still None (adopt's guard is `p.marks != l.marks && p.site.is_some()`). At T0+500ms follow_site installs the PRE-write Site. From then on marks_of(A) == p.marks forever, so nothing re-reads the rows: the header shows post-write counts over pre-write statuses for the rest of the session. NOT FIXED — outside the reviewed diff; deserves its own issue.

6. `src/tui/layer.rs:1780` — **The half of a_row_that_will_not_open_drops_the_sweeps_answer_but_not_the_sweep that proves the sibling row's answer still lands was vacuous.** layered(&cfg) settles the initial sweep, so `one` is already Look::Open before follow(). Replaying look_into over an unchanged directory yields an identical Look::Open, so the assertion passed even with adopt's guard flipped to an unconditional continue. Its own comment (`one 의 셈도 그새 바뀌었다`) described a setup step the test never performed. FIXED — the row is blanked to Look::Unread first; verified it now fails when adopt drops everything.

7. `src/tui/layer.rs:1837` — **Nothing proved that a LATER sweep's answer IS adopted for a stamped row** — the self-heal the whole cost-justification rests on. Both new tests keep the sender alive, so follow_layer never sees Disconnected, pending is never taken and launch() never fires a second sweep. The round that launch() stamps into pending was therefore never exercised against a row with non-zero set_at: if that capture were wrong, every answer for every stamped row would be discarded forever, the layer would re-read the same directories in a permanent loop, and all 72 layer tests would stay green. FIXED — the test now drops the sender and waits (5s deadline, 2ms sleep, same shape as settle_reads) for a real later sweep to land; verified it fails when launch() records the wrong generation.

8. `src/tui/draw.rs:3952` — **The new test asserts the mark on 2 of the 3 rows the change is named for; the blocked row — the arm-heavy match the diff reshaped most — was untested.** The loop ran over ["tui.about.epic", "tui.about.milestone"] only, and no test anywhere asserted BRANCH_GLYPH on a tui.block.* row. Replacing `fields.push((label.into(), mark, text))` with `None` in the blocker loop left the suite green. FIXED — the fixture now blocks its members on the overlaid milestone and the loop covers tui.block.open; verified the new assertion fails when the mark is removed.

9. `src/tui/draw.rs:2195` — **titled(site, b) was hoisted above the Blocker match, so the Missing arm resolved a title it discards and still attached a branch mark to a row whose text says the id does not exist.** Blocker::Missing is returned exactly when the id is not in site.index (report.rs:1470). The CLI guards this explicitly — view::block_line builds its title from b.issue, which is None there, and view::detail's epic line says `끊긴 쪽은 가지를 안 잰다`. Today origin.from and site.index come from one overlay so the spurious mark is latent, but every frame still paid an Index::find, an i18n lookup and a discarded `{id} (없음)` allocation per dangling blocked_by. FIXED — gated on `at`, which is exactly the Missing arm.

10. `src/tui/layer.rs:495` — **set_by_hand incremented self.rounds before checking places.get_mut(at), so a bad index burned a generation while stamping nothing.** The one case where the stamp silently does not happen is the one case where the counter advances, so Layer::rounds stops meaning "the generation of some hand-set row". Any later tightening to `>=`, or a `pending_round == rounds` currency check, then records a round no row can match. FIXED — the lookup comes first.

11. `src/tui/layer.rs:477` — **Layer::forget used the panicking `self.places[at]`** — the only panicking index on places in this file's non-test code — after a separate position() lookup. Safe only because position() produced the index two lines earlier. If the two lookups ever straddle a rebuild, the stamp lands on one row and the write panics the whole TUI where get_mut would no-op. FIXED — set_by_hand now returns the row, so stamp and write are one lookup at all three call sites.

12. `src/tui/layer.rs:725` — **open_place's success branch routed an already-opened Repo through two new `?` operators, so a bookkeeping miss would drop the Repo and report "could not open" with no notice.** Unreachable today, but it is a new silent-failure shape on a success path: enter_project does a bare `else { return }`, open_form declines silently, and read_wanted has already done wanted.remove(0) so that project is dropped from the queue for good — while rounds has been bumped and the row stamped. FIXED — the stamp is best-effort and Some(repo) is returned unconditionally.

13. `src/tui/draw.rs:2442` — **field's new doc claims the mark stands `CLI 상세와 같은 자리다(view::marked)`, contradicting a comment added by the same diff 250 lines up.** view::marked puts the mark immediately before the TITLE, so view::block_line renders `막힘 · <id>  ⎇ feat/x <title>`; field puts it before the whole value, `막힘  ⎇ feat/x · <id>  <title>`. about()'s blocker comment states that divergence and gives the reason. Two statements in one change that contradict each other leave the next reader unable to tell which placement was decided. FIXED.

14. `src/tui/layer.rs:1228` — **The comment defending `fresh.rounds = old.rounds` in relayer_with states its failure mode backwards.** It claims that recounting from 0 would let the in-flight sweep overwrite hand-set rows. It would not — that sweep's round was captured at spawn. What actually happens is the opposite and worse: rounds resets to 0 while places keep transplanted set_at > 0, so every FUTURE sweep's answer for those rows is rejected while read_at stays None, stale() re-picks them every step, and the layer re-reads the same directories forever without the counts ever standing. FIXED.

15. `src/tui/layer.rs:56` — **The Layer::rounds field doc asserts twice that only a keypress advances the generation, which is false and contradicts set_by_hand's own doc**; it also says the old blanket discard cost applied when a project was opened, where it only ever ran on the failed-to-open branch. `사람이 누른 키가 … 하나 오르고` and `셈은 사람이 키를 누를 때만 오르고` are both wrong: read_wanted reaches open_place → set_by_hand on the expand path, and adopt pushes marks-moved rows onto `wanted`, which read_wanted drains one per step. FIXED.

## What was fixed

`src/tui/draw.rs` — extracted `branch_tag(b, cap)`, one formatter for the `⎇ <branch>` mark shared by the list-row `branch_mark` and `field` (byte-identical copies before); it refuses to render when the name would clip away to nothing but `…`. `titled` now returns the bare branch name and `field` clips it against the room it actually has (`room - w - 4`, capped at BRANCH_CAP). `Blocker::Missing` no longer resolves a title or a mark. New test `a_branch_mark_in_a_narrow_pane_is_cut_once_and_keeps_its_tail`. `the_detail_pane_marks_an_epic_that_came_from_a_sibling_branch` now also pins the blocked row. Both detail tests isolate the pane with a shared `detail_pane` helper instead of `split('│').nth(1)`.

`src/tui/layer.rs` — `set_by_hand` validates the index before bumping `rounds` and returns the row; `forget`'s panicking `places[at]` and `open_place`'s two `?`-on-success are gone. `adopt` returns whether anything landed and `follow_layer` only advances `site.now` when it did. Four stale rationale blocks rewritten. Both new tests strengthened — the sibling-row assertion is no longer vacuous, and one drives a real later sweep to completion.

Every regression test was verified to fail against the pre-fix code and pass after.

## Not fixed, deliberately

- #3 (expand path discarding a good sweep answer) — a design call between `adopt` rejecting any stale answer vs. only pessimistic ones. The cost is now written into `open_place`'s `무는 대가`.
- #5 (`Layer::reading` has no generation guard) — a real hole, but outside this diff; worth its own issue.
- Also noted and left: the `tui.about.unused` row is a 4th row naming another issue that still gets no mark; `label_width` measures labels only, so marked rows' values start further right than unmarked ones; `Layer::forget` is only reached from `climb`, not from the sideways project jump; `read_wanted` leaks the `Tab` intent in `self.deep` when a project will not open.

Conventions angle found no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md violation.

## State

`cargo test` 1298 + 485 passing, `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean. Only `src/tui/draw.rs` and `src/tui/layer.rs` touched (+217/−67).

text:
리뷰 원문 — `/code-review max --fix` (agent-af53e6da4b692449f, 270,360토큰·툴콜 79). 열다섯 건, 무거운 순.

1. `src/hook.rs:6423` — The laziness probe in `one_turn_scans_the_command_line_once` samples its baseline AFTER the construction it measures, so the assertion is `x - x == 0` and can never fail. `let idle = Scan::new(&line, &cfg); let before = scans(); assert_eq!(scans() - before, 0, ...)` — nothing runs between the two `scans()` calls. The sibling probe it was copied from (hook.rs:6372) has the two lines in the opposite order and therefore tests something. The documented `게으르다` property is unasserted here.

2. `src/hook.rs:864` — `whole_for`'s `(0..words().count()).all(only)` is strictly stronger than the walk requires, so the memo misses on exactly the command shapes this repo's own conventions produce. `shell_scan` consults `only(n)` only behind `picks_up(&seg.words, cfg) &&` (hook.rs:4466, 4507), so a non-pick segment that `only` excludes cannot change the answer. But `cd /tmp && sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs` routes the post-`cd` segment `Route::Nowhere`, and `moai -C <other tracker> show && sed -i …` routes it `There`; `ours` is false there, `whole_for` returns false, and the turn pays a fresh full `shell_scan` in `guard_writes_in` plus another in `picked_in` — 4 walks when `settle` re-judges. The cache is never used on the motivating case.

3. `src/hook.rs:864` — `whole_for` evaluates the caller's predicate at EVERY segment index, putting `std::fs::canonicalize` syscalls into a per-tool-call hot path that previously avoided them. In production `only` is `ours` (cmd/hook.rs:216-219), whose `Route::There(n)` arm reaches `same()` → `user_config::same_dir` (user_config.rs:1720) = `a == b || canonicalize(a) == canonicalize(b)`. Before the diff `ours` was consulted only at `picks_up` segments; now every segment is asked, and `settle` re-runs `guard_writes_in` up to 3x. A `MOAI_HERE=1` worktree line `moai -C <root> show && moai -C <root> ready && sed -i …` pays up to 2 syscalls per There segment per judge pass. The doc's cost claim ("토막 수만큼 술어를 부르는 것뿐") silently assumes a cheap predicate.

4. `src/hook.rs:6392` — The headline win — one scan across `settle`'s up-to-three judge calls — is pinned by no assertion; the test calls `guard_shell_in` exactly once. The saving lives entirely in the PLACEMENT of `let scan = Scan::new(...)` at cmd/hook.rs:224, outside the `settle` closure at :233. Moving it inside that closure (a natural "shrink the capture set" edit, and the closure is where `line` and `repo.config` are both in scope) restores 3 full scans on every blocking Bash call, and all 1296 tests stay green.

5. `src/hook.rs:6400` — The `assert_eq!(scans() - before, 1)` cannot distinguish "the two questions shared one scan" from "rule 2 never ran at all". `Decision::then` short-circuits on `blocks()` (hook.rs:134), so if a future rule-1/rule-3 change makes `moai mv t-1 in_progress --from todo && sed -i …` deny, `guard_writes_in` is skipped, `picked_in` supplies the only scan, the count is still 1, and the sharing regresses silently with the test green.

6. `src/hook.rs:6415` — No test compares the VALUE `Scan::writes` returns against `shell_writes` under the same predicate — the tests only count scans, so a wrong cache hit is invisible. If `whole_for` is ever widened (or a third `only(n)` consult is added in `shell_scan` outside the `picks_up` guard), `writes` hands back the unfiltered list for a filtered question: the excluded `moai mv` segment opened `scope.pick`, `gate` swallowed the later `sed -i src/x.rs`, `writes.is_empty()` is true, and rule 2 returns `Pass` on an unheld write. Silent under-blocking, with no compile error and no red test.

7. `src/hook.rs:872` — `Scan::writes`'s `Cow::Owned` arm memoizes nothing, so on the restricted path `settle`'s repeated judging still pays a full walk each time — the exact repetition the new comments claim is now covered. `moai -C <other root> mv X in_progress && sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs` (a shape CLAUDE.md itself prescribes) excludes a pick segment, so every `writes()` call re-runs `shell_scan` and `shell_writes` discards the `.1` picks it just computed. With a blocking decision that is 3 restricted walks + 1 whole walk from `picked_in` = 4, identical to pre-diff. Closing it needs `Scan::new(line, cfg, picks)` plus a second `OnceCell`.

8. `src/cmd/hook.rs:336` — The loop-local `let scan = Scan::new(line, &other.config)` shadows the outer `scan` built from `repo.config`, with the same name and the same type. The compiler cannot tell the two apart, and `cfg` is exactly what decides a pick (`picks_up` reads `cfg.knows(to) && cfg.is_started(to)`). A later edit that deletes the line as redundant, or hoists a `picked_in(&scan, …)` into the loop, silently classifies pick-ups by the wrong tracker's column vocabulary — no compile error, no test. The file argues against precisely this shape elsewhere (the named `Pick`/`Bailout` structs exist because same-typed positions compiled when transposed).

9. `src/hook.rs:825` — The new `Scan` doc adds a broken rustdoc intra-doc link, ``[`crate::cmd::hook::Route::Here`]``, introducing a fresh `broken_intra_doc_links` warning. `cargo doc --no-deps` reports `unresolved link to crate::cmd::hook::Route::Here --> src/hook.rs:825 ... no item named Route in module hook`. `Route` is a private enum in `src/cmd/hook.rs:598`, so the cross-module link never resolves.

10. `Cargo.toml:40` — The `too_many_arguments = "allow"` comment still names `hook.rs`'s `guard_shell_in` as one of the three bought sites, but dropping `cfg` took it from 8 params to 7, below the lint threshold. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -W clippy::too_many_arguments` now reports only `src/cmd/add.rs:325` and `src/cmd/show.rs:390`. The block's own rule is "**어느 자리를 산 allow 인지 적어 둔다**" — a stale third entry is exactly the state that rule exists to prevent.

11. `src/hook.rs:863` — The cache's soundness rests on an unstated coupling: `whole_for`'s index domain matches `shell_scan`'s only because both `only(n)` sites are short-circuited behind `picks_up`, and nothing in either place says so. `shell_scan` walks `line.segs()` with `let n = k; if !seg.words.is_empty() { k += 1; }` (hook.rs:4412), so a word-less segment (`> f`, which still contributes writes) carries the NEXT used segment's index. Reorder those `&&` operands, or add an `only(n)` consult on a redirect-only segment, and `whole_for` validates a domain that excludes the index that actually differs.

12. `src/hook.rs:3609` — `guard_writes_in`'s new comment states the borrow covers `settle`'s three re-judgements unconditionally, which is false whenever `whole_for` is false. It reads as settled fact; on any mixed-route line it is wrong, and the next maintainer stops looking for the repeated walk.

13. `src/cmd/hook.rs:336` — A fresh whole-line scan is built per sibling tracker even when that tracker's config is identical to this one's. `picks_up` reads nothing from `Config` but `knows`/`is_started`, so two repos on the default columns produce an identical `(writes, picks)` pair. `moai -C /a mv x done && moai -C /b mv y done` with both registered pays 3 identical walks. Not a regression (pre-diff cost was the same), but the new comment reads as a closed decision and will stop the next reader from asking.

14. `src/hook.rs:6420` — Block 3's `assert_eq!(scans() - before, 2)` pins the ABSENCE of memoization on the miss path, so fixing that miss path reds a test that says the opposite. Implementing a second `OnceCell` drops the count to 1 and fails this assertion with the message "가려 묻는 판과 안 가린 판이 같은 벌을 봤다" — telling the next author they broke the contract when they honoured it.

15. `src/cmd/hook.rs:335` — The predicate `|k| routes.get(k) == Some(&Route::There(n))` now stands twice, in two loops over the same `there`, and the diff plants the new `Scan` beside the second copy. The copy at :252 decides which segments a foreign tracker JUDGES; the copy at :335 decides which picks are RECORDED against it. Refine one and not the other and a pick is recorded for a tracker that never judged the segment, or dropped. Pre-existing duplication that the diff extends; one shared `fn aimed_at(routes, n)` beside `same()` would bind them.

## What was fixed (working tree)

All fixes verified with `cargo test` (1296 + 485 pass), `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean), `cargo fmt --check` (clean), and `cargo doc` (the new link warning is gone).

- `whole_for` now asks `!picks_up(seg, cfg) || only(k)` per segment instead of `only` at every index. This is the exact guard `shell_scan` uses at its two `only(n)` sites, so it is provably equivalent and strictly weaker — it turns findings 2, 3 and 11 into one change: the memo now hits on `cd /tmp && sed -i …` and `moai -C <other> show && sed -i …`, and `only` is once again consulted only at pick segments, so no `canonicalize` storm.
- Test `one_turn_scans_the_command_line_once`: the laziness probe's two lines swapped (now falsifiable); the first block calls `guard_shell_in` 3x on the same `Scan` and asserts `!said.blocks()`, pinning the `settle` win and proving rule 2 actually ran; a new block pins the tightened predicate; a new loop asserts `Scan::writes(only) == shell_writes(line, cfg, only)` for three predicates.
- Doc fixes: the broken `crate::cmd::hook::Route::Here` link removed, `Scan::writes`/`guard_writes_in` claims qualified to what the code delivers.
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — the loop-local `Scan` renamed `theirs`.
- `Cargo.toml` — the `too_many_arguments` allow no longer lists `guard_shell_in`, and says why it left.

Probes run (not guesses): making `Scan::new` eager reds the first block; reverting `whole_for` to the old body reds the new `집기가 아닌 토막` assertion with `left: 2, right: 1`.

## What was skipped

- Finding 7 (the restricted path memoizes nothing) — the real fix is `Scan::new(line, cfg, picks)` plus a second `OnceCell`, which changes the constructor, `guard_writes_in`'s signature and seven call sites. That is a redesign, not a fix; after the `whole_for` change it only bites when a *pick* segment routes elsewhere. Worth its own issue.
- Findings 13 and 15 — pre-existing costs/duplication the diff extends but does not introduce.
- Finding 14 — block 3's `== 2` is semantically justified today; it should change only together with finding 7.

내가 판단한 것 — 열다섯 중 열하나를 받았다(`810ca1b`).

- 가장 무거운 것은 2·3·11번이다. **갈무리가 규약이 시키는 바로 그 줄에서 한 번도 안 쓰였다.** `whole_for` 가 "토막을 다 고르는가" 로 묻던 판은 `shell_scan` 이 요구하는 것보다 엄해, `cd /tmp && sed -i …` 처럼 집기가 아닌 토막 하나가 딴 자리를 겨누기만 해도 갈무리를 버렸다. 지적을 직접 대조했다 — `shell_scan` 의 `only(n)` 두 자리(4479·4520)는 둘 다 `picks_up(&seg.words, cfg) &&` 뒤에 서고, 낱말 없는 토막은 `picks_up` 이 빈손에 져 애초에 안 묻는다. 그래서 `!picks_up || only` 는 증명 가능하게 같고 더 헐겁다
- 4·5·6번은 시험이 못박는다던 것을 안 못박고 있었다. 셋 다 받았다 — 특히 6번(빌려 준 벌의 **값**을 안 보던 것)이 없으면 `whole_for` 가 넓어지는 날 규칙 2 가 조용히 꺼진다
- 1번(게으름 탐침이 `x - x == 0`)과 8번(고리 안 `Scan` 이 바깥 것을 가린다)과 9·10·12번은 그대로 받았다
- **넘긴 것**: 7번은 idea moai-juwb 에 담았다 — 좁힌 갈래에 갈무리를 더하는 것은 생성자와 부르는 자리 일곱을 바꾸는 일이라 고침이 아니라 다시 짓는 일이다. 14번은 7번과 함께 움직여야 해 같이 두었고, 그 까닭을 idea 에 적었다. 13·15번은 이 diff 가 낸 것이 아니라 잇기만 한 자리다 — 15번(같은 술어가 두 고리에 선다)은 뒤에 실제로 갈릴 수 있는 자리라 `moai-juwb` 본문에 안 적었으니, 다음 사람이 `cmd/hook.rs` 의 두 고리를 볼 때 이 줄을 읽기 바란다
- **판정 표를 다시 떴다.** 188블록이 고치기 전과 md5 까지 같다(0de5cc69fef4d5d5f66ad3bc3aafc7d2). 리뷰가 고친 `whole_for` 가 답을 바꾸지 않았다는 뜻이다
- 시험 1,781 통과, clippy 깨끗, `cargo fmt --check` 깨끗. 바이너리 6,106,872바이트

리뷰가 `whole_for` 를 넓힌 뒤 다시 쟀다. 앞 노트의 표는 그 전 바이너리의 것이다.

두 판을 잰다. 하나는 기계가 한가할 때(부하 10), 하나는 바쁠 때(부하 15). **바쁜 판에서는 잰 값이 ±10% 흔들린다** — 안 바뀌어야 할 `cp` 줄이 그만큼 움직인 것으로 안다.
