text:
리뷰 원문 (/code-review max --fix, agent-a17a0ca5a8d705e13, 영어 원문 그대로)

All 10 angles, the sweep, and the fix pass are complete. Gates: **1368 tests pass, clippy clean, rustfmt clean.**

## Findings

1. src/user_config.rs:1324 — merge_words runs drop_elements BEFORE the push loop, so worded samples the quote model from the post-removal array — a merge that empties the array loses the user's quotes, and in push_word's indent scan the indentation too.
   Failure: Verified end-to-end through merge_look: `hidden = ['todo']` with base [todo]/new [done] -> `hidden = ["done"]`. Two keystrokes reach it: `SPC v a` (View::show_all) clears every column -> `hidden = []` persisted, then hiding one column -> `hidden = ["done"]`. Multi-line is worse: `[\n  'todo',\n  'done'\n]` with base [todo,done]/new [review] -> `[\n"review"\n]` — quotes AND indent gone. The doc frames the empty-array case as 'a file written empty, no model to invent', but here moai emptied it one statement earlier. Fix: sample the model in merge_words before drop_elements and pass it into push_word.

2. src/user_config.rs:1499 — The premise 'Value::from always makes a double-quoted string' is false — toml_writer's as_default falls back to a literal string when the word holds a `"` and no `'` — so one such column name turns a hand-written double-quoted array single-quoted from the next run on.
   Failure: Measured: `Value::from("say \"hi\"")` renders `'say "hi"'`; `Value::from("C:\\work")` renders `'C:\work'`. Status names are unvalidated free text (config.rs:335 splits on `,`, trims, checks nothing else). `hidden = ["todo"]` + that column -> `["todo", 'say "hi"']`; next run worded models that element and every later word is single-quoted: `["todo", 'say "hi"', 'review', 'blocked']`. Before this change the mismatch was one stray element; now it spreads. The rule is one-directional: it forces `'` when the model is literal but never forces `"` when it is basic.

3. src/user_config.rs:1508 — The mirror of the above: a word that cannot be a literal falls back to Value::from, and once that double-quoted element is in the file it becomes the model, so a single-quoted array flips to double quotes permanently.
   Failure: A column named `won't do`: `hidden = ['todo']` -> hide it -> `['todo', "won't do"]` (correct). Unhide todo -> `["won't do"]`. Hide todo again -> `["won't do", "todo"]`. The user's `'todo'` never comes back and every later add is double-quoted. Same root cause as finding 1 — a model captured from the key's pre-merge text would fix both.

4. src/user_config.rs:1495 — Byte-identity regression on a mixed-quote array: a merge that removes one word and adds another used to restore the original bytes on toggle-back and now does not.
   Failure: `hidden = ['a', "b"]`, base [a,b] / new [a,c]. OLD: `['a', "c"]`, toggle back -> `['a', "b"]` = source byte-for-byte. NEW: drop_elements removes `"b"`, worded models the surviving `'a'` -> `['a', 'c']`; toggle back -> `['a', 'b']`, which is not the source — the hand-written `"b"` came back as `'b'`. Same on the multi-line form. This is the moai-n3ku invariant the change is built to protect. (The mirror `["a", 'b']` was already broken before, so the net effect is to move which half of the mixed case loses bytes.)

5. src/user_config.rs:1373 — Incomplete fix: write_value, the sibling scalar path in the same file, still flattens every single-quoted scalar to double quotes when the value changes — same promise, untouched.
   Failure: Measured by running write_value verbatim: `sort = 'title'` -> `sort = "created"`; `timezone = 'Asia/Seoul'  # 내 자리` -> `timezone = "UTC"  # 내 자리` (the comment survives, the quote style does not); `sort = '''title'''` -> `"created"`. It copies the old decor (line 1373) but not the repr, and Value::from carries repr: None. Reachable from set_hue (:777), merge_look (:1129/1132/1133/1147/1150/1153) and read_marks.rs (:1136, :1257). So the byte round-trip now holds per key, not per file: `sort = 'title'` toggled and back leaves `sort = "title"`.

6. src/user_config.rs:1320 — The mechanism only fires for an array that already exists with string elements; a key moai creates goes through write_value and lands double-quoted, and worded then models itself on those elements.
   Failure: A hand-written `[tui]` with `hidden = ['todo']` and no `fields_known`: `known |= !t.contains_key(FIELDS_KNOWN)` forces the write, merge_words line 1320 sees no array and calls write_value with a fresh Array -> `fields_known = ["id", …]` in double quotes beside the user's single-quoted line. fields_known is tool-authored, so worded will essentially never find a model for it.

7. src/user_config.rs:1489 — FIXED. The doc said a non-string element yields double quotes; `_ => None` makes find_map skip it and keep scanning backwards.
   Failure: Verified: `hidden = ['todo', 42]` + `done` -> `['todo', 42, 'done']`, not `"done"`. Only an array with no string element at all (`[42]`) matches the old comment. In a repo where the doc comment is the contract, the next reader sizes a change against a rule the code does not implement.

8. src/user_config.rs:1490 — FIXED. The advertised 'chained model' (the word just added becomes the model for the next) has no observable effect and contradicts worded's own stated rule.
   Failure: A pushed element can never move the answer: the literal path's Repr is `'w'` and reports the same literalness, and the Value::from path has repr None and is skipped. Proven by capping the scan at the pre-merge length — 0 of 11 cases can tell the two apart. The test comment at 2618 labelled an assertion with a guard it does not provide. The *skip* half of the walk IS observable and is now pinned by a new assertion.

9. src/user_config.rs:1495 — FIXED (doc). The headline 'follows the last element's quotes' is not the rule — it follows the last element that carries a Repr, so the same two adds give different bytes in one merge versus two.
   Failure: `hidden = ['todo']`, add `it's` then `done` in ONE merge -> `['todo', "it's", 'done']`; the same two adds in TWO merges (file written and re-read between) -> `['todo', "it's", "done"]`, because after the reparse `"it's"` has a repr and becomes the model. Also unstated: push_word's indent model is 'the last element that opens a line' and counts session-pushed elements, so the two scans in one function pick different models.

10. src/user_config.rs:1448 — FIXED. push_word's pre-existing paragraph still claimed a one-line push emits toml_edit's default shape `, "새것"`, which the repr no longer follows.
    Failure: After the change only the DECOR is toml_edit's default; the repr is whatever worded picked. The diff added a new paragraph below but left the older sentence and its `"새것"` example standing, so two paragraphs of the same doc block disagreed about what a one-line push emits.

11. src/user_config.rs:1493 — FIXED. The worked example justifying the round-trip guard was off by two quotes: `''` wraps to `''''`, which is a parse error, not a multi-line empty string.
    Failure: Measured: `''''` -> Err; `''''''` -> Ok with as_str() == Some(""). The word that actually produces the six-quote hazard is `''''`. The guard is right; only the sentence naming the hazard was wrong, and it is the only place the hazard is written down.

12. src/user_config.rs:2666 — FIXED (comment). The two rows added to the round-trip test do not discriminate, and their comment claimed a guard they do not provide.
    Failure: Proven by disabling worded and re-running: adding_a_word_and_dropping_it_again_restores_the_bytes still passes, only an_added_word_follows_the_quotes_of_the_last_one goes red. Every row in that table adds then removes the SAME word, so the model never moves; the comment '따옴표가 어긋나면 뺀 자리가 원문과 달라진다' is false — a flipped quote still round-trips.

13. src/user_config.rs:1505 — FIXED. `v.decor_mut().clear()` was dead code and its comment implied it was load-bearing.
    Failure: toml_edit 0.25.15 src/value.rs:249-253 does `value.decor_mut().clear(); value.despan(s);` under the comment 'Only take the repr and not decor, as its probably not intended'. Measured: `"'x'".parse::<Value>()` returns prefix=None suffix=None. The call could never change an outcome, and the match arm existed only to hold it.

14. src/user_config.rs:1495 — FIXED. `words.get(i).expect("차례 안이다")` is the one construct in the new code that can panic, and `?` says the same thing for free.
    Failure: toml_edit's Array::len() doc: 'In some rare cases, placeholder elements will exist', while get() is `values.get(i).and_then(Item::as_value)`. Unreachable today (nothing in the repo calls ArrayOfTables::into_array or Table::into_inline_table), but a placeholder would turn a cosmetic quote-matching helper into a panic that aborts the whole config write. `?` falls through to the previous element — the same skip the doc already describes.

15. src/user_config.rs:1502 — The literal path writes control and invisible characters raw where the old path escaped them, so a value that used to be self-describing in the file is now invisible.
    Failure: Measured: `worded("a\tb")` -> `'a<RAW TAB>b'` where the old path wrote `"a\tb"`; `" lead"` -> `' lead'`; U+200B and U+2028 go in raw. All are spec-legal and all re-parse to the same word, so nothing is lost — but editor trim-trailing-whitespace tooling can now silently change a config value the escaped form was immune to.

Two more that did not make the cut: separator spacing is still not copied (`['a','b']` -> `['a','b', 'c']`, and `[ 'a' ]` -> `[ 'a' , 'b']` — pre-existing, now documented), and `꼴(Repr)` put the code name inside the parentheses, which `docs/korean-terms.md` §4 reserves for the reverse order (fixed in the rewrite).

## What I fixed

All in `src/user_config.rs`, +45/-19 on top of the reviewed commit:

- **`worded` doc block rewritten** to say what the code does: the model is the last string element *with a `Repr`*; non-strings are skipped, not stopped at; several words in one merge cannot move the answer; the rule pushes one way only and `Value::from` is not always double-quoted; and the model is read *after* `drop_elements`. Fixed the `''` -> `''''` example.
- **`v.decor_mut().clear()` removed** (`Value::from_str` already clears the decor — confirmed in the vendored source and measured), collapsing the arm to `Ok(v) if v.as_str() == Some(word) => v`.
- **`.expect("차례 안이다")` -> `?`**, deleting the only panic path in the new code.
- **`push_word`'s stale paragraph** corrected, plus one line naming the non-goal (spacing is not copied).
- **Two new assertions** pinning the reverse walk, which nothing covered: skipping a session-pushed `Value::from` element and skipping a non-string element. Verified they are real coverage — capping the scan at the last element turns the test red.
- **The misleading round-trip comment** replaced with what those rows actually guard (`drop_elements` matches by `as_str()`, so quote style does not matter there).

## What I did not fix, and why

Findings 1-6 are behaviour changes outside the reviewed hunk, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that "범위를 넘어서 고치는 것이 범위를 못 채우는 것보다 나쁘다". They want their own issues:

- **Sampling the model before `drop_elements`** (findings 1, 3, 4) — the single highest-value follow-up; changes `merge_words` and `push_word`'s signature. Note it cannot fix the across-two-merges variant (`[\n]` persisted to disk, then re-added), where nothing in-process has a model left.
- **Making the rule two-directional** (finding 2) — needs a hand-built basic-string repr, since `set_repr_unchecked` is `pub(crate)`. The existing `as_str() == Some(word)` guard would make it safe.
- **Extending quote preservation to `write_value`** (findings 5, 6) — the larger half of the same promise, and it reaches `read_marks.rs` too.

Reachability for 2 and 3 is real but narrow: `hidden` holds status column names, and `config.rs:335` validates nothing about their characters.

## Applied (`--fix`)

All fifteen above are fixed in `src/hook.rs` (324 insertions, 69 deletions, one file). `cargo test` 1373 + 489 pass, `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean. Each fix carries a Korean comment naming what was measured, and I added test cases to the existing `guard_writes` Pass/Deny lists, `parallel_and_strace_are_measured_not_guessed`, `three_more_wrappers_hand_a_string_to_a_shell` and `a_handed_string_reaches_its_positional_arguments` (no test was removed or weakened).

Two fixes were slightly wider than the one line: `Lexer::push` now carries the watermark forward on a `hung` segment (finding 2), and `spread` was reshaped to return a bool so the "give the characters back verbatim" path lives at one call site. Cleanup items from the reuse/efficiency angles were folded in where they touched the same lines (`vals.to_vec()`, `v.clone()`, the `Vec<char>` in `${...}`, deferring the `Handed::args` clone into the `Text::Line` arm, `parallel`'s `appends` field made truthful).

## Skipped, with reasons

- **`su -x <user> -c '<text>'` fabricates a pick-up** (`src/hook.rs:4100`). `weird` is gated on `alien`, which needs `-s <non-shell>`; the shell branch is still open, so an invalid `su` line credits a pick that never runs. The honest fix is a new `Wrapper` field ("this row's short-option table is complete", true for `su`/`runuser` only) - a design decision the author should own, and the existing comment already argues against widening the criterion without one.
- **`find -execdir`/`-okdir` should set `*spot`** (`src/hook.rs:3709`). I applied it and reverted: it makes `a_command_inside_a_find_predicate_is_a_command` red, because `elsewhere` closes the whole moai axis and `find . -execdir moai add x \;` then stops tripping rule 1. Which axis to close is a call for the author; the code now carries a comment saying so. Today `find /tmp -execdir tee src/store.rs \;` is falsely denied.
- **`find -fprint`/`-fprintf`/`-fls`** really truncate their file operand and are invisible (pre-existing, not a regression - `find` was never a write-command head).
- **`flock FILE -n -c '<text>'`** is falsely denied: real flock only accepts `-c` as the word immediately after the lock file (measured: `failed to execute -n`). Fixing it needs an "index right after the operands" check in the generic loop, i.e. the same per-wrapper field finding 8's fix wants.
- **`parallel -l N` / `--max-lines N`** still hides the write. `max-lines|maxlines|l:f` eats the next word only when it is numeric, and the table has no way to say that; I left both spellings as valueless flags (which is strictly better than the previous `Stops`) and documented the residual in place.
- **`runuser -u <user> -c '<text>' A B`** yields empty `Handed::args` because `saw` breaks the operand loop - a gap, not a leak, documented at the call site.
- **`hard_exit` rejects `exit 0x10` / `exit ' 5'`** - over-blocks only, and making non-numeric arguments "hard" would wrongly harden `exit "$n"`.
- **Perf**: a `parallel` line now costs ~600-1000 string comparisons (vs ~35 for `xargs`) through linear `.contains()` over 110 `long` + 150 `free` entries, all of which are already sorted. `binary_search` plus a short/long split in `letter()` would cut it ~10x. Zero cost on non-`parallel` lines, and the added tables are ~12 KB against a 7.7 MB binary-size headroom, so no budget is at risk.
- **Structural cleanups** left for the author: five near-identical `Handed` literals in `handed_text`, `Wrapped::Hands { args: Vec::new() }` at seven sites with a destructure-and-rebuild at the eighth, the `hands` gate written in two spellings, `su`/`runuser`'s byte-identical `free` arrays, and `exec_of`'s requote-and-join being a third copy of the `Text::Words` expression. `parallel`'s `free` also still lists `--help`/`--version`/`-V`/`-h`, which `PRINTS` shadows on both paths (dead today, a trap if those checks are ever reordered).

Max-effort review of `develop...HEAD` (`b1344ed`, `b85c3fe`) — milestone `starts_on`/`due_on` calendar dates, board deadline warnings, the two-milestone notice, and the `Spent` rollup on `moai show <milestone>`. 10 finder angles + verification + a gap sweep; every finding below was reproduced live against the built binary.

**Final state: `cargo test` → 1370 + 499 pass, 0 fail. No compiler warnings. `cargo fmt --check` clean for every touched file** (the only remaining fmt diffs are pre-existing in `src/guide.rs`/`src/hook.rs`, untouched). `moai init --check` says the AGENTS block is current. 12 files changed, +336/−83.

## Findings

1. **`src/report.rs:1181`** — spent_on sums a parent issue and its children separately, so overlapping wall clock is counted twice.
   `is_work` only excludes epics, but a child (`<id>.r3q`) is also Kind::Issue and inherits the milestone through its parent. Reproduced: parent + review child both in_progress 05:00 -> done 06:00 gives `Spent 2h`, `{closed:2, minutes:120}` for 60 real minutes. AGENTS.md hook rule 3 files every review as a `--parent` child, so this is the common case.

2. **`src/model.rs:1148`** — parse_date's byte guard allows '-' at any position, so a negative year passes the strict validator.
   `!b.iter().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || *c == b'-')` lets "-026" reach i64::from_str. Reproduced: `moai edit <m> --due=-026-09-20` exits 0, writes `"due_on":"-026-09-20"`, and the board prints `! 1 milestones are past their deadline` with `(749469 days past)` forever.

3. **`src/model.rs:1176`** — days_until compares a calendar deadline against the UTC day while the same screen renders every other stamp in the viewer's timezone.
   Reproduced with TZ=Asia/Seoul, MOAI_NOW=2026-09-11T20:00:00Z (local 2026-09-12 05:00): a milestone due 2026-09-11 prints `(due today)` and files under due-soon although the deadline passed yesterday locally, while `Created` on the same screen prints in KST. Mirror-image west of UTC. Every 00:00-09:00 KST session is a day behind.

4. **`src/model.rs:566`** — validate_fields checks both date fields on every write, so a hand-merged bad due_on seals the row, and the refusal never names the way out.
   Reproduced: a milestone row carrying `"due_on":"2026-9-20"` refuses both `moai edit <id> --title x` and `moai defer <id>` with the format complaint and nothing else. `moai edit <id> --due none` works, but nothing on screen says so — CLAUDE.md's "되돌릴 방법이 도구 밖에만 남는다".

5. **`i18n/en.json:87`** — warn.milestones_running hardcodes "Two" but the trigger is `running.len() >= 2`.
   Reproduced with three running milestones: the board prints `+ Two milestones are running at once` and lists three ids under it; --json carries `count: 3`. `says` routes it through `one()`, which fills `{n}`, but neither en nor ko string contains `{n}`. The existing test only stands up two.

6. **`src/model.rs:570`** — Invalid::DateNotMilestone and Invalid::Date bake self.id into the message, so a create-time refusal hands back a command naming a row that was never written.
   Reproduced: `moai add 'just an issue' --due 2026-09-20` prints ``Clear it with `moai edit probe6-95al --due none` `` and leaves issues.jsonl empty; so does `moai add 'v9' --type milestone --due 2026-02-30`. store.rs:773 already picks At::Unwritten for the prefix precisely because of moai-1rkl; the id in the body bypasses it. The sibling invalid.milestone_in_milestone hedges with a create-time branch; both new messages dropped it.

7. **`src/cli.rs:839`** — `--from` does not conflict with the new `--start`/`--due`, and `bulk` never forwards them, so a plan silently discards both dates.
   Reproduced: `moai add --from - --due 2026-09-20 --start 2026-09-01` exits 0, creates the epic and its issue, and both dates are gone with no word. A plan cannot create a milestone at all (`refuse.plan_has_no_milestone`), so the flags can never be meaningful there — the same shape `--var`/`--dry-run` are explicitly refused for.

8. **`src/report.rs:3598`** — Overdue/due-soon ids are pushed in file (id) order while view::preview shows only the first three, so the most urgent milestone is the one folded away.
   Reproduced with five overdue milestones: the board showed 2-days-past, 102-days-past and 4-days-past, then `2 more` — the 253-days-past one was hidden. Every other warning in status_in builds ids through `ids_of`, whose doc says the order decides what is seen.

9. **`src/report.rs:3593`** — Warning.ages is given days-past and days-remaining as two positive magnitudes, so the JSON value means opposite things depending on kind.
   `overdue.push((m, -d))` plus `soon.push((m, d))` yields `ages: {id: 2}` for both "2 days late" and "2 days early"; view::preview re-derives the sign with `match w.kind`. The field's doc (report.rs:2891) says it is an age and enumerates four other kinds, and the neighbouring `oldest` doc forbids exactly this.

10. **`src/config.rs:602`** — status_due_days is read from config but exercised by no test, so its config read can be deleted and the whole suite stays green.
    `every_threshold_can_be_set` still says "여덟 키" and omits status_due_days; grep finds it nowhere in tests/. Changing config.rs:280 to `due_days: d.due_days` left all 498 tests passing — a repo writing `status_due_days = 10` would get no error (the key is in KEYS, so no NoSuchThreshold) and the board would silently keep warning at 3. That test exists to catch exactly this.

11. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:348`** — The merge driver runs validate_fields on rows neither side touched, so one row carrying a date the new rules reject makes every tracker merge conflict forever.
    by_issue walks the union of all ids and an identical-on-both-sides row still goes through `keep` -> `issue()` -> `validate_fields().ok()?` -> None -> conflict markers. A row with due_on on a non-milestone (hand-resolved conflict, or a future binary that extends dates to epics) makes .moai/issues.jsonl conflict on every merge until someone destroys the value. The mechanism pre-dates this diff; the diff widens the set of rows that trip it.

12. **`src/model.rs:1146`** — parse_date range-checks month and day but never the year, and far_ahead does not cover the new fields, so an implausible-but-well-formed date is accepted and never flagged.
    Reproduced: `moai edit <m> --due 0026-09-20` exits 0 and the board prints `(730476 days past)` permanently; `--due 9999-12-31` gives `(2912189 days left)`. No hyphen trick needed — `0026` for `2026` is the likelier typo. report.rs's far_ahead (moai-ugjp) warns about implausible created_at/started_at/done_at but was not extended to due_on/starts_on.

13. **`src/tui/draw.rs:2313`** — The explorer's detail pane builds its own field list and never gained the Due or Spent lines, so a mistyped date is invisible on the browsing surface.
    tui::draw::about mirrors view::detail field by field and carries the comment "CLI 상세와 같은 자를 쓴다"; started_at/done_at were added there for exactly this reason (moai-38mh). due_on/starts_on/spent appear nowhere under src/tui/. `moai edit <m> --due 2025-09-20` shows one warning line on the board and nothing at all in the explorer.

14. **`CHANGELOG.md:70`** — The epic's four CHANGELOG bullets landed under the already-released `## [0.1.1] - 2026-09-22` section instead of [Unreleased].
    The develop merge brought in 0.1.1's release cut, which renamed the heading around these lines. src/guide.rs:2219 states the consequence — the release workflow cuts a section by version name and hands it to --notes-file as it is, so these four features would never appear in any release's notes.

15. **`src/view.rs:1951`** — view::minutes drops the remainder once past an hour, so the human line and --json disagree by up to 59 minutes on the same value.
    Reproduced: a member spanning 05:00->06:59 renders `Spent 1h  (wall clock over 1 of 1 closed, median 1h)` while show --json reports `"minutes":119`. The doc justifies flooring rather than rounding, which is right, but flooring to a bare hour throws the remainder away. There is also no day unit, so a 30-day milestone prints `720h`.

Three more that did not fit the cap: `status_due_days` missing from `moai status --help` (and therefore from the generated `docs/cli.md` — CONTRIBUTING.md: "a reference that has drifted is worse than none at all"); `status_due_days = 0` renders the self-contradicting "1 milestones fall due within 0 days" and does *not* silence the pre-warning, where `flow_days` has an explicit zero guard; and `view::spent`'s `detail.spent_none` branch was exercised by no test at all.

## Fixes applied (`--fix`)

Eleven findings plus seven smaller items:

- **child double-count** — `spent_on` split into a `#[cfg(test)]` short form plus `report::spent_in(members)`. **The first version of this fix was wrong and the gap sweep caught it**: a blanket skip of any child whose parent is a member threw away a measured child whenever the parent had no span. Reproduced: parent still `in_progress` + a 60-minute closed review child gave `{closed:0, measured:0, minutes:0}` and *no Spent line*, next to `Members 1/2`; and a parent closed by an older binary gave `Members 2/2` beside "none of the 1 closed carry a start and a finish" — both halves false. The rule now is: `closed` counts every done work member (so it matches the `Members` bar), and a span is folded **only when the parent's span was actually counted**. Members are walked in id order so ancestors decide before descendants.
- **parse_date sign hole** — positional byte guard (`matches!(x, 4|7) ? '-' : ascii digit`).
- **both refusal messages** — `Invalid::Date` gained an `id`; both now mirror `invalid.milestone_in_milestone`'s two-branch shape, create-time clause first.
- **"Two milestones"** — both strings carry `{n}`.
- **`--from`** — `start`/`due` added to `conflicts_with_all`; now a clap error instead of a silent drop.
- **signed `ages`** — the report stores `days_until`'s own sign; `view::preview` reads it straight, with no `match w.kind` and no `unwrap_or(0)` (which rendered "due today" under an overdue heading).
- **ordering** — both lists sort by urgency, tie-broken by id.
- **`status_due_days` untested** — added to both threshold tests, plus an assertion that the test's TOML block and `Thresholds::KEYS` stay the same length so the next added key cannot slip through the same way.
- **CHANGELOG** — bullets moved to `[Unreleased]`; the "two milestones" and "no timezone can move them" claims reworded.
- **help/docs** — `status_due_days` added to `status --help`, `docs/cli.md` regenerated via `scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh` (+1 line).
- Also: the duplicated `// 6-2.`/`// 6-3.` section numbers (they collided with the idea-pile and deferred blocks and broke the cross-reference at report.rs:3492) renumbered 6-5/6-6; `view::spent`'s `sp.median?` — invisible control flow that would silently drop the line — replaced with one `let … else`, and the `spent_none` branch now has a test; a dead `ids.sort()` on an already-ordered BTreeMap source dropped; a `sort_by_key` cloning an id per comparison changed to a borrowed compare; the `cmd/add.rs` comment crediting `store::admit` with validation it deliberately no longer does (moai-yve0) corrected; `cmd/show.rs` hoists `group_members` once per branch so a milestone detail builds the belonging maps once instead of twice.

**Every fix was verified to bite.** Reverting the fold turns the unit test red with the double-counted `Spent`; reverting the ancestor ordering turns it red with a `p0` child counted ahead of its parent (that case was *not* covered until I added it — removing the sort left the suite green, so I wrote the fixture that catches it).

## Skipped, with reasons

- **timezone skew** — needs a `Zone` threaded into `report::status_in`, a pure `&[Issue]` function by design, or a new `model::today()` deciding the question once. Fixing only the display side would split the verdict from what the board shows.
- **merge driver** — pre-existing mechanism outside the diff; the diff only widens which rows trip it.
- **implausible year** — `0026-09-20` is well-formed; the project's precedent for implausible dates is `far_ahead`'s *warning*, not a write refusal. Extending `far_ahead` to `due_on`/`starts_on` is the author's call.
- **TUI** — `tui::draw::about` builds its own field list; two more rows there is a layout decision with its own tests.
- **minutes flooring** — the doc explicitly chooses to floor; `1h 59m` needs new i18n keys and changes intended output.
- **`status_due_days = 0`** — refusing 0 or giving it its own word is a product decision.
- The AGENTS block (`src/guide.rs:590`) hardcodes "within three days" while the threshold is configurable and the board line interpolates `{d}`; rewording it cascades into regenerating AGENTS.md and re-blessing the plugin content hash, so I left it.

## One thing to know about the patch

`spent_in` now walks members in **id order** to guarantee ancestors decide before descendants. That relies on a child id being its parent's id plus `.suffix`, which `crate::id::parent_of` already assumes. If ids ever stop nesting that way, this fold and `parent_of` break together.

Review complete. Scope: `git diff develop...HEAD` — one commit, `b72c867 fix(release): 태그 판은 캐시를 안 쓴다 (moai-ik77)`, touching only `.github/workflows/release.yml` (17+/48-). Working tree was clean at start.

**Findings (1)**

- `.github/workflows/release.yml:89` — low: the new comment justifies leaving the other workflows' caches alone with "그쪽은 PR 과 `develop` 에서 돌아 열쇠가 맞는다", but `smoke.yml` (its `on:` block, lines 8-14) has neither a `pull_request` trigger nor a `push: branches: [develop]` — it runs on `schedule`, tag pushes and `workflow_dispatch` only. Its `cargo-smoke-*` / `rustup-*` keys land on the default branch solely because scheduled runs execute there. Concrete scenario: someone later drops the nightly cron (or narrows `smoke.yml` to tags, the way `release.yml` already is) while trusting this comment, and `smoke.yml` silently becomes the exact dead save-never-restore cache this commit just removed — hundreds of MB written per tag into a repository cache already at 4.17GB/10GB, where LRU evicts the `cargo-dev` entry PRs actually use.

**Verified clean (no findings)**

- No leftover references to the removed steps: `steps.toolchain`, `actions/cache`, `cargo-rel-*` and `rustup-<target>` appear nowhere else in `release.yml`, and the removed `박아 둔 판을 읽는다` step's output had no other consumer.
- The removal is step-local: `rustup target add`, `musl-tools`, `build`, `check-size.sh`, `pack` and `upload-artifact` all stand on their own; the `release` job (`needs: build`) is untouched.
- The build matrix lines (`- target:`) are unchanged, so `tests/cli.rs::release_matrix()` and `the_install_table_and_the_release_matrix_name_the_same_targets` still parse it — ran that test, passes.
- `CHANGELOG.md:199` (the earlier "restored its cache after `rustup target add`" entry) sits in the shipped `[0.1.1]` section, not `[Unreleased]`, so it is correct history and not made stale by this removal.
- The measured numbers in the comment are consistent with the epic body on `moai-0s1h`; the 40-minute job timeout is far above the cold build times (92s musl / 122s darwin).

**Observation (not fixed, not a finding)**

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:98` points at "`release.yml` 의 `rustup target add` 가 그랬던 자리다" — a reader following that pointer now finds no cache in `release.yml` at all. It is worded in the past tense so it still reads as history; I left it alone rather than edit a file outside this diff that sibling worktrees may hold.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` entry was added. I judged that correct: this is CI-internal with no user-visible effect, and the `[Unreleased]` `Fixed` section carries user-facing items only.

**Fix applied** (working tree, uncommitted — `.github/workflows/release.yml`, +6/-2): rewrote the closing paragraph so it names each workflow's real trigger — `ci.yml` via PR and `develop` push, `smoke.yml` via the nightly `schedule` running on the default branch — and states outright that dropping that nightly run would turn `smoke.yml`'s cache into the same dead slot. Nothing else was changed; no behavioral edit was needed anywhere in the diff.

리뷰 원문 (/code-review high --fix, agent-ab201249c8cd0fee2):

## Scope

`git diff develop...HEAD` — one commit, `45b2204 feat(i18n): fill 이 안 채운 자리를 dev 빌드에서 잡는다 (moai-gw8r)`, touching only `src/i18n.rs` (+94/−9). Working tree was clean at review start.

## Verification done

- `cargo test` (dev): 1380 + 499 pass, 0 fail. `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean.
- **Wrote a static cross-check of every `fill(say(lang,"key"), &[…])` call site in `src/` against `i18n/en.json`** — 390 sites checked. Exactly one mismatch, and it is the benign direction (extra vars), so the new `debug_assert` has **no false-positive risk** on any current call site.
- Checked the variable-text call sites the static pass could not resolve (`view.rs:234/839/840/2463/3032`, `cmd/add.rs:75`) by hand — every branch's key carries exactly the slots the helper fills (`one()` → `{n}`, `aged()` → `{n}`+`{d}`, etc.).
- Grepped all five bundles for non-placeholder braces (`{}`, `{ }`, JSON/jq examples): none — so no table string can trip the assert.
- `Cargo.toml` `[profile.release]` does not set `debug-assertions`, so the doc's claim that release keeps the old behaviour holds.
- `scan()` is byte-for-byte equivalent to the old inline loop (unclosed `{`, `}` before `{`, multi-byte, filled values not rescanned) — no behaviour change in release.

## Findings (2, both low)

- `src/i18n.rs:107` — **low.** `fill`'s public doc says "안 채우는 것이 답인 자리는 `fill_lax` 를 부른다", but `fill_lax` was written as a module-private `fn`. No module outside `i18n` can take the escape hatch the public doc offers: the day a call site needs a two-stage fill (fill `{said}` now, `{n}` later — the shape `warn.carried_where` already composes by hand), the only reachable path is `fill`, which panics in dev/test builds. **Fixed** — `pub(crate) fn fill_lax`, with a comment on why the visibility is load-bearing.
- `src/tui/draw.rs:262` — **low, pre-existing, not fixed.** `fill(say(lang,"tui.prompt.hang"), &[("apply", …), ("cancel", …)])` — `tui.prompt.hang` is the bare word `"apply"`/`"걸기"` with no slots, so the `fill` is a total no-op and both key labels are discarded; the result is identical to `prompt_help(say(lang,"tui.prompt.hang"), lang)` on line 228. Output is unaffected today, but it is dead code that reads as if it did something. Note it is also the one direction the new checker cannot see: a var name the text does not use is dropped silently. **I did not add a reverse assert** — `view::says`' `one()` helper deliberately passes `("n", …)` to slot-less keys (`warn.agents_stale`, `warn.merge_driver_*`), so an extra-vars assert would fire on intentional code; the one-directional check is a design choice, not a defect. **Not fixed** because `src/tui/draw.rs` is outside the reviewed diff and CLAUDE.md is explicit that overstepping scope is worse than under-filling it — worth an `idea` if you want it cleaned.

## Applied

`src/i18n.rs` only, +5/−1: `fn fill_lax` → `pub(crate) fn fill_lax` plus a three-line rationale. Tests and clippy re-run green after the change.

No correctness bugs found in the diff itself.

Separately, `docs/korean-terms.md` §2 says `판`(회차) -> `번/때/회차/경우/벌`; report.rs:6151, report.rs:6175 and mod.rs:1462 are new lines using it. Left to the author — rewriting Korean prose is churn a review should not force."


## What was fixed

All five correctness findings, in the working tree (1,382 unit + 500 integration tests green; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean):

1. **`recount()` no longer clobbers what `overlaid` added.** Added `Site::stranded` / `Fresh::stranded` (the stranded-workplace count, which `report` cannot produce because it reads the disk); `recount()` now re-adds it plus the install count already held in `Site::install`. `src/tui/mod.rs`.
2. **The TUI deadline word moved in front of the dates** (`src/tui/draw.rs`), matching the deferred-blocker precedent, since `field()` clips from the right.
3. **`set_zone` (`SPC o t`) now recounts** (`src/tui/zones.rs`) — safe only because of fix 1.
4. **The outside-a-repo layer sweep gets the real zone**: new `App::on_projects_in(layer, zone)`, with `on_projects` kept as the `#[cfg(test)]` short path (`src/tui/layer.rs`, `src/cmd/tui.rs`).
5. **`moved` compares clocks, not names**: new `Zone::same_clock` (`src/tz.rs`).

Plus three cleanups: the five-line comment duplicated verbatim between `App::build` and `recount()` is gone; `rollup()` skips the per-frame `spent_in` allocation+sort when `done == 0` and stops indexing `site.issues` unguarded; `view::spent` builds its label after the `?`.

**Three regression tests added, two of them proven to fail on the pre-fix code:** `adopting_a_timezone_keeps_what_the_opening_read_added` (reports `(0,0)` instead of `(0,2)` without fix 1), a narrow-window assertion in `detail_draws_the_deadline_and_what_the_milestone_spent` (the word vanishes at 80 columns without fix 2), and a negative-offset case in `a_deadline_line_counts_from_the_reader_s_day` — no existing test exercised `format_rfc3339`'s day-rewind branch.

## Verified clean (worth knowing)

Both `days_until` call sites were updated — nothing was missed. The board's milestone preview reads `w.ages` rather than re-measuring, so it follows automatically. `ready`, `show --json` and the TUI list carry no day math. `zone.shift` is correctly hoisted out of the milestone loop and is never in a per-row path. `Ctx::zone` is a `OnceLock`, so repeated calls are free.

text:
Review of `worktree-moai-514e` (commits `2dfff61` moai-hktu + `a4b4472` moai-phhz, `src/hook.rs` only, +226/-20). Max effort: 10 finder angles + a gap sweep, every claim checked against the real binaries on this machine (coreutils 9.4, util-linux 2.39.3, findutils 4.9.0) and every applied fix proven by flipping the code and watching the suite go red.

Final state: **1380 tests pass, `cargo fmt --check` clean, clippy 0 warnings.** Working tree is +168/-15 on `src/hook.rs`, uncommitted.

## Findings

1. **`*spot` was set for the whole find line**, but `exec_of` folds every predicate into ONE text carrying ONE `elsewhere` bit — so one `-execdir` also threw away a plain `-exec` command, which really does run in the invocation directory. `find . -execdir true \; -exec sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs \;` really rewrites <repo>/src/x.rs, but spot=true -> Cmd::elsewhere -> Layer::Shell{elsewhere:true} -> off_site drops the relative path -> Pass with nothing picked up (rule 2 bypassed). Rule 1 leaks identically with `-exec moai add …`. PROVEN: adding that string to the Deny list made the suite red before the fix. FIXED — the flag now needs `-execdir`/`-okdir` AND no `-exec`/`-ok` on the line.

2. **The same `any()` matched `-execdir`/`-okdir` anywhere in argv**, including where the word is data rather than a predicate — appending one word to any find line turned off the relative-write axis and the whole moai axis. `find . -exec sed -i s/a/b/ src/store.rs \; -name -execdir` — `-execdir` is only `-name`'s pattern; the only running predicate is `-exec`, which truncates <repo>/src/store.rs from the invocation dir. spot=true -> Pass. The same one-word trick hides rule 1 on any find line. FIXED by the same guard.

3. **`-execdir`/`-okdir` run in the directory CONTAINING each match**, so whenever a match sits at depth 0 of the starting point they run in the calling directory — the decided Pass is therefore the common case, not the `/tmp` edge case the comment justifies it with. MEASURED 2026-09-23 in a scratch dir: `find . -maxdepth 1 -name Cargo.toml -execdir tee src/store.rs \;` created ./src/store.rs, and `-execdir pwd \;` printed the starting directory. So `find . -execdir sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs \;` edits the repo with nothing picked up, and `find . -execdir moai add '딴 일' \;` creates outside the held epic. NOT FIXED by the reviewer — this was the 2026-09-23 user decision (moai-hktu). The comment now states the approximation honestly and names the rule that would close it without reopening the false block: key `*spot` on the STARTING POINT (is the first operand under this repo?), not on the predicate.

4. **`--<name>=<value>` was skipped without recording that the table does not know the name**, so on a `whole: true` row an option the real program refuses still credited a pick-up — the exact hole `whole` was added to close, in the other spelling of the same option. Measured: `su --zzz=1 nobody -c 'echo RAN'` -> `unrecognized option '--zzz=1'`, nothing runs. Before the fix `su --zzz=1 남 -c 'moai mv t-1 in_progress --from todo' && sed -i s/a/b/ src/store.rs` returned Pass — the hook read the `-c` text, counted a pick-up that never happened and released the empty-handed write. The bare `--zzz` spelling already returned Stops, so two spellings of one option gave opposite answers. FIXED.

5. **`COMMON` (`--debug`, `--verbose`) and the `--<digits>` escape** are "accept although the row does not list it" fallbacks; they stayed in force on `whole: true` rows, contradicting the claim that those rows' tables are complete. Measured: `su --verbose nobody -c 'echo RAN'` -> `unrecognized option '--verbose'`. Before the fix the same pick-up-then-write line returned Pass. FIXED.

6. **A `whole: true` row has to model getopt_long ABBREVIATION** or `Stops` hides a line that really runs — and on a `whole` row a false `weird` is a leak, not a block, because `Stops` means the `-c` text is never handed to any rule. Measured: `su --sh=/bin/bash nobody -c 'echo RAN'`, `su --whit=FOO …`, `su --gro=root …` all get past getopt (they reach the password prompt), while `su --s=/bin/bash` -> `is ambiguous`, nothing runs. This bit the reviewer's OWN first fix for finding 4: exact-name matching turned `su --sh=/bin/bash 남 -c 'sed -i …'` from Deny into Pass. FIXED — the check now matches unambiguous prefixes over the row's FULL long vocabulary (`long`+`free`+`stops`+`elsewhere`+`chdir`+`hands`+`shell`+PRINTS), compares NAMES not occurrences (`--shell` stands in two columns and double-counting made it look ambiguous), and keeps `weird` for genuinely ambiguous prefixes. Three regression rows added; verified red without the fix.

7. **The `elsewhere` (and `stops`) arms accept an `=`-glued value** on both the long and the short spelling, which the real program refuses — the one `=` door on a `whole` row that the new `weird` line does not close. Measured: `su --login=1 nobody -c 'echo RAN'` -> `option '--login' doesn't allow an argument`; `su -l=x …` -> `invalid option -- '='`. Nothing runs either way, yet the hook takes the `elsewhere` branch, sets `*spot`, and goes on to read the `-c` text — so a rule-4 line is denied for a line that does nothing, and the pick-up twin credits a pick-up that never ran. The sibling `chdir` glued arm already guards the short form with `.filter(|f| f.starts_with("--"))`; `elsewhere` and `stops` do not. NOT FIXED — pre-existing arms the diff did not touch.

8. **`saw` and `prog` compare long option names EXACTLY**, so an abbreviated `--user=`/`--shell=` is not recognised as the switch that decides the command position or names the target program. Measured: `runuser --us=nobody -- /bin/echo RAN` is accepted by getopt (it reaches the root check). But `saw` never fires, so `runuser --us=남 -- sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs` is not read as a command and the real write is invisible — Pass with nothing picked up. `prog` has the same gap: `su --sh=/bin/echo -c '<text>'` hands the text to /bin/echo, but `alien` stays false and the hook reads it as a shell command. NOT FIXED — this touches how the command position is found.

9. **The diff's new test asserts the hook reads `runuser -u 남 -c '<text>'` as a running command**, but real runuser refuses `-u` together with `-c`. The row is keyed on letters alone; nothing models mutually exclusive switches, so `whole: true` claims more than the table can deliver. Measured: `runuser -u nobody -c 'echo RAN'` -> `options --{shell,fast,command,session-command,login} and --user are mutually exclusive`, and that check fires BEFORE the root check. So that line counts a pick-up that never happened. NOT FIXED — exclusion needs a new Wrapper concept; the gap is now documented on the test row that exercises it.

10. **su and runuser call getopt without `+`**, so GNU permutes and parses options standing inside the command's own argv — but once `Runs::With`'s switch is seen the loop breaks at the command position and never looks at them. Measured: `runuser -u nobody /bin/echo --from todo` -> `unrecognized option '--from'`, nothing runs. So `runuser -u 남 moai mv t-1 in_progress --from todo && sed -i …` counts a pick-up that never happened. The write-axis twin is a false deny: `runuser -u 남 sed -i s/a/b/ src/x.rs` is refused by real runuser over `-i`, and an existing test pins that Deny. NOT FIXED — pre-existing.

11. **`exec_of` treats any word equal to a predicate name as a predicate head**, so a predicate name standing as DATA before the real predicate shifts the harvest by one and the real command's head becomes a `-` word. `find . -name -execdir -exec tee src/x.rs \;` really truncates <repo>/src/x.rs, but exec_of harvests `-exec tee src/x.rs` (head `-exec`) so the write is invisible — Pass with nothing picked up. NOT FIXED — pre-existing, and telling a predicate position from an operand needs find's full grammar.

12. **`whole: true` is keyed on the wrapper NAME** while the twelve-letter table is util-linux 2.39's `su`; and because `Wrapped::Stops` withholds the handed text from every rule, a wrong entry costs rule 4 as well as rule 2. On a machine whose `su` is BSD or busybox and accepts a letter this table lacks, a rule-4 line really runs but `weird && w.whole` returns Stops and the tmux guard never sees the text. PARTIALLY ADDRESSED: doc note added on `Wrapper::whole`; the name-keying itself is unchanged.

13. **The rule-4 case `su -zx 남 -c '<tmux server kill>'` was asserted through `guard_writes`**, which carries no tmux axis — the line has no write target, so the assertion passed no matter what the code did, while the real behaviour change (Stops now hides the handed text from rule 4) was pinned by nothing. Probed: with su's `whole` flipped to false, `guard_shell` returns Deny; with it true, Pass. The change is real and was untested. FIXED — asserted via `guard_shell` with a `su -m` mirror that goes red if the letter table breaks.

14. **Nothing drove su's other short letters through the `whole` path** — only `-m` and `-pf`. The completeness claim `whole: true` rests on lived in a prose comment, and a letter falling out of the table fails as a silent Pass, not a red test. Delete `-P` from su's `free` and `su -P 남 -c 'sed -i …'` starts passing with every test green. FIXED — a loop now drives `-m -p -f -P -l -s -w -g -G` (with values) through a Deny assertion; verified red by removing `-P` from the table.

15. **Five newly written Korean comment lines use `감싸는 명령` for "wrapper"**, which docs/korean-terms.md lists in the do-not-use column for that meaning (docs/korean-terms.md:35 — `| wrapper | 래퍼 | 감싸는 명령 |`). Its scope line names `src/**/*.rs` 의 한국어 doc comment, and its closing rules are `이 표는 앞으로 쓰는 글에 걸고 … 새로 쓰는 줄에서만 지킨다`. FIXED on the five new lines (53 pre-existing occurrences left, as that document prescribes).

## What was applied

**Correctness**
- `find` guard: `*spot` now needs a location-shifting predicate **and** no `-exec`/`-ok` on the line — closes the lost-write on mixed lines and the one-word `-name -execdir` bypass. 4 regression rows.
- `--<unknown>=<value>` now records `weird`; `COMMON`/`--<digits>` leniency withdrawn on `whole: true` rows. 5 regression rows.
- getopt_long abbreviation support for that check (unambiguous prefix over the row's full long vocabulary, name-wise not occurrence-wise). 3 regression rows. **This fixed a regression the reviewer's own first attempt introduced** — caught by the sweep, confirmed by measuring `su --sh=…`, and re-verified red/green.

**Tests**
- The vacuous rule-4 assertion now runs through `guard_shell`, with a `su -m` mirror.
- A per-letter loop pins the completeness claim `whole: true` depends on.

**Structure / docs**
- `exec_of`'s local `PREDS` replaced by shared `FIND_HERE`/`FIND_AWAY` module consts.
- `!mixes &&` added to both new positional guards, stating the getopt-`+` rule the function already derives as `mixes` (no verdict changes today; removes a latent trap where a future `args>0` + permuting row would lose `ops`/`dashed`).
- Terminology on the five new lines; doc note that a wrong `whole` entry costs rule 4; the `find` comment rewritten to state the approximation honestly; pointer comments on the two `w.args` clauses the new loop head made unreachable.

**Skipped, reported only:** findings 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 3 (the `-execdir` depth-0 measurement — flagged because it shows the decided Pass is the common case, not the edge case the comment argues from).

**Cut from the list (all already fixed or low value):** the `alien ||` disjunct is now unobservable (`shell` is non-empty only on the two `whole: true` rows, so `alien || w.whole` equals `w.whole`); `if seen == w.args` in the operand arm now equals `w.args == 0`; flock's `glued: true` is now unread; several rows in `options_end_at_the_positional_argument` restate coverage already in `three_more_wrappers_hand_a_string_to_a_shell`; and commit `2dfff61` bundles two independently revertible fixes against CLAUDE.md's `한 커밋은 한 가지 일이다`.

**Verified sound:** every measurement claim in the reviewed diff reproduces here — the four positional wrappers all fail on a post-positional `-` word and on `--`; `flock -- <f> -c`, `flock <f> --command <text>`, `flock -n <f> -c` all run; `-execdir` prints the match's directory; su/runuser's short alphabets are exactly the twelve/thirteen letters the table covers. No new dependency, no new command, no `.moai` write in the worktree.

Ten finder angles plus a Phase 3 sweep, all findings reproduced against the built binary. Fixes applied to the working tree; `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` (0 warnings) and `cargo test` (1,384 + 506, all passing) are green.

Four more that did not fit the cap, each reproduced: the carried body is re-measured by `check_text_size` on write, so an over-limit idea body (hand-merged row) now blocks `promote` outright and names a title rather than the idea (`store.rs:745`; `moai-clta` fixed exactly this trap twelve lines below with `fit_bytes`); `--body` is refused even for a **file** plan where there is no stdin contest, so `add --from plan.md --body …` is impossible while `Rooted.body` exists and `promote` fills it; the deleted line "Unfolding into a single issue is the same: move the idea's body over as it is" left the `-e <standing epic>` flow — the supervisor brief's own step 7-1 recall path — with no guidance for the dropped body, and the new prose argues only about the milestone; and `moai add 'member' -e <epic> --milestone <other>` silently writes a dead field while `moai edit` explains the identical situation via `report::milestone_from_above`, so one binary has three behaviours for one field.

## Fixes applied

- **Body fan-out** — `create_drafts` hands the body to the **first** root only (`body.take()`); the milestone still goes to every root because members inherit it. The assignment is additive (`if let Some(…)`) rather than an unconditional overwrite. New test `a_multi_epic_unfold_copies_the_body_once`. Verified: a two-epic promote writes 1 body copy and 2 milestone fields, members still resolve under the milestone.
- **Rehearsal/real parity** — `check_plan` gained `milestone` and `lang` and refuses a bad-shaped id, reusing `store::At::Unwritten` + `model::Invalid::GroupId` + `view::invalid` so rehearsal and write emit the byte-identical message and the same exit code. Wired into both `bulk`'s and `promote`'s dry-run. New test `a_rehearsal_measures_the_milestone_it_reports` asserts the two stderr strings are equal and that a well-shaped dangling id still passes both.
- **`--quiet`** — added to `--from`'s `conflicts_with_all`, matching the diff's own moai-fppn rule, and folded into `a_plan_refuses_the_flags_it_cannot_use`. (Having `bulk` honour it would invent a new output contract for a flag documented as "the id only", so I took the refusal.)
- **Row-blind test** — `promote_carries_the_milestone_and_the_body` now selects the epic row by `"kind":"epic"` and the member by title, asserts the epic holds body and milestone, and asserts the member holds neither.
- **Prose, all three synced surfaces regenerated** (`moai init` + `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`): the supervisor gate now says "carries over the milestone and the body"; the `ideas()` rule now covers no-milestone, shipped and deferred ("carries the id the idea held whatever state it is in"), names `--milestone none`, and states the deferred consequence; the worker brief step 1 no longer claims there is nothing to hang when `<milestone>` is `none`; `add --from --milestone` is documented in fork 3.
- **rustfmt** — `cargo fmt --all`.
- **CHANGELOG** — stale Unreleased entry rewritten, entries added for `add --from --milestone` and the flag refusals, flagged as a break, with the exit-2/non-JSON caveat.
- Also: stale `refuse.plan_has_no_milestone_how` advice updated (en+ko); `bulk` reads the milestone line off the written rows through a shared `add::stood_on`, so both verbs derive it one way; `Rooted`'s dead `Default` derive removed.

- **The raw-vs-resolved milestone and the deferred/shipped carry (findings 1, 3, 5)** — the deeper half. Switching `promote` to `report::milestones_in`, or refusing/warning on a `deferred`/`done` milestone, changes which release whole bundles land in and touches the write path inside the lock, in cases the recorded user decision ("idea 의 마일스톤") does not cover. **This is the most important open item**: the deferred case makes a freshly approved plan vanish from `ready`, from `held` and from the warnings, with the only signal being a line that reads as success. A refusal, a stderr line, or a `promote --milestone <id>|none` opt-out would all close it; which one is the user's call.
- The two refusal contracts, the masked namespace refusals and the file-plan `--body` conflict all need the flag set split per namespace (or a `--body -`-only conflict); clap cannot keep the actionable refusals otherwise.
- `--type` with `--from`, the singular/unchecked `milestone_line` wording, truncating an over-limit carried body, inventing the `-e` body guidance, and giving `add` the `milestone_from_above` notice are behaviour or policy calls outside this diff.

**Below the cut:** `App::on_projects` no longer seeds `App::zone` (src/tui/mod.rs:1481) — correct today only because `cmd/tui.rs:215` calls it before `adopt_look` at :231 with no draw in between; insert any early render and the layer's `+N` and every on-screen timestamp judge in UTC. And the one decision ("the count does not touch the timezone") is restated in 26 comment blocks across 6 files, three of which had already gone stale inside the diff itself (findings 5, 8).

**Checked and clean** (so the next round need not redo it): every reader of `Site::warnings` / `Summary::warnings` / `Fresh::warnings` judges the dues; every `report::status` caller gets the folded form and every `status_in` caller wants the unfolded one; `StatusReport` is never deserialized and `--json` emits no `dues`; `moai tui --json` and `moai -C <dir> status --json` agree on the count and honour `TZ` identically across the `status_due_days` boundary; no signature breakage anywhere (`cargo check --all-targets`); no dependency or budget change. Also checked and found correct, despite looking inverted: the two `"전제: …"` messages in the new draw test are failure-condition messages, not premise statements.

## Fixes applied

Unstaged in the worktree, on `worktree-moai-fgjj` (5 files, +54/−36):

- **src/report.rs** — `judged` captures `at` before the `mem::take` (the correctness bug); the `(days, id)` sort moved from `Dues::split` into `Dues::judge` so the per-frame `count` no longer sorts; duplicated `Soil` paragraph removed; the test's `at()` helper panics on an absent kind and a `no_epic < milestone_overdue` assertion pins the insertion slot.
- **src/tui/draw.rs** — `fn surfaced` moved out from under `shut_style`'s doc comment; "자리 셋" → "자리 둘" with both call sites named; stale `App::recount`.
- **src/tui/mod.rs** — the `[Site::stranded]` broken link; `Surfaced::count`'s `now` doc corrected to say what the callers actually pass; stale `App::recount`.
- **src/tui/zones.rs**, **src/view.rs** — stale `App::recount` and the two `report::status_in` deadline cross-references.

**Verification:** `cargo test` 1388 + 500 pass, 0 fail. `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` clean. `cargo doc` no longer warns at src/tui/mod.rs:615 and every new intra-doc link resolves. End to end, the fixed binary and develop's binary now print byte-identical warning ordering (`['no_epic','no_milestone','future_timestamp','milestone_overdue']`) on the same fixture.

## Two things you still own

1. **No review issue exists for this round.** `moai show moai-fgjj --json` shows `in_progress`, epic `moai-pmhv`, no children, empty `work`. Per the hook rule you need `moai add 'review — 기한 판정을 그릴 때 재는 갈래' -t review --parent moai-fgjj -b '<고른 등급과 까닭>'`, then the reviewer text and a separate hand-on note naming the ids.
2. **The AI line**, for that review issue — `tokens=` dropped because I cannot count my own, and CLAUDE.md says a guess is worse than a blank:

   `model: anthropic/opus-5 (max — report·tui 이지만 저장 꼴과 캐시 계약을 건드렸다)`

Two skipped findings are worth parking as ideas rather than losing: the `banner()` double call (finding 14) and the `status_in` type-level guard (finding 10).

title: 시간대를 고르는 자가 그리는 쪽에 셋이다

text:
리뷰의 덧붙임(원문, 영어) — 늦게 돌아온 Phase-3 훑기가 셋을 더 냈다. 고침은 없다.

1. src/tui/draw.rs:715 — three independent choosers of the fold clock, plus a shadowed helper name.
   The (&app.site.now, &app.zone) pair is picked in three unrelated places: banner at draw.rs:715,
   fn surfaced at draw.rs:2726, cmd/tui.rs:189. fn surfaced takes &Summary, so banner (which holds a
   Surfaced from Site) structurally cannot reuse it, and banner's `let surfaced = …` shadows the
   module-level fn from that point on. Whoever makes the change the Surfaced::count doc anticipates
   ("이 자리를 crate::model::now() 로 바꾸면 그 틈까지 사라진다") edits the helper the doc calls the
   one place and misses draw.rs:715 — and then the explorer crosses midnight with the banner saying
   "드러난 것 1건" (stale site.now) while the layer row for the same repo shows no ! (live clock),
   which is literally the "한 화면에 시계 둘이 돈다" symptom moai-fgjj was filed for. Four-line fix:
   drop the #[cfg(test)] at draw.rs:19 so `use super::Surfaced;` is unconditional (that test-only
   import is what forced the &Summary signature); make it
   `fn surfaced(app: &App, counted: &Surfaced) -> usize { counted.count(&app.site.now, &app.zone) }`;
   have place_line:2681 and place_about:2789 pass &sum.warnings; have banner:715 rename its local
   binding and call surfaced(app, &app.site.warnings). cmd/tui.rs:189 stays separate and correct.

2. src/tui/mod.rs:1509 — stale rationale, not a stale name. count_all has exactly one caller, but the
   comment above that call still reads "까닭은 [`App::count_all`] 에 있다 — 여기 베껴 두면 한쪽만
   고쳐져 둘이 갈린다", which presupposes a second site, while count_all's own new doc four lines
   below says it is "여는 걸음([`App::build`])이 부르는 한 자리다". All ten finder angles missed it
   because it is a reason, not a name.

3. src/report.rs:6305 — the report-side test cannot see a zone-blind Dues::count. Both assertions
   expect 1: count(now, utc()) == 1 and count(now, &seoul) == 1. A regression that drops
   zone.shift(now) from Dues::split leaves both green; so would a count hard-coded to return 1. Only
   the kind_of assertions separate the zones, and those exercise judge, not count — so Dues::count,
   the value every TUI surface draws through, has no zone-sensitive test on the report side. The
   sibling draw test got this right: it picks a due date straddling status_due_days so the count
   itself moves between zones.

**그리고 원문의 한 줄이 틀렸다** — "the Phase-3 gap sweep contributed nothing"。그 훑기는 뒤늦게
돌아와 위 셋을 냈다. 리뷰가 스스로 고쳐 알렸다.
model: anthropic/opus-5 tokens=352158 (max — 셈의 계약과 스레드가 든 값을 함께 봤다. 늦게 돌아온 Phase-3 훑기도 이 수에 든다)

받은 것 — 일곱을 `8d05268` 로 남겼다.

- 1번이 실제 버그였다. `judged` 가 `mem::take` 뒤에 `self.dues.at` 을 읽어 그 값이 늘 0 이었고,
  기한 줄이 목록 머리에 끼어 `moai status`·`--json`·훅의 보드가 다 그 차례로 섰다. 리뷰가 두
  바이너리를 같은 판에 돌려 차례를 글자째 견줘 왔다
- 2번은 그 버그가 초록으로 지나간 까닭이다. 내가 넣은 시험의 차례 견주기가 `Option` 끼리 견주는
  꼴이라 `None < Some(_)` 으로 늘 참이었다. 없는 갈래에 패닉하는 것과 `no_epic` 이 앞이라는 줄을
  함께 받았다
- 4번(프레임마다의 정렬)은 내가 못 본 값이다. `Dues::count` 는 갈래가 비었는지만 보는데 `split`
  이 정렬까지 해, 그리는 걸음마다 프로젝트 수만큼 버릴 차례를 지었다
- 3·5·6·7·8·9번은 글이다 — 문서 주석이 엉뚱한 함수에 붙은 것, 지운 필드를 가리킨 링크, 두 벌이
  된 문단, `recount` 라는 옛 이름 셋, `status_in` 이 기한을 재는 자라던 `view` 의 가리킴 둘,
  그리고 `Surfaced::count` 의 `now` 가 지키지 못하는 약속을 적어 둔 것

9번은 되돌아간 것이 없음을 리뷰가 스스로 확인했다 — 날 판정이 마지막 읽기의 시각으로 얼어 있는
틈은 60초(`REREAD_EVERY`)고 옛 꼴도 셈이 돈 때의 날로 얼려 들었다. "층의 `site.now` 가 세션 내내
얼어 있다" 는 더 센 주장은 리뷰가 직접 반박했다(`follow_layer` 가 쓸기를 들일 때마다 찍는다).

덧붙임 셋은 **moai-ynd6** 로 세웠다 — 에픽의 멤버이고 첫 칸에 둔다. 1번이 내가 넣은 덫이라
넘기지 않고, 다음 회차(moai-yz4j)가 같은 가지에서 함께 고쳐 그 회차의 리뷰가 보게 한다. 4줄
고침 하나에 리뷰 한 판을 새로 사는 것이 moai-bx6t 의 비용 결정과 어긋나서다.

넘긴 것 — idea 다섯을 담았다. 에픽이 내건 셋(기한·하나씩·든 시간)은 다 서므로 멤버로 안 세웠고,
이 판이 없어도 v0.1.2 가 나가므로 마일스톤 밖에 둔다.

- moai-sx2d — 10번. 판정 안 한 보고서를 내는 문을 꼴로 막는다. 지금 부르는 둘은 맞지만, 다음
  표면이 `Soil` 아끼기를 쓰려고 옮기면 말없이 기한 경고를 잃는다
- moai-fwwr — 12번. `Dues` 의 기본값이 "안 정했다" 가 아니라 자리 0·문턱 0 으로 읽힌다. 1번이
  컴파일된 까닭이다
- moai-4xvr — 13번. 시험의 `shown()` 이 견주는 쪽마다 판정을 다시 한다
- moai-p3pv — 14번. `draw::screen` 이 한 프레임에 `banner()` 를 두 번 부른다 (이 판이 만든 것이 아니다)
- moai-i15e — 15번. `Dues` 가 `due_on` 을 문자열로 들어 프레임마다 다시 푼다

moai-a678(첫 화면이 훑기를 두 벌 돈다)은 이 판이 **다른 길로** 없애 닫았다 — 둘째 훑기가 선
까닭이 사라졌고, 그 idea 가 댄 길(`App::open` 부르는 자리 열두 곳)은 안 갔다.

안 받은 것 둘.

- 리뷰가 "이 회차의 리뷰 이슈가 없다" 며 `--parent moai-fgjj` 로 세우라고 했는데, 이 이슈가 그
  리뷰 이슈다(감독 브리프 7단계가 `--parent moai-pmhv` 를 정했다). 서브에이전트는 트래커를 안
  보고 `moai show moai-fgjj --json` 의 자식만 봤다
- "한 결정을 주석 스물여섯 곳에 다시 적었다" 는 잘라 낸 지적. 되돌리지 않을 결정을 그 자리에
  적는 것이 이 저장소의 규약이고, 그중 낡은 셋은 위에서 고쳤다

note: 고침 일곱을 받고(1번이 실제 버그였다) 덧붙임 셋을 moai-ynd6 로, 나머지 다섯을 idea 로 넘겼다. moai-a678 은 이 판이 다른 길로 없애 닫았다

text:
Summary: review agent-a11d913b433c6dcff, `/code-review max --fix`, opus-5. 10 finder angles, 71 candidate findings. The run was cut off by a session rate limit after it had applied its fixes but before it wrote its own final list, so what follows is the angles' own reports, condensed to one line each. Fixes landed in 047c51a; what is still open is named at the end.

## Angle A — line-by-line scan
1. src/view.rs — `view::detail` still reads the written `epic` field, so `moai show <member>` no longer names the epic for any issue a plan created: the one surface AGENTS.md points sessions at went blind. FIXED
2. src/tui/draw.rs — the explorer's About pane has the identical blindness (`if let Some(id) = &i.epic`), even though it resolves the milestone through the index precisely to avoid this bug class. FIXED
3. tests/cli.rs — the new test code is not rustfmt-clean, so `cargo fmt --check` exits 1 and ci-gate fails on this branch. FIXED
4. src/cmd/show.rs — a member reassigned with `moai edit <id> -e <other epic>` is still drawn as a `Child` row under the old epic while the count, the tree and the rollup put it under the new one. NOT FIXED — it is a child by id, and the id never moves; the Child row is the truth.
5. src/cmd/add.rs — `create_drafts` encodes membership in an irreversible id while relying on an invariant it never checks: `into: Some` must imply `Shape::Members`, or the plan's `#` epic is minted as `<into>.<abc>` and silently loses its milestone and body. FIXED (debug_assert!)
6. tests/cli.rs — `list_in` finds its key by a raw substring scan, so a title or body containing `"members":[` steers it at the wrong array. PARTLY FIXED (it now dies loudly on an array it cannot read)

## Angle B — removed-behavior auditor
1. src/cmd/edit.rs — removing the written `epic` makes a plan member's membership irreversible: `-e none` is a no-op and `-e <other>` leaves the id pointing at the first epic. The reversal path now lives outside the tool. FIXED AS DOCUMENTATION (guide paragraph)
2. src/report.rs — `moai rm <epic>` now trips `no_epic` plus `orphan_child` where the old shape tripped only `dangling_epic`. HANDED ON (idea moai-d2vy)
3. src/view.rs — no test covers the missing Epic row; the one test that asserts it builds its member with `add -e`, so it stays green. FIXED (test added)
4. src/tui/draw.rs — the About pane is now inconsistent with its own Milestone field right below, deliberately changed by moai-9yrv to read the placed value. FIXED
5. src/cmd/mod.rs — every list/row `--json` surface dropped the `epic` key for plan members while `prime --json` still hands the derived epic over: two machine surfaces in one binary answer "which epic" differently. HANDED ON (moai-wuzi)
6. src/cmd/edit.rs — the moai-vndz de-duplication was applied to only one of the two `view::detail` call sites, so `moai edit <epic>` still prints every member as a Child row. FIXED
7. src/view.rs — `view::detail`'s children loop documents an invariant the diff broke: it asserts the list it receives is never filtered. FIXED (comment)
8. src/id.rs — the module doc states the opposite of the design: the dot is now the sole record of membership for plan members. FIXED

## Angle C — cross-file tracer
1-2. Same two blind surfaces as Angle A/B. FIXED
3. src/cmd/rm.rs — `rm <epic>` permanently orphans every plan member; before, they only lost a rewritable field. HANDED ON (moai-d2vy)
4. src/cmd/add.rs — `moai add '<title>' -e <epic>` still mints a flat id with an `epic` field, so one binary produces two member shapes for the same act. HANDED ON (moai-7f03)
5. src/cmd/add.rs — the `Rooted` doc still defines the root as "the row with no epic of its own", three lines above the corrected `stood_on`. FIXED
6. src/id.rs — module contract stale. FIXED
7. src/id.rs — plan members move from the 36^4 root space into the 36^3 per-parent space, raising cross-branch duplicate-id probability for the workflow this repo runs. NOT FIXED — same space reviews have always used; `mint` still walks `taken` inside the lock.
8. src/cmd/mod.rs — `--json` gives a machine no derived epic although `Row` already carries derived values beside the stored ones. HANDED ON (moai-wuzi)

## Angle D — language pitfalls
1. src/cmd/show.rs — the de-duplication matched members by id string, so with duplicate id lines a row that is NOT the member is dropped from the Child block and never reappears: it vanishes from `moai show <epic>` entirely. FIXED (`report::kin_of` matches on line identity; unit test)
2. tests/cli.rs — `text.matches(id).count() == 1` is a substring count, and this change makes every member a parent id, so it reports "drawn twice" for a row drawn once as soon as a member gets a child. FIXED (`drawn` helper)
3. tests/cli.rs — `ids_in` scrapes every `"id":"`, including ids nested in a preserved unknown field or in journal entries. FIXED (row-opening match)
4. tests/cli.rs — `list_in` answers `Some(vec![])` for arrays it cannot parse, the empty-vs-could-not-ask conflation the codebase forbids. FIXED
5. src/cmd/add.rs — `ids[nth]` is an unchecked index that now decides the minted id inside an open write transaction, and the invariant keeping it in range lives only in `draft::parse`. FIXED (debug_assert! on the `into`/Shape pair)
6. tests/cli.rs — fmt. FIXED

## Angle E — derived-state consistency
Eight findings, all restating the three above: the detail, the explorer pane and `edit` read the raw field (FIXED); the `--json` contract is now false and its doc still asserts the old meaning (HANDED ON, comment added naming the fix); `-e none` is a permanent no-op (documented); `id.rs` doc stale (FIXED); `add -e` mints the other shape (HANDED ON); `epic_from_parent` names the same id twice for a plan member, so the message reads as a tautology (NOT FIXED — it is the honest answer: the parent is the epic).

## Angle Reuse
1. tests/cli.rs — `parent_in` re-implements `id::parent_of` character-for-character; this file already pulls source modules in with `#[path]` (`git_leaks`, `scratch`) and `src/id.rs` is std-only. FIXED
2. src/cmd/add.rs — the inlined mint match is byte-for-byte `store::new_id`. NOT FIXED — `new_id` builds its own `taken` per call; the plan path carries one growing set.
3. src/cmd/idea.rs — `grown` inlines the root test that `add::stood_on` also uses. FIXED (`add::is_root`)
4. src/cmd/show.rs — "which children are not members" is a new unnamed rule living in `cmd/`; every other membership question is owned by `report`. FIXED (`report::kin_of`)
5. src/cmd/edit.rs — re-implements `report::children_of` and loses its ordering contract. FIXED
6. tests/cli.rs — `list_in` duplicates a closure already written inline in `an_epic_counts_the_children_that_inherit_it`. NOT FIXED — left for whoever touches that test next.
7. tests/cli.rs — the "drawn once" counter already existed at tests/cli.rs:6256. FIXED (hoisted to `drawn`)
8. tests/cli.rs — fmt. FIXED

# 리뷰 — 훅이 아직 못 보는 쓰기: su·runuser 의 옵션과 find 의 술어 자리 (moai-514e.mvw)

## 무엇을 봤나

범위는 `a312a53` 한 커밋(`develop`...`HEAD`)이고 고쳐진 파일은 `src/hook.rs` 하나다(+301/-44). 이슈 여섯을 함께 든 커밋이다 — moai-s8dp·moai-694g·moai-j9i9·moai-2m3l·moai-fg47·moai-xk0q.

등급은 `max`. 멤버가 전부 쓰기 경로와 훅을 건드렸고(CLAUDE.md 의 "any member touched the write path, concurrency, the storage format or hooks"), 옵션 읽기·`*spot`·`Stops` 세 계약을 한꺼번에 바꿨다.

열한 갈래로 나눠 보고(줄 단위·걷어낸 행동·호출 자리·Rust 함정·모델 충실도·재사용·단순화·효율·고도·규약·틈 훑기), 잡힌 것은 **되도록 진짜 프로그램으로 쟀다** — findutils 4.9.0, util-linux 2.39.3, coreutils 9.4, sudo, 그리고 `getopt(1)`. 아래에 "쟀다" 라고 적은 것은 이 기계에서 실제로 돌려 본 것이다.

---

## 고친 것 (열한 자리)

### 1. `flock <파일> --com '<글>'` 을 도는 줄로 읽었다 — 이번 커밋이 연 자리

`expand` 가 고리 머리에서 줄인 긴 이름을 되돌리는데, 그 되돌린 낱말이 **getopt 를 안 거치는 유일한 자리**까지 갔다. flock 은 잠글 파일 바로 다음 낱말이 글자째 `-c`·`--command` 인지를 제 손으로 견주는데(바로 위 주석이 그렇게 적어 뒀다), `--com` 이 `--command` 로 바뀌어 그 견줌을 통과했다.

쟀다: `flock <파일> --com 'echo RAN'` 은 `flook: failed to execute --com: No such file or directory` 로 지고 `--command` 라고 적은 것만 돈다.

값: `flock /tmp/l --com 'moai mv <id> in_progress --from todo' && <쓰기>` 가 안 도는 집기를 세어 뒤의 빈손 쓰기를 풀어 준다. 쓰기 축 쌍둥이는 안 도는 줄을 잘못 막는다.

고침: 고리 머리에서 친 그대로의 낱말을 `raw` 로 들고, 그 갈래만 `raw` 를 본다.

### 2. `longs()` 가 `COMMON` 을 안 들어 `expand` 가 모자란 표로 앞머리를 푼다

`--debug`·`--verbose` 는 `COMMON` 에만 서 있고 `longs()` 에는 없다. 그런데 맨 `--이름` 갈래는 `loose` 로 그 둘을 받아 준다 — **같은 이름의 두 철자가 반대 답을 내고 양쪽 다 틀렸다.**

- 새는 쪽(이번 커밋이 열었다): `env --de …` 를 `--default-signal` 하나로 풀어 도는 줄로 읽는다. 진짜 env 는 `option '--de' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--default-signal' '--debug'` 로 125 에 진다. 고치기 전에는 `Stops` 였다.
- 막는 쪽(전부터 있던 자리): `timeout --verb 1 echo` 는 정말 도는데(`--verbose` 의 모호하지 않은 앞머리다) 훅은 `Stops` 를 내어 그 줄의 `sed -i` 를 통째로 못 봤다. `chrt --verb`·`xargs --verb` 도 같다.

고침: `longs()` 가 `loose` 와 **같은 잣대로** `COMMON` 을 든다(`if w.whole { &[][..] } else { COMMON }`). 표가 다 찬 줄(su·runuser)에서는 `loose` 도 안 받으니 여기서도 안 든다 — `su --verbose` 의 답은 그대로다.

### 3. `-exec` 무리를 아무 `+` 에서나 끊었다

GNU find 은 `{}` **바로 뒤**의 `+` 만 끝맺음으로 읽는다. 딴 자리의 `+` 는 그 명령의 평범한 인자다.

쟀다: `find . -exec echo ARG + more \;` 는 `ARG + more` 를 찍고, `find . -exec tee + src/x.rs \;` 는 `+` 와 `src/x.rs` 를 **둘 다** 만든다.

값: `+` 한 낱말이 어느 `-exec` 쓰기에나 붙이면 되는 샛길이었다. 옛 `exec_of` 부터 있던 자리인데 이 커밋이 그 함수를 다시 쓰면서 그대로 옮겨 왔다.

### 4. find 의 `-D <debugopts>` 가 낱말 하나를 먹는 것을 두 자리가 다 몰랐다

- `exec_spots` 가 안 먹어 그 값을 술어로 읽는다. 쟀다: `find -D -exec . -maxdepth 0 -exec tee src/x.rs \;` 는 모르는 debug 이름을 **경고만 하고 그대로 돌아** 그 파일을 만드는데, 걷는 자리가 한 칸 밀려 쓰기가 통째로 안 보였다.
- `find_starts` 는 `-D` 를 붙여 쓰는 것으로 읽었다(`w.starts_with("-D")`). 쟀다: `find -Dtree .` 는 `unknown predicate` 고 `find -D tree .` 가 돈다. 그래서 `exec` 가 시작 자리로 세어져 딴 자리에서만 도는 `find -D exec /tmp -execdir tee src/x.rs \;` 를 **잘못 막았다**.

고침: `FIND_EATS` 한 표를 둘이 함께 본다. `find_starts` 의 `at += 2` 가 끝을 넘을 수 있어 슬라이스 자르기를 `rest.get(at..)` 로 바꿨다 — 안 그러면 `find -D` 만 친 줄에서 훅이 터진다.

### 5. `find -- <시작 자리>` 가 시작 자리를 빈 목록으로 냈다

`find_starts` 가 `--` 에서 끊고, 빈 목록은 "안 댔다"(곧 `.`, 여기 밑)라는 뜻이라 딴 자리의 쓰기를 잘못 막는다. 쟀다: `find -- . -name a` 도 `find -L -- /tmp …` 도 정말 돈다.

### 6. `expand` 가 빈 값을 단 줄인 이름을 되돌렸다 — 이번 커밋이 연 자리

`runuser --u=` 를 `--user=` 로 되돌리면 아래 `--이름=값` 갈래가 `saw` 를 세워 명령 자리가 열린다. 진짜 runuser 는 빈 optarg 를 받아 `user '' does not exist` 로 진다. 고치기 전에는 모르는 이름이라 `Stops` 였다.

값: `runuser --u= moai mv <id> in_progress && <쓰기>` 가 안 도는 집기를 세었다.

### 7. `sudo --shell=x` 를 도는 줄로 읽었다

값 없는 깃발에 `=` 를 달면 그 프로그램이 거절하는데, `glued: false` 인 줄에서는 붙은 값만 버리고 마저 읽었다. 쟀다: `sudo --shell=x /bin/echo` 는 `option '--shell' doesn't allow an argument` 다. 짧은 `sudo -s=x` 는 뭉치 고리가 `=` 에서 이미 멈춰, **같은 옵션의 두 철자가 반대 답**을 냈다 — moai-s8dp 가 없애려던 바로 그 꼴이다.

### 8. `hands` 갈래가 짧은 꼴에서도 `=` 를 먹었다

`=` 로 값을 붙이는 것은 긴 이름뿐이다. 쟀다: `getopt -o c: -- -c=x` 의 optarg 는 `x` 가 아니라 `=x` 고, `--command=x` 의 optarg 만 `x` 다.

값: `su -c='moai mv <id> …' 남` 은 진짜로는 `=moai …` 라는 없는 명령을 돌리는데(`sh -c '=echo RAN'` → `not found`, rc 127 로 쟀다) 훅은 그 집기를 세었다. `env -S=…` 도 같다. moai-s8dp 가 `stops`·`elsewhere` 에 세운 "긴 이름만 본다" 잣대가 이 갈래에만 안 들어 있었다.

고침: 붙인 값 걷기를 `--` 이름으로만 한다. 짧은 꼴은 아래 뭉치 고리가 `=` 를 값의 첫 글자로 받아 제 답을 낸다.

### 9. 홀로 선 `-`(로그인)이 `clash` 를 안 지났다

`runuser -u 남 -` 의 `-` 는 피연산자 갈래로 가서 `clashed` 를 못 세운다. 쟀다: 그 줄은 `-c` 를 준 것과 글자 하나 안 틀리게 `options --{shell,fast,command,session-command,login} and --user are mutually exclusive` 로 진다. moai-j9i9 가 `-l` 로 닫은 구멍이 그 철자에만 열려 있었다.

### 10. 뭉치 고리에서 `saw` 와 `clashed` 가 다른 글자 무리를 훑었다

`clashed |=` 는 고리 머리에 섰는데 `saw |=` 는 `chdir`·`hands` 갈래 **아래**에 있었다. 그 넷은 제 값을 만나면 `break` 하니, 한 글자가 그 표와 `Runs::With` 목록에 함께 드는 날 `saw && clashed` 의 문이 조용히 안 선다. 지금은 그런 줄이 없어 답이 안 바뀐다 — 앞으로 안 어긋나게 둘을 한자리로 올렸다.

### 11. 자리 튜플과 낡은 주석

- `exec_spots` 가 `Vec<(bool, usize, usize)>` 를 냈다. `from`·`to` 가 둘 다 `usize` 라 자리를 바꿔 적어도 컴파일이 되고, 그러면 훅이 Bash 한 번마다 슬라이스에서 터진다 — `Wrapper` 가 다섯 자리 튜플을 이름으로 바꾼 것과 같은 까닭이라 `ExecSpot` 구조체로 뒀다.
- `hands_at` 반환 위의 주석이 "`saw` 면 피연산자 고리가 곧장 끊겨 `ops` 가 빈 채로 온다" 고 적고 있었는데, moai-2m3l 가 `&& !saw` 를 걷어내 더는 사실이 아니다. 지금 그 자리가 안 닿는 까닭(`clash` 가 먼저 `Stops` 를 낸다)과 `skip(1)` 이 아직 맞는 까닭으로 고쳐 적었다.

### 시험 쪽에서 고친 것

- **안 도는 줄을 Deny 로 못박고 있던 시험**: 새로 든 `"find . -newermt -exec -exec tee src/x.rs \;"` 는 진짜 find 이 `I cannot figure out how to interpret '-exec' as a date or time` 로 아무것도 안 돌린다. `-newerXY` 의 `Y` 가 `a`·`B`·`c`·`m` 이면 값이 **파일**이라 술어 이름도 받으므로 `-newermm -execdir` 로 바꿨다 — 앞머리 규칙은 그대로 재면서 정말 도는 줄이다.
- **아무것도 안 재게 된 시험**: `"runuser -lu 남 -- sed -i …"` 는 `clash` 때문에 이제 `Stops` 라 Pass 무리에서 늘 참이었다. `-u` 없는 철자로 바꾸고, 그것만으로는 여전히 안 재기에(`elsewhere` 를 걷어도 `-l` 이 모르는 글자가 되어 같은 Pass 가 난다) **절대 경로 짝**을 함께 세웠다. 재 봤다 — runuser 의 `elsewhere` 를 걷어내면 그 짝이 붉어진다.
- **문이 열리는지 안 보던 시험**: `every_door_that_hands_a_string_costs_what_a_substitution_costs` 는 상한 둘만 재서, 첫 겹에서 멈추는 철자는 두 값을 거저 지난다. `runuser -u x -c` 가 `clash` 에 닫혔을 때 아무것도 안 붉어져 그 줄을 손으로 바꿔야 했던 까닭이다. 한 겹에서 글을 정말 읽는지 먼저 묻는 한 줄을 더했다.
- **새 `Stops` 셋의 짝**: 셋 다 제 주석에서 집기 누수를 까닭으로 드는데 시험은 쓰기 축만 재고 있었다. 집기 쪽 쌍둥이 일곱 줄과 규칙 4 짝 넷을 더했다.

---

## 안 고친 것과 까닭

1. **`sudo -i -s` 를 잘못 막는다.** `clash` 는 `saw && clashed` 로 재는데 `saw` 는 `Runs::With`·`Runs::Unless` 에서만 서니, `Runs::Always` 인 열다섯 줄에서는 이 칸이 **구조적으로 안 읽힌다**. 진짜 sudo 는 `you may not specify both the -i and -s options` 로 진다. 고치려면 `exclusive: &[&[&str]]` 같은 일반 어휘로 바꿔야 해서 표 모양을 건드린다 — 리뷰가 낼 고침의 크기가 아니다.
2. **`-fprint`·`-fprint0`·`-fls`·`-fprintf` 가 만드는 파일이 안 보인다.** `FIND_TAKES` 는 그 값을 "건너뛸 낱말" 로만 알고, 그 낱말은 find 이 만들고 비우는 파일이다. 쟀다: `find . -maxdepth 0 -fprint src/y.rs` 는 그 파일을 만든다. 읽어 내는 것은 새 기능이라 이슈로 세울 자리다.
3. **`*spot` 이 줄 하나에 한 값이라 `-exec` 와 `-execdir` 이 함께 선 줄이 잘못 막힌다.** `find /tmp -execdir tee src/x.rs \; -exec true \;` 가 그 줄이다. 이미 코드가 까닭과 함께 적어 둔 결정이고, 이제 `exec_spots` 가 무리마다 `away` 를 들고 있으니 갈 길은 열렸지만 `Text::Find`·`handed_text` 계약을 함께 바꿔야 한다.
4. **`env --null=1` 을 도는 줄로 읽는다.** `free` 가 값을 안 받는 이름(`--null`)과 붙여서만 받는 이름(`--block-signal`)을 한 칸에 들어, 붙인 값 훑기를 `whole` 로 가르게 됐다. 제대로 고치려면 래퍼 열일곱 줄의 `free` 를 전부 다시 걷어야 하고, 하나를 빠뜨리면 정당한 `--이름=값` 이 통째로 안 보이는 **새는 쪽**으로 기운다. 전부터 있던 자리다.
5. **`Wrapped::Runs { skip }` 이 permute 된 래퍼 깃발을 그대로 넘긴다.** `runuser -u 남 moai mv <id> in_progress -m x` 에서 진짜 runuser 는 `-m` 을 제 것으로 먹는데 훅은 그것이 든 argv 를 본다. `Runs` 가 자리 하나가 아니라 피연산자 목록을 들어야 해서 구조 변경이다.
6. **su 표에 `-u`·`--user` 가 없다.** 쟀다: `su -u nobody -c true` 는 `invalid option` 이 아니라 su 가 제 손으로 거절하는 말을 낸다 — getopt 는 그 글자를 안다. 지금은 양쪽 다 "안 돈다" 로 모여 답이 같지만, `whole: true` 가 내건 "표가 다 찼다" 는 사실이 아니다. `takes` 에 넣으면 `su -u X -c …` 가 도는 줄이 되어 되레 틀리니, 적을 자리는 `clash` 를 일반화한 뒤다(위 1번과 한 몸이다).
7. **규약 둘.** 한 커밋이 이슈 여섯을 든다(CLAUDE.md "한 커밋은 한 가지 일이다" — `git revert` 로 하나만 되돌릴 수 없고 `moai show moai-fg47` 의 `commits` 가 남의 것 여덟 할을 가리킨다). 그리고 moai-xk0q 는 "지금은 안 고치기로 했다" 는 주석만 들어간 채 `in_progress` 로 남아 있다 — `defer` 나 moai-99yy 로의 재배치가 그 결정을 적는 자리다. 둘 다 트래커·이력 쪽 일이라 손대지 않았다.
