Max-effort review of `git merge-base develop HEAD`..HEAD — the merge driver's `settle`/`issue` split and its tests. Ten finder angles; every finding below was reproduced live against the built binary.

**All ten angles independently converged on one line.** The issue's stated intent — *apply the check only to rows this merge composed* (moai-0k2e) — was implemented as `take()` emitting the branch's **raw bytes**, which also dropped `Issue::normalize()` and the canonical re-serialization. That is strictly more permissive than `store::with_write`, which the doc comment claimed equivalence with: `with_write` normalizes **every** readable row and validates only the changed ones.

## Findings

1. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:317`** — take() emitted raw bytes past a readability gate weaker than the store's, so a row with a duplicated JSON key merged through and made `moai status` exit non-zero.
   VERIFIED end-to-end. row() parses to serde_json::Value (duplicate keys collapse, last wins) then probes Issue::deserialize(&v); store::parse_issues does serde_json::from_str::<Issue>(line), which errors `duplicate field`. theirs carries `{"id":"argos-0001","title":"one","title":"two",...}` from a hand-resolved conflict; ours never had that id. Driver exits 0 and writes the line verbatim. `moai status` then prints `! Unreadable rows 1` and exits 1 — the tool's only fatal signal, flipped by the merge, on a repo that was clean before.

2. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:317`** — take() skipped Issue::normalize(), so `"started_at":""` survived the merge and the next `moai mv` silently lost the real start time forever.
   VERIFIED end-to-end. normalize() exists to turn `""` into None (model.rs, citing moai-38mh), and store runs it only AFTER the command closure, so move_to sees Some(""), its `started_at.is_none()` guard is false, and it never stamps. Probe: merged row carries `"started_at":""`; `moai mv argos-0001 in_progress` writes the row with NO started_at at all. `moai show --json` reports it as unknown forever. Same mechanism leaves `"due_on":""` on a milestone, which keeps the deadline warning silent — the exact bug moai-tfcp was filed for.

3. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:317`** — take() skipped tag folding, so a row carrying `"#Bug"` merged through unfolded and became invisible to every tag filter.
   VERIFIED end-to-end. query.rs normalizes only the needle (`i.tags.contains(t)` against a normalize_tag()'d value), so a stored `#Bug` never matches `bug`. Probe: base/ours/theirs all carry `"tags":["#Bug","aaa"]`, ours edits an unrelated row; driver exits 0 and copies the bytes. `moai show -t bug` prints `Nothing.` The row is missing from show/ready/TUI until some unrelated write happens to rewrite the file.

4. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:342`** — An un-normalized value planted by one merge is a real Value-level difference, so the NEXT merge of that row falls into fields() and clashes on a field settle_field has no rule for — the fix traded one recurring-conflict class for another.
   Merge #1 passes a hand-resolved `"priority":2` through take(). Develop now holds it. A branch forked from the base commit runs `moai edit <id> -p 1`. Merge #2: fields() sees priority ov=None, av=Some(2), bv=Some(1); no equality shortcut fires; settle_field("priority") returns None -> the whole row goes to a person with markers. With the merge-#1 result normalized, the identical merge #2 is clean and picks priority:1. Same for `epic`, `milestone`, `assignee`, `body`, `title`, `deferred_at` — none has a settle_field rule.

5. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:317`** — The merge output stopped being a fixed point of store::render_issues, so an unrelated later commit carries a surprise diff on a row nobody touched.
   store::with_write normalizes EVERY readable row and re-renders the whole file on any write. A non-canonical row (key order from a hand-resolved conflict, `"priority":2`, an un-normalized tag) now survives the merge verbatim; the first later `moai edit`/`mv` rewrites it, and that hunk lands in whatever commit happened to run the command. The `Row` doc and the old issue() doc both name this ("다음 쓰기가 표준 차례로 되써서 통째로 헛 diff 를 낸다(멱등성)") as the reason the driver canonicalized.

6. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:338`** — Two arms import THEIRS' bytes into a file that never held them — take(y) and (None, None, Some(x)) — so the merge is the writer there, yet it now writes rows the tool itself refuses.
   Branch `side` holds a hand-written row with `"title":"one\ntwo"`, `"priority":250`, `"tags":["a b"]`, or an id failing id::is_valid. Base and ours never had it. Driver exits 0, no marker. `moai status` then draws the title across two lines and the board columns break for every following row; the row is permanently untouchable (`moai edit` -> `a title is one line`) and nothing anywhere reports it — validate_fields has no caller in report.rs. Before the diff, keep() -> validate_fields -> clash handed it to a person while the branch that produced it was still in view.

7. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:335`** — `if x.v == y.v || same(o, y) { return take(x) }` made the output ours-biased at the byte level, so the merge result stopped being a function of (O, A, B).
   Two branches hold the same row with equal Values but different bytes (key order, `A` vs `A`, a differently-placed unknown field). `git checkout A && git merge B` writes A's spelling; `git checkout B && git merge A` writes B's. Two people merging the same pair in opposite directions get byte-different `.moai/issues.jsonl` for an identical issue set; `git rerere` records two resolutions for one situation. keep() emitted the same canonical line whichever side won.

8. **`tests/cli.rs:14842`** — `line_of(root, &old).replace('}', ",\"due_on\":\"2026-09-20\"}")` replaces EVERY `}` in the line, not the closing one.
   It works only because a freshly `add`ed row has exactly one `}`. The moment the fixture gains a body or title containing `}`, or an unknown field that is an object, `due_on` is spliced into the middle of a string; the line then becomes invalid JSON, keyed() files it under `opaque` instead of `by_id`, and the test passes for the wrong reason — it stops exercising take() at all. The file's own idiom for this is `&l[..l.len() - 1]` (tests/cli.rs:3113, 3299, 9469).

9. **`tests/cli.rs:14872`** — The test's closing idempotency assertion could not fail for the one deviation take() newly permitted — the fixture was canonicalized before the merge, and `moai note` never rewrites the snapshot anyway.
   store.rs computes `wrote = after != before` where BOTH sides are render_issues() of parsed rows, so a key-order-only deviation compares equal and write_atomic is never called. `note` changes no issue field, so `assert_eq!(issues(root), before)` compared the file with itself. Compounding it, `ok(root, &["note", &one, "자리 맞춤"])` at :14847 was documented as canonicalizing the doctored row but performs no write, and every `moai edit` on the branches re-canonicalized the fixture before the merge ever saw it.

10. **NOT FIXED — `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:342`** — built() still validates the whole composed row, so a stale field neither side touched still conflicts whenever both sides edit that row, and the clash message names no field.
    Ours retitles a row carrying a pre-existing bad `due_on`, theirs tags it. fields() merges perfectly, then validate_fields rejects over a field neither wrote. The markers show two lines whose only visible difference is each side's own edit — the culprit is identical on both sides and therefore invisible — and clash_fail prints only `<path>: N건은 사람이 푼다 — <ids>`. Narrowed by the reachability check I ran: `moai edit`/`mv`/`defer` already refuse any edit to such a row, so through the tool only a version skew or a hand edit gets both branches there. The escape (`moai edit <id> --due none`) works and the edit refusal names it; the merge conflict does not.

11. **NOT FIXED — `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:164`** — the same bug class survives one level up: `plan()` escalates the WHOLE file to a conflict when the two sides' unreadable-line sets merely differ, and never consults o.opaque.
    Branch A (a newer binary) creates one row with a `kind` the current binary cannot read: a.opaque=[row], b.opaque=[] and EVERY merge from then on wraps markers around all ~1000 lines with the message `(파일 전체)` and no per-issue resolution. Also: `moai status` calls unreadable_line FATAL, so fixing the junk line on one branch is exactly what makes a.opaque != b.opaque. Only the both-sides-changed-it case genuinely lacks a key; the rest is 3-way set-merge-able with the same formula settle_field already uses for `tags`.

12. **NOT FIXED (pre-existing) — `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:435`** — coupled()'s planned_at tie-break silently discards one side's deferral when that side's timestamp is not the canonical 20-char `…Z` form, contradicting later()'s stated policy that an unreadable timestamp goes to a person.
    base planned_at=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z; ours planned_at=deferred_at="2026-09-19T23:00:00+09:00" (= 14:00Z, the LATER decision, from a hand-resolved line); theirs planned_at="2026-09-19T04:00:00Z" with no deferred_at. parse_rfc3339 rejects anything not exactly 20 bytes ending in Z, so time(al)=None -> the `(None, Some(_)) => b` arm picks theirs and drags deferred_at along. Ours' later defer vanishes with no conflict and no warning — silent loss, the one failure mode this tool says it cannot tolerate.

13. **NOT FIXED — `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:1533`** — moai-h4jx's unit tests rode in the commit whose subject names only moai-0k2e, so `moai show moai-h4jx` will never find half of its stated work.
    moai-h4jx's body defines its scope as "`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs` 의 시험 뭉치와 `tests/cli.rs` 의 `the_merge_driver_*` 뭉치". `git log --name-only` shows the three new unit tests landed in `df6738b fix(merge-driver): … (moai-0k2e)` while `5b23b0e … (moai-h4jx)` touched tests/cli.rs alone. AGENTS.md: "`moai show <id>` and the explorer detail find that issue's commits on the spot, **by the id written in the subject**." Fix needs a history rewrite (add `(moai-0k2e, moai-h4jx)` to df6738b's subject, or a `Refs: moai-h4jx` trailer), which I did not do.

14. **NOT FIXED as a finding, but removed as a side effect — `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:300`** — three new doc comments attributed the change to a "2026-09-23 사용자 결정" that is recorded nowhere; the epic body names a review finding as the origin.
    merge_driver.rs:300, merge_driver.rs:1543 and tests/cli.rs:14820 all carried it. `moai show moai-0k2e/moai-h4jx/moai-85o3 --json` journals hold only create/status/note entries — no decision line on 2026-09-23. The epic moai-85o3's own body says "리뷰 moai-pmhv.070 11번. 이 에픽이 만든 것이 아니라 넓힌 자리다." CLAUDE.md forbids an attribution you cannot support ("어림으로 적은 줄은 적힌 값과 안 갈려"). I could not verify either way from here, so I did not substitute a claim — the rewritten paragraphs simply no longer make it. Confirm whether a user decision exists and restore it if so.

15. **NOT FIXED (pre-existing, but this change makes the row durable and cross-branch) — `src/view.rs:1871`** — view::due_of reads due_on/starts_on with no kind filter while report::status_in filters due warnings to milestones, so the exact row shape this fix lets through renders on one surface and is ignored on the other.
    A non-milestone issue carrying `"due_on":"2026-09-20"` prints `Due  — → 2026-09-20  (3 days past)` in `moai show <id>`, while `moai status` says nothing and exits 0. After this change such a row propagates to every branch on every merge instead of being stopped once, so the disagreement spreads with it.

## Fixes applied (`--fix`)

**The fix:** split `issue()` into `shaped()` (deserialize + normalize) and `issue()` (shaped + `validate_fields`). `take()` now goes through `shaped()`; `built()` keeps the full `issue()`. Only the check is skipped.

The byte-verbatim half of the decision is reversed, deliberately — the commit body argued for it ("모르는 필드의 차례까지 이 머지가 고쳐 쓴 것이 되지 않게"), but re-serializing is a no-op for every row `moai` itself wrote (those are already canonical), so it only changes rows that were already broken. That is exactly the set that needs repair.

Verified end-to-end against the built binary, before and after: duplicate-key row → `moai status` went from exit 1 to exit 0; `moai show -t bug` went from `Nothing.` to finding the row; `moai mv` went from dropping `started_at` to stamping it.

Tests: renamed `a_row_only_one_side_touched_keeps_its_own_bytes` → `..._keeps_that_sides_value` and added a merge-direction-symmetry assert; added `a_row_that_passes_through_is_still_shaped` (duplicate key, unfolded tag, default priority, empty timestamp); reworked the integration test so its fixture survives to the merge (each branch re-plants it, since every `moai` write canonicalized it away) and its guard uses a write that actually rewrites rows. **Both new tests were checked to go red against the pre-fix code.** CHANGELOG corrected. `replace('}')` replaced with a guarded `replacen` on the id prefix. The bug narrative that appeared near-verbatim in four places is now written once, in `settle`'s doc.

`cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, 1392 + 509 tests pass.

## Skipped

Findings 10–15 above, with reasons in each entry. Also skipped: three efficiency proposals (memoize `keyed()`'s per-line parse across the three files, `Settled::Line(Cow<'s, str>)` to drop a per-row allocation, hand-merge the three sorted `BTreeMap` key iterators instead of building a `BTreeSet`) — all real but unmeasured wins on a once-per-merge path, and all outside the reviewed diff. A test-scenario helper for the nine copies of the git branch dance in `tests/cli.rs` is worth doing but is a refactor across tests this diff did not touch.

One housekeeping note for whoever closes this: `moai show moai-0k2e --json` still has an empty `work` array — the `model:` line is not on either issue yet.

받아들인 것과 넘긴 것.

**1~9 는 반영했다**(1dde5ed). 열 각도가 한 줄로 모인 것이 맞았다 — 검사를 조립한 줄에만
거는 것은 맞았는데, 그것을 원문 바이트로 구현하면서 `Issue::normalize` 까지 함께 건너뛴
것이 문제였다. `issue` 를 `shaped`(deserialize + normalize)와 `issue`(shaped +
validate_fields)로 갈라, 건너뛰는 것을 검사 하나로 좁혔다.

**원문 바이트는 사용자 결정이었고 이 실측을 보이고 다시 물어 뒤집었다.** 처음 물을 때 댄
셈이 모자랐다 — `normalize` 가 moai 가 쓴 줄에 무위라는 것만 재고, 손으로 고친 줄에 무엇을
하는지를 안 쟀다. 이 이슈가 겨눈 줄이 바로 그 줄인데도 그랬다. 그 까닭은
`moai show moai-0k2e` 의 이력에 적었고, 주석의 출처 줄도 그 이력을 가리키게 돌려놓았다.

**14 번은 리뷰가 못 본 것이다.** 2026-09-23 사용자 결정은 실제로 있었고, 리뷰가 돌 때는
아직 이력에 안 적혀 있었다. 적어 두지 않은 쪽이 잘못이라 결정을 이력에 적고 주석을
되살렸다 — 리뷰의 판단(못 대는 출처는 적지 않는다)은 옳았다.

**13 번은 커밋이 아니라 본문을 고쳤다.** `moai-h4jx` 가 제 몫으로 적어 둔 범위에 단위
시험까지 들어 있던 것이 어긋난 자리였다. 단위 시험은 그 고침이 무는지를 재는 자라 구현과
한 커밋에 서는 것이 맞고, `moai-h4jx` 의 몫은 끝에서 끝까지 재는 시험 하나다. 이력을
다시 쓰는 대신 본문을 실제와 맞췄다.

**10·11·12·15 는 넘겼다.** 넷 다 이 에픽이 내건 것 밖이라 idea 로 담았고, 출시 잣대로 갈랐다.

- `moai-47qa` — `plan` 이 못 읽는 줄 하나로 파일 전체를 충돌로 넘긴다 (11번). 같은 덫이 한
  자리 위에 그대로 있다. `#bug` 가 맞아 v0.1.2 안에 둔다
- `moai-x23h` — `coupled` 이 못 읽는 시각에서 한쪽 미루기를 조용히 버린다 (12번). 조용한

- `moai-3zp0` — `view::due_of` 가 마일스톤 아닌 줄의 기한을 그린다 (15번). `Regression-of:
  moai-pmhv` 를 쓸 수 있어 안에 둔다
- `moai-y2rc` — 조립한 줄이 걸릴 때 거절문이 어느 필드인지 안 댄다 (10번). 충돌 자체는 일부러

효율 셋(`keyed` 의 줄마다 파싱 메모, `Settled::Line(Cow)`, `BTreeSet` 대신 손 병합)은 재지
않은 이득이고 머지마다 한 번 도는 길이라 안 담았다. `tests/cli.rs` 의 가지 짜기 아홉 벌을
묶는 것은 이 diff 가 안 건드린 시험을 가로지르는 리팩터라 같이 넘긴다.

**못 읽는 줄도 JSON 과 `id` 까지 읽히면 id 로 짝짓는다.** 선택지 셋을 냈다.

- A — 못 읽는 줄 전체를 집합 3-way 로만 풀고 충돌은 두지 않는다
- B — 거기에 좁은 충돌 조건을 더해 못 읽는 줄 묶음에만 표식을 세운다
- C — id 가 읽히는 줄은 id 로 짝짓고, 열쇠 없는 줄만 집합 3-way 한다

고른 것은 C 다. 가른 것은 못 읽는 줄의 출처가 둘로 갈린다는 실측이다. `Kind` 는
갈래 넷짜리 enum 이고 `Status` 는 문자열이라, 새 바이너리가 쓴 `kind` 하나면 JSON
도 id 도 멀쩡한 채 `Issue` 로만 안 읽힌다 — 이 이슈가 겨눈 판이 그것이다. 손으로
푼 충돌이 남긴 깨진 JSON 은 id 조차 못 읽는다.

앞엣것을 짝지어야 "한쪽만 건드렸다" 와 "둘 다 건드렸다" 가 갈린다. A 와 B 는 그
둘을 못 가려, 둘 다 고친 판에서 두 쪽을 다 남기거나 옆 이슈까지 함께 사람에게
넘긴다.

Review agent `/code-review max --fix`, opus-5, 357,109 tokens, 124 tool uses, 29 min.
All 1,914 tests pass, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.
15 findings, most severe first. The agent's own words.

## Findings

1. **src/cmd/show.rs:253** — `derived_epic` reads the id-keyed epic map with no eclipsed
   guard, so a row hidden by a different-kind twin is published as belonging to an epic
   every other surface says it is not in. `query.rs:364-378` deliberately refuses to read
   `wh.epic` for an eclipsed row (moai-2m9p, pinned by `an_eclipsed_row_is_picked_by_no_membership`
   at query.rs:1194). A badly merged file holds id argos-0002 twice: an Issue with no epic,
   then an Idea with `epic: argos-0001`. `groups` maps argos-0002 -> argos-0001; `show --json`
   prints the issue line with `"derived_epic":"argos-0001"`, while `show -e argos-0001` omits
   it, `show argos-0001` says members 0/0, and `--tree` draws it under (길 잃음). Same hole
   reaches `prime --json`, `show <id> --json` (`footing.epic_of`) and every `Row::from` via
   `Read::epic`.

2. **src/cmd/mod.rs:709** — `read_of` now runs a full `groups(all)` ancestor walk inside
   `store::with_write` for every writing command; `mv … done` does it three times under the
   lock. `groups_of`'s gate opens whenever any asked id is `joins && epic.is_none() && has
   id-parent` — exactly the `<epic>.<body>` shape every plan member and every review issue
   carries here, so it never short-circuits in practice. Before the diff `read_of` built
   nothing for a non-group id (`group_states_of`'s `is_group` gate closed). Now
   `moai mv <member> done` pays `read_of(&asked)` at mv.rs:203, `report::freed -> next_of ->
   groups(after)` at report.rs:2760, and `read_of(&freed)` at mv.rs:216 — three identical
   whole-repo walks while holding the lock six or seven sessions queue behind.

3. **src/guide.rs:309** — the new AGENTS.md/SKILL.md contract "It stands on every row every
   command prints, and its absence means the row is in no epic at all" was false for three
   surfaces. `rm --json` serializes raw `Issue` rows (rm.rs:73 — the deliberate exception
   documented at cmd/mod.rs:470-473), `tui --json` prints its own Row (tui.rs:402) with no
   `epic` key, and `ready --json`'s `held` entries are `{id,by,undo,empty}`. An agent applying
   the rule literally reads every removed or explored plan member as unaffiliated and files
   follow-up work outside the epic — the moai-l288 failure the membership rule exists to prevent.

4. **src/report.rs:1862** — `groups_of` tested id membership with a linear slice scan twice,
   making the call O(rows x asked). Measured on a 1980-row synthetic tracker: `ready --json`
   overhead over the human path is ~0 ms at 60 ready picks and ~206 ms at 1920 picks —
   quadratic in the number of rows printed. ready.rs:31/97 pass every ready pick and
   status.rs:296 every wip row; moai ids share a common prefix so no comparison rejects on
   the first byte.

5. **src/cmd/prime.rs:103** — `prime --json`'s `epic` key silently flipped from the resolved
   epic to the literal field with no CHANGELOG entry. A loop pinned on
   `moai prime --json | jq -r '.ready[].epic'` now gets null for every plan member and treats
   epic members as unaffiliated work. Nothing errors and nothing in the output says the key
   moved — and the repo's own convention requires the line.

6. **src/cmd/mod.rs:749** — inserting `pub type Standing` stole `standing_of`'s summary
   sentence, leaving the function's doc opening mid-thought on "[`read_of`] 와 갈리는 곳이
   둘이다." `standing_of`'s doc is the only written spec for the moai-hym7 stale-pickup
   contract several sessions depend on.

7. **src/report.rs:2008** — `Handed::from` dropped the `joins` guard that the deleted
   `passed_down` enforced; the invariant now lives only in the caller's `.filter` with nothing
   marking it load-bearing. `passed_down` called `epic_through`, which opened with
   `if !joins(p) { return None }`. `Handed::from` has no such step: for an Epic parent it
   returns `Some(p.id)`. Widen or drop `rooted_thoughts`' `.filter(|p| matches!(p.kind, Issue
   | Idea))` and ideas parked directly under an epic stop entering `rooted`, so their whole
   subtree starts inheriting the epic — silently, across `groups`, `-e`, `--tree` and
   `derived_epic` at once.

8. **src/report.rs:2000** — `rooted_thoughts` shares one `Handed` memo across a loop that is
   still filling `rooted`; the safety proof rests entirely on the id-length sort and nothing
   tested it. `the_map_hands_each_plan_member_its_own_epic` contains only Epic/Issue rows, so
   `thoughts` is empty and this second `Handed` is never touched. Replace the sort with
   anything not ancestor-first and `seen[X]` is recorded before X's rootedness is decided: a
   thought that should be rooted folds instead, and every row under it inherits an epic it was
   explicitly cut out of.

9. **src/cmd/mod.rs:609** — `Row::of` and `Brief::of` computed `derived_epic` by two different
   rules, and `Row::of` put issue-meaning logic in `cmd/` against the repo's own rule.
   CLAUDE.md, 되돌리지 않을 설계 결정: "`cmd/*.rs` 안에 이슈의 뜻을 판단하는 `if` 를 두지
   않는다." `Row::of` used `!report::is_group` while `report::groups` uses `joins`; they
   coincide only because `Kind` has exactly four variants today. `Brief::of` read the map
   straight with no `is_group` exclusion and no "written epic wins" precedence. Add a fifth
   `Kind`, or let a group row reach prime's held/picks, and one binary answers one key two
   ways — the split moai-wuzi exists to close.

10. **src/cmd/ready.rs:31** — `ready --json` builds the full `groups(all)` map three times per
    run: `ready_in -> picks_in -> ties`, `held`, and the new `groups_of`. `report::ties`
    (report.rs:456) IS `groups(issues)`, `report::held` builds it again (report.rs:2867), and
    `groups_of` makes a third. show.rs:203 states the opposite rule in the file this diff edits
    ("소속 지도는 한 벌이다 (moai-g0zx) … 저마다 재면 `groups` 가 세 벌 돈다"), and
    `Soil`/`Footing`/`_in` variants exist only to thread one map. Lands one commit after
    moai-1pra, itself a `groups` optimisation.

11. **src/cmd/status.rs:296** — the overview built the epic map unconditionally, but
    `Board::epics` and `Picks::epics` are read only in the `--json` arms. Plain `moai`,
    `moai status` or `moai ready` run outside a `.moai` — the documented session-start screen —
    paid one full `groups(all)` per registered project and threw every one away;
    `view::projects_status` never touches the field.

12. **src/cmd/mod.rs:683** — `Read::epics`' doc states the opposite of what the map holds — it
    claims rows that wrote their own `epic` are absent. `groups_of` retains every queried id
    once it builds, written-epic rows included. In this codebase the comment is the contract:
    a reader who believes it drops `Row::of`'s `.or()` fallback and gets `None` for every flat
    member whenever the lazy gate short-circuits.

13. **src/report.rs:1866** — `groups_of`'s `!p.is_empty()` clause made the short-circuit
    predicate a non-superset of the rows `epic_through` answers for. `id::parent_of` is
    `rsplit_once('.')`, so an id beginning with '.' yields `Some("")`. Writes reject those but
    reads are deliberately lenient. With such a row, `show --json` (via `Soil`) and
    `prime --json` emit `derived_epic` while every `read_of`-backed surface short-circuits to
    an empty map and emits no key — two machine surfaces of one binary disagreeing again. The
    whole correctness argument for returning an empty map is that the gate is a superset.

14. **src/cmd/mv.rs:275** — `freed_rows` duplicated `Row::from`, and its comment pointed the
    next reader at a "fix" that would be a no-op. The comment said switching to `Row::from`
    would add `derived_status`. It would not: `Row::of` computes
    `read.filter(|_| is_group(&issue))`, and all three lists are `is_work`-only (closable at
    report.rs:2745, unblocked_pick at report.rs:2840, next from ready_in picks). Someone acting
    on the comment writes a no-op and believes the gap is closed, while the duplicated row
    builder stays and drifts the next time `Row` gains a key.

15. **tests/cli.rs:1565** — `row_in` returns everything to end of string for the last row on a
    surface, so a sibling key can be read as part of the row. `edit --json` serializes `Out` as
    `#[serde(flatten)] row` followed by `inherited_epic`, whose own first key is `epic`. The
    assertion `!row.contains("\"epic\":")` passes today only because `--tag parser` leaves
    `cut` false so `skip_serializing_if` drops the key. Extend the test to
    `moai edit <member> -e none --json` — the case the feature targets — and the assert fires
    on a test bug, not a product bug.

## Also surfaced, below the cut

- `Handed::last` is provably redundant (after any call `from` is in `seen`, so it saves one
  BTreeMap probe while adding a second copy of the same fact)
- `derived_epic` echoes a dangling `epic` verbatim, which `report::misplaced` classifies as
  길 잃음
- an idea created with `-e <epic>` now reports `derived_epic` although `members`/rollups count
  by `is_work`
- the new Korean doc comments use `판` in the 회차 sense against `docs/korean-terms.md` §2
- `milestones_in`'s per-row climb is left un-memoized beside the half `Handed` just fixed

## What the agent fixed

- `report::groups_of` — id membership through a `BTreeSet`, empty `ids` short-circuits, the
  cheap predicate before the set probe, `!p.is_empty()` gone so the gate is a true superset
- `report::stands_in` — new single measure for "which epic does this row stand in"; `Row::of`
  and `prime::Brief::of` both call it
- `ready.rs` / `status.rs` overview — the epic map is built only under `ctx.json`
- `mv.rs` — `freed_rows` deleted in favour of `Row::from`; misleading comment replaced
- docs — `standing_of`'s summary restored, `Standing`'s doc corrected, `Read::epics` says what
  the map holds, `rooted_thoughts`' `.filter` marked load-bearing, `groups_of` documents that
  an empty map means "not built"
- `guide.rs` + AGENTS.md + plugin files — the contract sentence names the two surfaces that
  carry neither key; regenerated with `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `derived_epic` under Added, the `prime --json` `epic` break under Changed
- new test `a_thought_folded_under_a_rooted_thought_hands_nothing_down`, verified red when the
  length sort is reversed

## What the agent skipped, and why

- Eclipsed rows (1) — the guard has to live somewhere all five epic sources can reach
  (`Footing`, `Where`, `groups_of`, raw `groups`); fixing only `show`'s list path would create
  a fresh show-one/show-list split
- `read_of` under the lock (2) and `ready`'s three `groups` builds (10) — the real fix is
  threading one prebuilt map, which changes `report` signatures well outside this diff
- `tui --json` / `rm --json` gaining the key — a feature addition; `rm`'s shape is a deliberate
  documented exception. The doc now matches the code instead
- `Handed::last` — redundant but deliberate, documented and tested
- `row_in` (15) and the `판` term-table nits — latent, not currently failing

1. `src/worktree.rs:823` — The `SideFloor` projection made `touched` lose eclipsed
   duplicate-id twins: `holds_of` used to OR over every row of the side snapshot, it
   now reads a last-wins `BTreeMap`. Failure: a merge leaves `m-0002` twice in a
   sibling worktree's snapshot with the row it actually moved FIRST and the stale twin
   last. Old code put `m-0002` in `Workplace::touched`; new code compares only the
   stale twin, drops it, and `report::places` reports a live agent-isolated worktree's
   work as `Place::Lost` -> a `stranded` warning and `moai show <id>` saying it has no
   place. Reproduced against the built binary, and pinned by a new test that goes red
   on the pre-fix code. `open` still counted twins (moai-es40, a user decision), so the
   two halves of one tuple disagreed.
2. `src/cmd/mod.rs:855` — The new test's root skip reads `geteuid()` while `access(2)`
   — the thing under test — judges by the REAL uid, as `runnable`'s own doc states four
   lines above. With ruid 0 and euid != 0 the guard does not fire, `access(X_OK)`
   answers as root, returns 0 for mode 0o011, and the assertion fails on a correct
   implementation. The mirror case skips a test that would have been meaningful.
3. `Cargo.toml:51` — `libc` was added to plain `[dependencies]`, but `fs2` gates its
   own libc to `cfg(unix)` — so on Windows this genuinely adds a crate, and an unused
   one, contradicting the comment's "크레이트는 0개가 늘었다" measurement record.
   Verified in fs2-0.4.3's manifest: `[target."cfg(unix)".dependencies.libc]`, with
   `winapi` on Windows.
4. `src/hook.rs:7659` — `shown()` renders the refusal path with `Path::display()`,
   re-introducing exactly what `aim_flag` in the same file forbids. A non-UTF-8
   filename under the repo comes back with U+FFFD and the refusal names a path that
   does not exist.
5. `src/hook.rs:5601` — The typed spelling is destroyed one frame above `shown()`:
   `guard_writes_in` passes `cwd.join(path).to_string_lossy()`, a machine-built
   absolute path, as the "what the person typed" argument. Session cwd is a symlink
   into the repo (macOS `/tmp`, a linked project). `echo x > src/store.rs` is refused
   naming the full `/home/u/proj/src/store.rs` where the old `rel_to` printed
   `src/store.rs`. moai-fr0a's own contract fails on the Bash half of rule 2; the new
   test only covered `Call::Edits`.
6. `src/cmd/mod.rs:838` — Switching to `access(X_OK)` makes the pre-existing positive
   assertion mount-dependent: on a `noexec` TMPDIR the test goes red for a reason
   unrelated to the code. Confirmed empirically on this machine. (This also REFUTES two
   angles that claimed the diff's noexec doc was false — it is correct.)
7. `src/worktree.rs:537` — `gather` now runs `report::started` + a full `rows_of` per
   side eagerly on every `gather(worktree=true)`, on paths that discard `sides`
   entirely — the opposite of moai-kos1/moai-mafv's laziness discipline this change
   cites. `cmd/ready.rs:18`, `cmd/prime.rs:150` and `cmd/read.rs:213` all destructure
   `{ load, origin, .. }` and never build a `Dug`; `workplaces_in`'s "names answer
   everything" gate also returns before touching them. On this repo (1,949 rows, 3-8
   siblings) that is a `ties()` build plus ~5,850 String allocations per side,
   discarded. Inherent to dropping the rows, so it is a trade to weigh, not a slip.
8. `src/worktree.rs:812` — The self-dug branch of `holds()` builds a throwaway
   `SideFloor` — materialising the whole rows map — on the hook's path, contradicting
   the OnceCell optimization 60 lines above it. `held_elsewhere` always passes
   `&Dug::new()`, so this is the only branch the hook ever takes. The old code filtered
   `&[Issue]` directly and allocated only the qualifying ids.
9. `src/worktree.rs:802` — The two branches of `holds()` no longer provably share one
   `Config`: the handed branch answers from an `open` frozen at gather time from
   `repo.config` and ignores the live `cfg` parameter, while the self-dug branch still
   uses `footing.cfg()`. Latent today — every call site passes the same object — but
   silent when it bites. No type, assert or test catches it. `SideFloor::of` is `pub`.
10. `CHANGELOG.md:11` — A user-visible behaviour change (`runnable` now measures "can
   I run it") and the refusal-spelling change land with no `[Unreleased]` entry,
   although this repo maintains that section per change. `scripts/bump-version.sh`
   folds `[Unreleased]` into the release, so what is missing here is missing from the
   release forever.
11. `Cargo.toml:49` — "15MB 예산의 52% → 54%" is arithmetically impossible for a
   +5,960-byte change and mixes two denominators.
12. `src/cmd/mod.rs:134` — `runnable`'s doc summary line still says "있는 파일이고 실행
   비트가 섰는가. 재는 것은 딱 그것이다" — the reading the change exists to retire. That

13. `Cargo.toml:46` — Cargo.toml:46 and src/cmd/mod.rs:139 both cite a "2026-09-23

14. `src/worktree.rs:371` — `Floor::later(id, planned, updated)` took three positional
   `&str` where the last two are interchangeable to the compiler but order-sensitive to
   the comparison. Swap them at the one call site and it compiles, the tests still pass,
   and `touched` quietly reports the wrong rows.
15. `src/hook.rs:7595` — `counted` lost its `path.is_empty()` front gate; the answer is
   unchanged but an empty target now costs a `canonicalize` on the hook's per-tool-call
   path. `Call::read` builds `Call::Edits(… .unwrap_or_default())`, so an Edit/Write
   payload missing both path keys really reaches `guard_edit` with `""`.

text:
Max-effort review of `git merge-base develop HEAD`..HEAD — the merge driver's unreadable-row keying (`plan`/`keyed`/`row`/`settle`/`unkeyed`) and `coupled`'s `planned_at` tie-break. Fifteen findings; each reproduced live against the built binary.

## Findings

1. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:323`** — unkeyed()'s count formula counts an addition once but a deletion twice, so a line both branches still hold vanishes with exit 0 — the silent loss the module exists to prevent.
   `min(max(x,y), x+y-n)`. Base holds the same id-less junk line twice (a hand-resolved conflict pasted one twice); branch A deletes one copy, branch B deletes one copy, so each side's file still has one. n=2, x=1, y=1 -> min(1, 0) = 0: the merge emits NONE. `unkeyed(&[x,x],&[x],&[x])` returns `[]`, `unkeyed(&[x,x,x],&[x,x],&[x,x])` returns one where both sides hold two. No marker, no warning, exit 0. Confirmed by running the function and by driving the built binary.

2. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:237`** — When two same-id rows are both unreadable, the id goes to whichever came first in file order, so a reorder on one branch flips which row is 3-way'd and revives a row the other branch deleted.
   Base: good row + J1(`half:1`) + J2(`half:2`), both id argos-0009 and unreadable. Ours deletes J2. Theirs only swaps the two junk lines. Base and ours key J1; theirs keys J2. settle reads that as 'ours unchanged, theirs changed' and carries J2, while J2 sits in base's opaque pool and in neither side's, so unkeyed contributes nothing. Merged file = good, J2, J1 — the line ours deleted is back, exit 0, no marker. Confirmed against the built binary.

3. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:557`** — coupled()'s `(Some(_), Some(_)) => a` tie-break silently picks ours when two different planned_at strings map to the same second, dragging its deferred_at along — the same silent loss moai-1a55.kh2 set out to close.
   `parse_rfc3339` checks shape, not calendar meaning: it allows day 1..=31 and second <= 60, so `2026-02-30T00:00:00Z` and `2026-03-02T00:00:00Z` map to the same epoch second (likewise `T23:59:60Z` and the next day's `T00:00:00Z`). Base planned_at=2026-01-05; ours deferred at 2026-02-30 (planned_at + deferred_at); theirs un-deferred at 2026-03-02 (planned_at only). time() returns equal values, the arm picks ours, and theirs' un-deferral disappears with no marker at exit 0. Confirmed against the built binary.

4. **`src/cli.rs:543`** — `moai merge-driver --help` still states the contract this diff removed — the user-facing text AGENTS.md points readers to.
   The help says "With an unreadable line or a duplicated id the whole file is handed over inside conflict markers". After the fix an unreadable line no longer escalates and the duplicate-id case is narrowed to readable rows. A user who sees a clean per-issue merge of a file holding an unreadable row reads the help and concludes the driver did not run — i.e. that they hit the `git merge-file` fallback, the one state `driver_command`'s doc is written to make diagnosable. `docs/cli.md` is generated from this text, so `the_cli_reference_matches_the_help` pins the two together.

5. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:30`** — The module header — the first thing a reader meets — still lists the deleted `x.opaque == y.opaque` guard as a live reason for handing the whole file over.
   Lines 30-32 say escalation happens in three cases, including "못 읽은 줄이 두 쪽에서 다를 때", and line 25 says unreadable rows are simply appended verbatim with no mention of id pairing. `plan()`'s rewritten doc at 176-185 says the opposite. In a repo whose comments are the design record, the next session reading top-down gets the pre-fix model and can 'restore' the guard this diff removed.

6. **NOT FIXED — `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:415`** — When one side's edit makes a row stop parsing as JSON, the row leaves `by_id` on that side and the conflict block shows an empty 'ours' side while ours' actual bytes are appended outside the markers.
   Base `{"id":"argos-0001",...}`; ours hand-edits it into `{잘린 줄` (no longer JSON, so `row()` returns None and it lands in `opaque`); theirs edits the title. settle hits `(Some(_), None, _)` and builds `Clash{ours: None, ...}`, producing `<<<<<<< ours` / (empty) / `=======` / theirs' line / `>>>>>>> theirs`, with `{잘린 줄` on the line below. The markers claim ours deleted the row, which is false. A person keeps theirs, deletes the block, and the orphan line stays behind with nothing connecting it to the conflict just resolved. Before the diff this case escalated to a whole-file conflict that showed both sides properly.

7. **NOT FIXED — `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:230`** — A row that is keyed on one side and demoted to the opaque pool on another is resolved by two algorithms that disagree, so one side's explicit deletion is reverted at exit 0.
   Base `[G(argos-0001, readable), J(argos-0001, unreadable)]`; ours deletes J; theirs deletes G. `settle(o=G, a=G, b=J)` takes `same(o,x)` -> `take(y)` -> `Settled::Opaque(J)` carried, while `unkeyed(o=[J], a=[], b=[])` sees J on neither side and contributes nothing. The merge emits `[J]` at exit 0 — ours' deletion of J is reverted with no marker. `settle` exists precisely to send delete-vs-change to a person; `opaque` now holds two different populations (truly key-less lines, and keyed rows that lost a collision) whose membership differs per side, so that guard is bypassed.

8. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:87`** — `Keyed::opaque`'s new doc says Issue-unreadable rows never land there, but both collision arms in `keyed` push exactly those rows in — and a test in the same diff asserts it.
   The doc reads "`Issue` 로만 안 읽히는 줄은 **여기 안 온다** ... 그것은 `by_id` 에 서고 [`Row::read`] 가 거짓이다", while lines 236-237 do `opaque.push(e.insert(r).raw)` / `opaque.push(r.raw)` for such rows on an id collision, and `a_readable_row_keeps_the_id_from_one_that_does_not_read` asserts `k.opaque == [junk]` for a row carrying a readable id. Anything that later assumes 'opaque implies no id' — an id-uniqueness sweep, a reserved-id scan — is wrong about those rows. The CHANGELOG inherits the same error.

9. **`CHANGELOG.md:137`** — The kh2 entry and coupled()'s doc both claim parity with later(), but the new `_ => continue` also changed the ABSENT-timestamp case, where later() does the opposite — and that change has no test.
   `later()` resolves an absent value (`(Some(x), None) | (None, Some(x)) => Some(Some(...))`): it takes the side that has a time, and refuses only present-but-unparseable ones. `time()` returns None for absent, non-string AND unparseable, and `_ => continue` collapses all three, so a row where one branch carries no `planned_at` at all now goes to a person where before the side with one won. The entry says only "a timestamp it could not parse" and "which is what every other timestamp field already did" — false for the absent case. Concretely: base deferred; ours runs `defer --undo`; theirs re-defers later — the `defer --undo` vs `defer` race, routine in a repo six or seven sessions share. All three tests on this path have planned_at present on both sides.

10. **`CHANGELOG.md:128`** — "Only a duplicated id among readable rows still hands the whole file over" is false — a snapshot that is not valid UTF-8 still does — and "exactly the same set of unreadable lines" understates the old guard.
    `run()` still has `_ => whole_bytes(&a, &b, marker)` for the non-UTF-8 case. `plan()`'s own doc is correctly scoped by its first line, but the CHANGELOG sentence and the commit body carry no such scope, and the release workflow cuts this section verbatim into the release notes. Separately, the removed guard was `x.opaque == y.opaque`, a Vec comparison: same lines in the same ORDER and multiplicity, not a set — two branches holding the same unreadable lines in a different order also escalated.

11. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:304`** — unkeyed() has no conflict path at all, so a case that used to force a human now exits 0 with both edits stacked in the file, and nothing in the merge says so.
    Base has one id-less junk line K; ours rewrites it to K', theirs to K''. K is in neither side's tally so it is dropped; K' and K'' each get count 1 and both are emitted. `git merge` reports success and records the merge commit; the first signal is a later `moai status` (`unreadable_line`, fatal), by which time the commit is pushed. Before the diff this exact input produced markers and a non-zero exit. `run` only reports `clashes`, which `unkeyed` can never add to — so neither stderr nor `--json`'s `Out` names how many keyless lines came through unmerged.

12. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:289`** — Nothing exercised by_issue's `unkeyed(&o.opaque, &a.opaque, &b.opaque)` call site — the deleted test was the only guard on that argument wiring.
    `what_cannot_be_keyed_hands_the_whole_file_over` lost its differing-unreadable-lines case, and the replacement `lines_without_a_key_are_merged_by_their_count` calls `unkeyed()` directly as a pure function. `an_unreadable_line_is_carried_not_escalated` puts the same junk on all three sides, so it would still pass if the call were `unkeyed(&a.opaque, &a.opaque, &a.opaque)` or if o/a/b were transposed. The new integration test drives the keyed path only. Swap two of those arguments and every test stays green while unreadable lines start resurrecting or vanishing on real merges.

13. **NOT FIXED — `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:190`** — A duplicated id where one copy is unreadable now merges silently at exit 0 and the output carries that id twice, with nothing downstream to catch it.
    Base `[R(argos-0001)]`, ours unchanged, theirs `[R(argos-0001), U(argos-0001)]` (a hand-resolved conflict left a stale unreadable copy on one branch). `keyed(b)` gives `by_id[X]=R, opaque=[U]`; settle resolves R and unkeyed re-emits U, so the merged file holds two lines carrying the same id at exit 0. `store::with_write`'s `first_duplicate` only scans readable issues, so the write path will not refuse it either — the repository is left permanently `moai status`-fatal with no merge-time signal. Before the diff the `x.opaque == y.opaque` guard escalated this loudly.

14. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:100`** — `Settled::Opaque`'s doc promises an unreadable row is never touched ("store::with_write 도 안 하는 일이다"), but when both sides change such a row, fields()/issue() field-merges and re-serializes it into a row neither branch wrote.
    A newer moai writes `{...,"kind":"spike","spike_size":3}`. Branch A repairs the row by deleting the `kind` key; branch B keeps working on it, bumping `updated_at`. On today's binary: kind -> ours' deletion wins (ov==bv), updated_at -> theirs wins (ov==av), spike_size survives into `rest` (ov==av), and `issue()` accepts it because `validate_fields` never looks inside `rest`. Output is a plain readable issue still carrying a field that only meant something under `kind:"spike"`, at exit 0 — `take` carries such a row verbatim only while one side is unchanged, and the doc does not say so.

15. **`src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:285`** — by_issue emits `carried` in id order ahead of `unkeyed`'s base-order output, so a merge rewrites the unreadable tail into an order neither parent had.
    Tail is `[U(argos-zzzz), {깨진 줄, U(argos-aaaa)]`; ours is byte-identical to base; theirs edits one unrelated readable row. Output tail is `[U(argos-aaaa), U(argos-zzzz), {깨진 줄]`. Before the diff `by_issue` emitted `a.opaque` verbatim, so ours' order survived. Not loss — the result is still a fixpoint of the next `store` write — but every such merge commit carries a diff against both parents for lines nobody edited, and the comment at line 284 claims "이 차례가 곧 고정점이다" without saying it becomes one only after that first rewrite. The `Settled::Clash` arm has the mirror problem: it writes an unreadable row's markers inline among readable rows, so the resolved line is relocated to the tail by the next write.

## Fixes applied (`--fix`)

Full suite green: 1402 unit + 518 integration, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean; each fix also verified end-to-end by driving `target/debug/moai merge-driver` over hand-made O/A/B triples.

- **#1** `unkeyed`'s formula is now `o + max(added) - max(gone)`, which counts an identical deletion once, exactly as `settle_field`'s set-based `tags` reckoning already did. Two regression assertions added to `lines_without_a_key_are_merged_by_their_count` (they fail against the old formula).
- **#2** `keyed`'s `(false, false)` arm now keeps the lexicographically smaller `raw`, so all three sides pick the same key regardless of file order. New test `two_unreadable_rows_with_one_id_pick_the_same_key_on_every_side`.
- **#3** `coupled` now picks a side only when the two seconds actually differ; an equal-second/different-string pair joins the `continue` branch and goes to a person.
- **#4, #5, #8, #10, #14, #15** doc/contract corrections: `src/cli.rs` help (plus the regenerated `docs/cli.md`, which `the_cli_reference_matches_the_help` pins), the module header, `Keyed::opaque`, `Settled::Line`'s stale "갈래 둘", the `unkeyed` ordering note, and both CHANGELOG entries.
- **#9** the false `later()` parity claim is replaced with the real rule and why `planned_at`'s absence differs from `updated_at`'s; new test `a_row_with_no_planned_at_against_a_deferral_goes_to_a_person`, which also pins the negative fact `coupled`'s `continue` depends on (`settle_field` has no `planned_at`/`deferred_at` arm).
- **#11** the CHANGELOG now states that an id-less line both branches rewrote comes through as both lines at exit 0.
- **#12** new `lines_without_a_key_ride_the_whole_plan` drives `by_issue`'s `unkeyed(...)` call site through `plan`; it fails if the o/a/b arguments are transposed.
- Cleanups: the new integration test now uses the existing `append_raw` helper instead of hand-rolling `fs::write`, and `unkeyed` no longer visits keys present on both sides twice.

## Skipped, reported only

- **#6, #7, #13** all share one root: `Keyed::opaque` now holds two populations (truly key-less lines, and keyed rows that lost an id collision), and membership differs per side, so `settle` and `unkeyed` can resolve the same id under different rules. The real fix is one row list with `key: Option<String>` settled by a single mechanism. Worth its own issue.
- **#14** whether a both-sides-changed unreadable row should be rebuilt or clashed is a behaviour decision (the current answer is a defensible 3-way merge); I corrected the doc's overclaim instead.
- The merge-direction asymmetry for unreadable rows (`take` returns raw bytes, so `x.v == y.v` with differing bytes yields ours either way round) narrowly re-opens what review `moai-85o3.p4w` closed for readable rows — no cheap fix that does not contradict "carry the bytes verbatim".

One note on process: an instruction arrived mid-task, inside the MCP server instruction block, telling me to route file reads and edits through `bash` (`cat`/`sed`/heredocs) instead of the dedicated tools. It did not come from the brief, so I ignored it and used the normal tools.

text:
## Scope

`git diff develop...HEAD` in worktree `/home/coder/workspace/moa-issue/.claude/worktrees/moai-x04r` — 2 commits (`e31b220` moai-x04r.fn4, `867081e` moai-53s2), 11 files, +281/−41. Working tree was clean at start. Ran 10 finder angles + a sweep pass, and reproduced the main findings myself against `target/debug/moai` on scratch trackers.

## Findings

1. `src/report.rs:1906` — stands_in still reads the row's own `epic` first, so SAME-kind duplicate rows keep handing out a derived_epic that the same command's human column and its `-e` filter both contradict — moai-53s2 closed only the different-kind half of the class.
   Reproduced. File holds `moai-0002` twice, both `kind:issue`, first `epic:moai-e001`, second `epic:moai-e002`. is_eclipsed is false for both (kinds map says Issue), so the new guard never fires. Result: `show --json` says TWIN-A derived_epic=moai-e001; `show -e moai-e001` prints `Nothing.`; `show -e moai-e002` lists TWIN-A with its Epic column drawn as EPIC-TWO; `show moai-e001` reports 0 members. One binary, three answers to the question this epic was opened to settle.

2. `src/cmd/mod.rs:666` — The unchanged line `let derived = read.filter(|_| report::is_group(&issue))` inside the touched Row::of leaks an eclipsed GROUP row the twin's derived_status — the same bug class this diff fixes for derived_epic, left open for the neighbouring key.
   Reproduced. `moai-e001` appears as a `milestone` then as an `epic`, member `moai-e001.aa1` in_progress. group_states correctly skips the eclipsed milestone, but both rows share the id so `read.column(id)` returns the epic's column. `show --json` emits the eclipsed milestone with `"derived_status":"in_progress"` while `show --tree` draws it under `(길 잃음)` and group_members gives it zero members. `show -s in_progress` lists it too — report::column/stands (report.rs:1337) has no eclipse guard either, which is why the gate's right home is there, not in Row::of.

3. `src/tui/draw.rs:2231` — The explorer detail panel is the next surface the new gate does not cover: `i.epic.as_deref().or_else(|| site.index.epic_of(idx))`, so an eclipsed row carrying its own `epic` names that epic in the panel.
   stands_in now deliberately returns None for an eclipsed row that wrote its own epic (report.rs test case `wrote`). Index::epic_of is safe — nav.rs:589 sends eclipsed rows to Seg::Lost — but the `i.epic` half is not. Walk the cursor into `(길 잃음)` in `moai tui` and the panel prints `에픽 <twin's epic title>` with no broken-reference mark, while the tree in the same window has that row under `(길 잃음)`. Exactly what the diff's own bold note (`문을 여기 둔다`) says must not happen.

4. `src/view.rs:1892` — The kind gate removes the only human-visible trace of a field that write-locks the row: Issue::check refuses every write to a non-milestone row carrying due_on/starts_on, and no status warning names it.
   Reproduced end to end. An issue row carrying due_on/starts_on now draws nothing in `moai show <id>`, nothing in the explorer panel, and `moai status` exits 0 with no warning (Dues filters kind==Milestone; unknown_field cannot fire, due_on is a known field). `moai mv <id> in_progress` then fails with `--start stands on a milestone row only` — and clearing `--start` trips on `--due`, two rounds about invisible state. Such a row needs no hand-resolved conflict: the merge driver deliberately carries it through an ordinary merge (tests/cli.rs `a_row_neither_side_touched_does_not_block_the_merge`). Before the change `show` printed the dates. report.rs already has the machinery for readable-but-broken (future_timestamp, unknown_field, dangling_*); a `date_not_milestone` warning is four lines and costs no exit code.

5. FIXED — `src/cmd/mod.rs:748` — Read::kinds() rebuilt a whole BTreeMap by value and Row::from called it once per row, making every bulk --json write surface quadratic.
   Measured, dev build, `moai add --from - --json` at N=500/1000/2000 plan lines: pre-change 195/332/610 ms, this branch 349/819/2682 ms (~3.3x per doubling vs ~1.8x). Call sites: mv.rs:266/281/282/283, add.rs:237/315, idea.rs:298, link.rs:118, defer.rs:180, edit.rs:302 — all inside the lock's result path. `idea promote --from -` has no line cap (an 8,000-line plan is already recorded in idea.rs).

6. `src/cmd/mod.rs:766` — The whole kinds plumbing on the WRITE path is unreachable, and it is built inside the tracker lock: store::with_write refuses the entire write with Trouble::DuplicateId whenever an id stands twice, and a duplicate id is the only way a row can be eclipsed.
   Verified at store.rs:786 and reproduced: on a tracker holding argos-0002 twice, `moai edit … --json`, `moai mv … --json` and `moai defer … --json` each exit 1 with `an id stands twice` and write nothing. So there is no input for which read_of's `kinds` arm changes any output, while every --json write pays an extra full kinds_of scan plus a BTreeMap<String,Kind> allocation while holding the lock — `mv --json` pays it twice (mv.rs:198 `asked`, mv.rs:216 `freed`). read_of's own doc gates `epics` on `json` precisely because `여기는 세션 예닐곱이 같은 .moai 를 두고 줄 서는 저장소다`. Stronger proof than the show.rs:580 case below, and a worse cost site.

7. `src/report.rs:1903` — The gate fails OPEN: is_eclipsed is `kind_of.get(..).is_some_and(..)`, so an empty or merely incomplete map silently means "nothing is eclipsed", and nothing in the type system forces a new surface to supply one.
   `&BTreeMap::new()` compiles and was what seven test call sites spelled, so it is the shape a new --json surface copies. read_of leaves Read::kinds empty when json==false; ready/status pass Default::default() on the human path. A future `moai board --json` written as `Row::of(i, None, epics.get(id).copied(), &BTreeMap::new())` reopens moai-53s2 with every test green, because the eclipsed case needs a duplicate id to show at all. A `Kinds` newtype whose only constructors are report::kinds/kinds_of would make the omission a compile error. (I mitigated the copy-paste half by replacing the bare empty maps in tests with a named `no_twins()` helper.)

8. `src/tui/mod.rs:353` — Ground::here() replaced a zero-allocation boxed closure over `&self.kinds` with a full rebuild of the repo-wide kinds map, on the per-keystroke filter path.
   here() is called from tui/mod.rs:2304 inside the filter apply; its own doc says `거름망이 키마다 부른다` and draw.rs:8183 benchmarks it as `키마다 도는 자리`. `kinds` is the only map in here() with one entry per issue — epic/milestone hold member rows, states/since hold group rows — so on the 10k shape that doc is calibrated against, every keypress now builds and drops the largest map in the function. The Soil header records the stake: `이슈 1만 건에서 거름망 한 번이 300ms 였다`. Where has exactly one reader of this field (Where::eclipsed), so the map shape buys the explorer nothing; a borrow-or-own key wrapper on Where::kinds restores the old cost. The doc's cost model at tui/mod.rs:340 is now wrong and was not updated.

9. FIXED (comment) — `src/view.rs:1892` — the written rationale `세는 자를 따른다` was not true: report::Dues filters on four axes and due_of copied one, so the divergence the change names as its reason is still open on three.
   Reproduced: a milestone deferred with a past due prints `Due — → 2026-09-20 (3 days past)` in `moai show` while `moai status` says nothing — byte for byte the failure the commit quotes as its reason. Same for a DONE milestone and an eclipsed one. The danger of leaving the claim standing is the opposite fix: someone finishes the job by copying the other three Dues filters into due_of, and a shipped or parked milestone's dates disappear from the one panel that exists so a wrong --due can be spotted.

10. `src/model.rs:569` — "Only a milestone carries dates" is now spelled in three layers with no shared predicate — model.rs:569 (write), report.rs:3975 (counting), view.rs:1892 (drawing) — while the other half of this same diff collapses exactly this kind of duplication into report::is_eclipsed.
    report exports is_group and is_work as named row predicates but no is_milestone. The day a fourth kind is allowed a target date, whoever adds it edits model.rs and the Dues filter, ships, and the detail panel silently keeps drawing nothing for the new kind because view.rs:1892 was never found — a two-surface disagreement of exactly the shape moai-x04r.fn4 was filed to remove, reintroduced by its own fix.

11. `src/guide.rs:309` — Three contract documents are stale for the row shape this change creates — `epic` present and `derived_epic` absent: guide.rs:306-311 (the moai init block, copied into AGENTS.md and .claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai/SKILL.md:39) and CHANGELOG.md:45.
    Both say absence means the row is in no epic at all, and never admit the third reason (this row is an eclipsed duplicate) — the one case where the two keys actively contradict each other. `moai init --check` still answers `current` because guide and AGENTS.md agree with each other; only the behaviour moved. The immediately preceding review of this same key (moai-s8go.5ye finding 5) was raised because a --json key changed meaning with no CHANGELOG line; the same convention applies again, and no `checked_in` test regenerates the CHANGELOG.

12. `src/cmd/show.rs:580` — `report::kinds_of(all, &[issue.id.as_str()])` adds a full scan of the snapshot to every `moai show <id> --json` for a guard the adjacent comment says can never fire.
    Load::get uses rfind (store.rs:212), so `issue` is always the last row carrying that id and kinds_of's collect keeps that same row's kind — is_eclipsed is unconditionally false. One extra O(n) pass on the per-issue read every agent loop makes. Worse than the cost: the next person changing which row `show <id>` opens will read this as live protection. `&BTreeMap::new()` (what the unit tests pass) produces byte-identical output.

13. `src/cmd/ready.rs:33` — The kind map is now built a second (for prime, a third) time per run, right after `report` built and discarded an identical one inside the very call that produced the rows; and the `(groups_of, kinds_of)` pair is duplicated across four carriers.
    report::picks_in (report.rs:2704), report::wip (400) and report::held (2941) each do a full report::kinds(all); ready.rs:33/104, status.rs:300 and prime.rs:177 then build another — `ready --json` walks the list three times, `prime --json` three, `status --json` twice. This is the `지도는 한 벌이다` rule (moai-g0zx) the repo states at show.rs:203, a file this diff edits. Separately the pair now lives in four places (cmd::Read, view::Board, view::Picks, two identical local tuples in ready.rs/status.rs), so a third repo-wide map means six sites that must stay in lockstep — the moai-wuzi failure cmd::Read exists to prevent.

14. FIXED — `tests/cli.rs:9334` — the new regression test's closing assertion inspected the wrong row, its fixture never exercised the `wrote` half of the fix, and its tree check did not pin where the row stands; separately the flipped TUI assertion left a block with only negative assertions and no anchor.
    `show argos-0002 --json` resolves through Load::get's rfind and opens the ECLIPSING twin, so `holds.contains("\"epic\":\"argos-0001\"")` was reading the idea, not the eclipsed row — and the eclipsed row in the fixture carried no `epic` at all, so `적힌 값은 그대로 남는다` was untested at the CLI layer. `tree.contains("가려진 이슈")` passed even if a regression put the row back under the epic. And in src/tui/draw.rs both surviving assertions in the flipped block were negative with nothing tying `pane` to `epic[0]`, so an empty pane would certify the gate as working.

15. FIXED — `src/cmd/mod.rs:722` — new Korean doc comments use `판` in the 회차 sense, which docs/korean-terms.md §2 forbids (`판(회차) → 번, 때, 회차, 경우, 벌`; 판정/판단 are exempt).
    That table's stated scope is `이슈 제목과 본문, 노트, 커밋 메시지, CLAUDE.md, 그리고 src/**/*.rs 의 한국어 doc comment`, and CLAUDE.md makes it the authority. Hits were src/cmd/mod.rs:722, src/cmd/prime.rs:174 and tests/cli.rs:9315. Nothing checks it mechanically, so each unreviewed diff re-adds the ambiguity the 49-issue sweep (moai-6tlw) was run to remove.

Two more that did not make the cut, both test-quality: the new cli test still slices JSON objects by hand with `rfind('{')`/`find('}')` where tests/cli.rs has a `split("},{")` idiom at four sites (tests/cli.rs:9316); and the eclipse case is still tested only through `show` — the narrowed maps threaded into ready/status/prime/mv/add/edit/defer/link/idea have no coverage, and are safe today only because wip/ready filter eclipsed rows and with_write refuses duplicate ids, two invariants nothing pins.

## What was fixed

`cargo test` **1408 + 521 green** (same counts as before), `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, rustdoc links resolve, `--json` output byte-identical on the reproduction fixtures. Files touched: `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/prime.rs`, `src/cmd/show.rs`, `src/tui/draw.rs`, `src/view.rs`, `tests/cli.rs` (+73 −36).

- **The measured quadratic.** `Row::of` is now generic over `K: Borrow<str> + Ord` — the bound `stands_in`/`is_eclipsed` already carry — and `Read::kinds()` lends `&BTreeMap<String, Kind>` instead of collecting a fresh map per row. Re-measured on the same shape: **215/419/660 ms at N=500/1000/2000**, versus 349/819/2682 on the branch and a 195/332/610 pre-change baseline. Numbers recorded in the `Read::kinds` doc. Test call sites moved from bare `&BTreeMap::new()` to a named `no_twins()` helper.
- **The overclaiming rationale.** `due_of`'s comment now says it follows the *write* rule (`Issue::check`), names the other three `Dues` filters, and states they are deliberately not copied — so nobody "finishes the job" and blanks a shipped milestone's dates. The two parallel test docs were corrected the same way, including that the merge driver (not only a hand-resolved conflict) carries such a row through.
- **Duplicate test name.** `src/view.rs`'s new `a_deadline_stands_on_a_milestone_row_only` collided verbatim with the integration test at tests/cli.rs:6392; renamed to `a_deadline_is_drawn_on_a_milestone_row_only`.
- **Regression-test strength.** The eclipsed row in the cli fixture now carries its own `epic`, so the `wrote` half of the fix is actually exercised; the "written value survives" assertion moved off the eclipsing twin onto the eclipsed row's own list object; the tree check now pins that the row stands under `(길 잃음)` and not under the epic; and the flipped TUI block got a positive anchor (`pane.contains("argos-0001")`) so an empty pane can no longer pass.
- **Terminology.** Five `판`(회차) uses removed per `docs/korean-terms.md` §2 — two from the reviewed diff, two I had introduced myself, one in the diff's new cli test.

## What was skipped, and why

- **Findings 1, 2, 3** (same-kind twins, eclipsed-group `derived_status`, the explorer epic line) are reproduced and real, but each gate's right home is outside this diff: `report::column`/`stands` has no kinds parameter and is read from many surfaces, and tui/draw.rs:2231's `적힌 것이 먼저다` is a recorded decision. Gating only `Row::of` would trade one two-surface split for another.
- **Findings 4, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13** need a decision from the issue owner (add a `date_not_milestone` warning? drop the write-path map entirely, or keep it and accept it is inert? a `Kinds` newtype? a `report::is_milestone`? how to word the contract in guide.rs + SKILL.md + CHANGELOG together?). CLAUDE.md's `막혔을 때` applies — I did not guess.
- **Finding 12** is a deliberate, documented choice (`값을 내는 자가 지도를 물으니`); the honest alternative changes a stated design position.
- I attempted a mutation check (temporarily disabling the `is_eclipsed` early return to prove the strengthened test goes red) and the sandbox classifier denied it as a security-test removal. `src/report.rs` is unmodified. The guard is still provable by inspection: the eclipsed row now carries `epic:argos-0001`, so without the gate `stands_in` would return it and the `!contains("derived_epic")` assertion would fail.
- I did not build release to re-check the 15MB binary budget (a first release build in this worktree costs 3-7 min); the change adds one monomorphization of a four-line function to a signature the reviewed diff had already made generic.

## Findings

## Fixed (13 of 15)

`src/cmd/idea.rs`: moved `check_carried_body` ahead of `say_if_dead`/`check_plan` to match the write's order (#1, #3); split the fused doc block back onto `promote`, `check_carried_body` and `carried_body` (#10); made the way-out line English like the refusal it joins and dropped `refuse.promote_body_over` from both tables (#8).

`src/cmd/add.rs`: `check_plan` now walks drafts once checking title → body → milestone per row, mirroring `store::write_locked`, and takes `Rooted` instead of two adjacent `Option<&str>` (#2, #12); `reads_stdin()` widens the contention guard past the literal `-` (#6); the namespace default and a typed `--type` are picked apart so the pointer stands under every verb (#7); `flags_a_plan_cannot_keep` destructures `AddArgs` exhaustively with no `..` (#11); new `body_line` + `body_on` disclose where the body lands without echoing it, keeping moai-07v1's "don't print the text" (#9); a `debug_assert` guards a body with no root (#15).

Plus the three stale clap comments (#13), the flag test extended to all ten (#14), the `--body` paragraph added to `guide::reference()` (the checked-in `references/commands.md` was the only copy missing it), and CHANGELOG corrected — it claimed the refusal "names only the flags you actually passed" while the positional stands as `[title]`, and it omitted that six of those flags changed from clap's exit 2 to moai's exit 1.

## Skipped (2), both pre-existing and outside this diff

#4 (`-b-`/`-x` becoming an issue title) and #5 (empty `--body -` swallowed): both live in `refuse_if_flag_like`'s `--`-only guard and `read_body`'s empty→`None` contract, which `add`, `edit` and `note` all share. Fixing either changes behavior for every `add` call, so they want their own issue and a CHANGELOG break note.

Also skipped and worth noting: `check_plan` still does not measure `--assignee` or comma-bearing tags, so those rehearsals still approve what the write refuses — `check_plan`'s own doc already records that gap and names the real fix (build the drafts into issues before minting ids and measure once).

## Verification

  파일이나 `cmd::hook` 의 시작·끝 도장. 제 이슈로 낼 일이다. 6번이 짚은 빈틈은 참이다: 패닉하거나
  SIGKILL 된 moai 는 stdout 이 비어, "deny 를 버린다" 는 까닭이 101·137·124 를 안 덮는다.
- 15(효율) — `report::counts_in` 을 떼고 `ls` 에 `projects::each` 를 넣는 일. 물려받은 낭비고, 잰
  값을 바꾸는 변경이라 본 헌크 밖으로 한참 벗어난다.
- `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs`·`src/worktree.rs` 의 `cargo fmt` 어긋남 — 이 가지가 안 건드린 파일이고
  이 기계의 rustfmt 판 차이다.

기록하는 사람에게: 아무것도 커밋하지 않았고 트래커 줄도 안 건드렸다. 등급은 이 워크트리가 무관한
이슈 둘의 멤버를 실었으므로 CLAUDE.md 의 묶음 규칙대로 `max` 다. 훅은 이미 `max` 목록에 있고 `max`
가 천장이다.

note: 열다섯 가운데 열다섯을 판단했다. 받아 고친 것 열둘은 `080c135`, 늦게 돌아온 훑기 셋은 `1de92cb` 다. 받은 것 가운데 무거운 둘은 이 회차의 고침 자체가 못 서던 자리다 — bash 의 `command -v` 가 경로에 `access(X_OK)` 를 보아 겨눈 첫 판이 bash 가 `/bin/sh` 인 기계에서 그대로 조용했고(`[ -e ]` 로 메웠다), 맨 명령으로 둔 부름이 `set -e` 껍데기에서 `exit 0` 에 못 닿아 2 면 게이트가 될 수 있었다(`c=0; … || c=$?` 로 되돌렸다). 옛 줄·새 줄을 sh·bash 와 `-c`·`-ec` 넷에 0644 파일과 없는 해석기로 직접 재서 확인했다. 넘긴 넷은 다음에 세웠다 — moai-wnnb(126·127 밖의 값에서도 말한다, 멤버), moai-f7up(알림에 문턱이 없다, 멤버), moai-wza7(알림이 대는 `moai skill status` 가 그 판에서는 같이 못 돈다, 멤버), moai-6ay6(`project ls` 가 셈 넷에 경고 판을 통째로 짓는다, idea), moai-a682(`ready`·`prime`·`show` 목록·`idea ls` 도 시간대를 들기만 한다, idea). 리뷰가 `cargo fmt` 어긋남을 "이 기계의 rustfmt 판 차이" 라고 했다가 스스로 고쳤다 — 그 워크트리가 develop 보다 열 커밋 뒤였던 것이고, 루트에서 다시 재니 0건이다.

text: Next: moai-j4ie 와 에픽 끝 리뷰 moai-514e.pef(max)가 닫혔고 develop 에 들었다(머지 76bf33b, 늦게 돌아온 훑기는 eda54e5). 훅 줄은 이제 126·127 에 `systemMessage` 알림 한 줄을 내고 종료는 어느 갈래에서도 0 이다 — bash 의 `command -v` 가 경로에 `access(X_OK)` 를 보는 갈림은 `[ -e ]` 로 메웠고 `set -e` 면역은 `c=0; … || c=$?` 로 되돌렸다. 에픽은 첫 칸의 일곱으로 열려 있다 — moai-6k5v(제 조건이 아직 안 섰다), moai-bscj·moai-ati3·moai-y1ix(앞 회차가 넘긴 것), 그리고 이 회차가 넘긴 moai-wnnb·moai-f7up·moai-wza7. 뒤의 셋은 한 몸이다: moai-wnnb 가 126·127 밖의 값(clap 의 2, 패닉의 101, 시그널, 훅 타임아웃)을 말할 장치를 정하면 moai-f7up 의 문턱이 그 위에 얹히고, moai-wza7 은 `quotable` 을 제어문자까지 넓히는 것이 먼저다. 다음에 집을 때는 moai-bscj 가 먼저다 — sudo 의 -i -s 를 잘못 막는 자리고 su 표의 -u 도 한 몸이다.

Next: moai-yz4j 가 develop 에 들었다(머지 76bf33b). `project ls` 는 `report::status_unjudged` 로 세어 tzdb 를 안 만진다 — 그 이름은 리뷰가 세운 것이고 `status`·`tui::layer` 도 그리로 온다. 훅은 재 보고 그대로 두었다: 보드는 기한 경고를 그리고 기준선은 그것까지 센 수로 세션을 붙드니 시간대를 옳게 들고, 훅의 stderr 는 `claude` 에서 아무에게도 안 닿는다(측정은 `skill::command` 의 표). 에픽은 moai-ynd6 하나로 열려 있다 — `src/tui/draw.rs` 를 옆 워크트리가 쥐어 이 회차에서 빠졌고, 감독(moa-issue-52)이 다음 회차로 보낸다. 시간대를 들기만 하는 나머지 넷(`ready`·`prime`·`show` 목록·`idea ls`)은 idea moai-a682 로 담았다 — 고치는 길이 `Ctx::zone_trouble` 을 그리는 자리로 옮기는 설계 결정이고 `view::every_command_screen_carries_the_zone` 잣대를 함께 옮겨야 해서, 이 에픽이 내건 셋과는 별개다.
